details.label: Contribution of the AI
details.value: Waymo told The Verge that automated technology helps its teams identify potential violations such as a firearm in the cabin. Waymo did not say whether software or staff first flagged the weapon in this ride. It also did not explain how the system judges that an object may be a firearm or what role people play between an alert and a call to police. The driverless car pulled over, and police officers made the stop, the search and the arrests. In the July 2026 San Mateo case, Reason reports, citing NBC Bay Area, that a Waymo representative who was watching the live interior camera feeds called police.

record.title: Police book two juveniles over a loaded AR-style “ghost gun” in a Waymo robotaxi that the company pulled over in San Francisco's Richmond District on detecting a firearm violation
record.summary: After Waymo detected a firearm violation, one of its driverless cars pulled over in San Francisco on 3 September 2026. Police found a loaded ghost gun. They booked two minors.
record.account: Shortly before 4 a.m. on Thursday 3 September 2026, Waymo pulled one of its driverless cars over in San Francisco's Richmond District. Waymo had detected a “violation of our terms of service involving a firearm”. A Waymo spokesperson told the Los Angeles Times (12 September) that the company alerted emergency services. The spokesperson said that it “cooperated fully” with police. The San Francisco Police Department said that officers made a “high-risk vehicle stop”. It said that officers detained the two juvenile passengers. Officers found a loaded AR-style assault rifle. They found suspected marijuana. Mace spray was among the items that they found. The two were taken to juvenile hall. The Independent, citing SFGATE, quotes police spokesperson Allison Maxie calling the weapon an “AR-styled assault rifle also known as a ghost gun”. It says that the boy was booked into the Juvenile Justice Center on firearm-possession charges. According to The Independent, the girl was booked on the same charges. The California Post puts the stop at 40th Avenue and Cabrillo Street. The Independent and Xataka both say that it is unclear how the firearm was detected. On 17 September 2026, Waymo spokesperson Julia Ilina told The Verge that the company uses automated technology to help its teams identify potential violations such as firearms inside the vehicle. She said that Waymo may contact local police when it detects a firearm. Waymo did not say whether software, rather than staff, flagged the weapon in this ride. It did not explain what role humans play between an automated alert and a call to police. By 29 October 2026 the outcome of the firearm charges against the two minors had not been reported.
record.purpose: Waymo built the Waymo Driver to provide driverless rides. Its rider rules prohibit weapons, and Xataka says that interior cameras record rides so that the company can check compliance and respond to emergencies.

record.title: KPCW reports that a Pano AI camera on Lewis Peak spotted a lightning-caused fire that North Summit Fire District crews extinguished quickly
record.summary: KPCW reports that a Pano AI camera spotted a smoldering lightning-caused fire on Lewis Peak on 17 July 2026. It reports that North Summit Fire District crews extinguished it quickly.
record.account: KPCW, a public radio station in Utah, reported on 21 July 2026 that a Pano AI camera on Lewis Peak spotted a smoldering, lightning-caused fire on 17 July. North Summit Fire District crews extinguished it quickly. The district's battalion chief told KPCW that he was in his office almost all day. He said that he saw no smoke from that direction. He said that the fire could have smoldered for days until a hot, windy day made it a much bigger issue. Pano says that people review each fire that its AI flags before they text subscribers. The Summit County sheriff's office receives the alerts. Rocky Mountain Power pays for the station. The chief said that in the year since his district gained access, most fires were reported before the camera caught them. He said that he receives false positives when farmers and ranchers perform controlled burns. The report gives no fire size. It gives no response time. KPCW notes that the infrastructure at risk included its own 88.1 FM signal.

fields.summary: KPCW reports that a Pano AI camera spotted a smoldering lightning-caused fire on Lewis Peak on 17 July 2026. It reports that North Summit Fire District crews extinguished it quickly.
fields.account: KPCW, a public radio station in Utah, reported on 21 July 2026 that a Pano AI camera on Lewis Peak spotted a smoldering, lightning-caused fire on 17 July. North Summit Fire District crews extinguished it quickly. The district's battalion chief told KPCW that he was in his office almost all day. He said that he saw no smoke from that direction. He said that the fire could have smoldered for days until a hot, windy day made it a much bigger issue. Pano says that people review each fire that its AI flags before they text subscribers. The Summit County sheriff's office receives the alerts. Rocky Mountain Power pays for the station. The chief said that in the year since his district gained access, most fires were reported before the camera caught them. He said that he receives false positives when farmers and ranchers perform controlled burns. The report gives no fire size. It gives no response time. KPCW notes that the infrastructure at risk included its own 88.1 FM signal.

record.title: The AI cameras of Phú Thọ provincial police identify all 18 teenagers found gathering with weapons to fight in Việt Trì within about 30 minutes. All were summoned. All confessed
record.summary: On 13 June 2026 Phú Thọ police saw teenagers preparing weapons to fight in Việt Trì. The provincial AI camera system identified all 18 faces in about 30 minutes.
record.account: On the night of Saturday 13 June 2026, Phú Thọ provincial police detected a group of teenagers gathering in Việt Trì ward. Officers were mining data from the camera system as they monitored it. Tuổi Trẻ reports that police found the group through camera monitoring, helped by tips from residents. It reported on 14 June that the teenagers were preparing weapons for a fight that would disturb public order. They had vehicles ready for it. Within about 30 minutes the AI camera system of the provincial command center had accurately identified the faces of all 18 participants. They were aged 14 to 18. They came from Việt Trì, Vân Phú and Nông Trang wards and Phù Ninh and Bình Phú communes (Tuổi Trẻ, VietNamNet). Tiền Phong says that the whole matter was clarified in just over two hours. It says that 17 of the 18 were pupils of schools including Vũ Thê Lang High School and Dữu Lâu Middle School. One had dropped out. It says that the provincial police summoned all 18. It says that at the police station they admitted the violations. None of the reports of 14 June says whether a fight took place. On 19 June 2026 Phú Thọ police said that two groups had fought with knives, swords, tridents and glass beer bottles at the Hội Thịnh roundabout around 23:30 on 13 June. They charged 10 people aged 16 to 18 with public disorder (Thanh Niên). One was detained. Nine were barred from leaving their place of residence. Thanh Niên describes most of the 10 as workers. Whether these 10 are among the 18 identified by camera is unknown.
record.purpose: Phú Thọ police installed the provincial AI camera system to monitor traffic routes and major sites and detect violations for investigation and enforcement, according to Tuổi Trẻ.

Officers were mining data from the camera system as they monitored it. Tuổi Trẻ reports that police found the group through camera monitoring, helped by tips from residents. It reported on 14 June that the teenagers were preparing weapons for a fight that would disturb public order. They had vehicles ready for it. Within about 30 minutes the AI camera system of the provincial command center had accurately identified the faces of all 18 participants. They were aged 14 to 18. They came from Việt Trì, Vân Phú and Nông Trang wards and Phù Ninh and Bình Phú communes (Tuổi Trẻ, VietNamNet). Tiền Phong says that the whole matter was clarified in just over two hours. It says that 17 of the 18 were pupils of schools including Vũ Thê Lang High School and Dữu Lâu Middle School. One had dropped out. It says that the provincial police summoned all 18. It says that at the police station they admitted the violations. None of the reports of 14 June says whether a fight took place. On 19 June 2026 Phú Thọ police said that two groups had fought with knives, swords, tridents and glass beer bottles at the Hội Thịnh roundabout around 23:30 on 13 June. They charged 10 people aged 16 to 18 with public disorder (Thanh Niên). One was detained. Nine were barred from leaving their place of residence. Thanh Niên describes most of the 10 as workers. Whether these 10 are among the 18 identified by camera is unknown.

ratings.reason: The AI camera system identified all 18 participants for Phú Thọ provincial police within about 30 minutes, per Tuổi Trẻ and VietNamNet. Tiền Phong reports that the case was clarified in just over two hours, with all 18 summoned and admitting the violations.

Residents of Việt Trì were spared a street fight only if one was about to happen. Thanh Niên reports that two groups fought at the Hội Thịnh roundabout that night, and neither Thanh Niên nor the police say whether the 18 identified by camera took part.

record.title: A ZeroEyes alert sends Florida State University police to a man whom they charge on four counts for pointing a stolen Glock at bystanders
record.summary: According to court documents, ZeroEyes gun detection flagged a man pointing a gun in a Florida State University garage on 2 May 2026. Police found a stolen Glock 19 on him. They charged him.
record.account: On 13 February 2026, Undark reported that there is little or no empirical evidence that AI weapons detection systems have prevented shootings in real settings such as schools. According to arrest papers cited by WCTV, Florida State University police responded to the St. Augustine parking garage at about 2:30 a.m. on Saturday 2 May 2026. ZeroEyes gun detection technology had detected an individual in black pointing a gun on the bottom level. ZeroEyes works on top of existing cameras. It routes human-verified detections to police. Camera footage showed a 19-year-old man brandishing a loaded firearm at four other people. Officers found a Glock 19 handgun, stolen from Miller County, Georgia, in his waistband. He was charged with possessing a firearm on school property. He was charged with unlawful carry. He was charged with improper display of a firearm. He was charged with grand theft of a firearm. He bonded out on Sunday 3 May 2026. The Tallahassee Democrat, citing court records, says that police responded to a “ZeroEyes camera notification”. It says that the man is not a student at the university. FOX49 reported on 5 May 2026 that, in their report, the police credit the ZeroEyes notification with helping officers respond more quickly. The police say that it helped them know what they faced. The university declined to say when it bought the system. It declined to say why.
record.purpose: ZeroEyes built its system to detect visible firearms in existing security-camera feeds, have human analysts verify them and alert police within seconds, so that police reach potential shootings sooner.

data.retained_case_account: According to arrest papers cited by WCTV, Florida State University police responded to the St. Augustine parking garage at about 2:30 a.m. on Saturday 2 May 2026. ZeroEyes gun detection technology had detected an individual in black pointing a gun on the bottom level. Camera footage showed a 19-year-old man brandishing a loaded firearm at four other people. Officers found a Glock 19 handgun, stolen from Miller County, Georgia, in his waistband. He was charged with possessing a firearm on school property, unlawful carry, improper display of a firearm and grand theft of a firearm. He bonded out on Sunday. The Tallahassee Democrat, citing court records, says police responded to a “ZeroEyes camera notification” and that the man is not an FSU student. ZeroEyes layers over existing cameras and routes human-verified detections to police.

record.title: AI smoke-detection camera for Arizona Public Service spots early signs of the March 2026 Diamond Fire, which crews hold to 7 acres in Coconino National Forest
record.summary: An AI smoke-detection camera of unnamed make, installed for Arizona Public Service, spotted early signs of the Diamond Fire near Flagstaff on 26 March 2026. Crews held the fire to 7 acres.
record.account: In a staff report of 26 March 2026, the Arizona Daily Sun reports that a small fire later named the Diamond Fire began shortly after 2 p.m. on Thursday, 26 March 2026. It started just north of Lake Mary Road, about three miles southeast of the intersection of Lake Mary Road and Beulah Boulevard. That is south of Pine Canyon Golf Club. It is east of Flagstaff Pulliam Airport. It reached seven acres by 3:16 p.m., according to WatchDuty. Its forward progress was stopped at 3:37 p.m., about 80 minutes after the first report. It was 100% contained at 6:09 p.m. The Daily Sun does not mention a camera, the Coconino National Forest or who made the first report. In the interagency wildfire record (2026-AZCOF-000289), the Diamond Fire is on the Coconino National Forest. It was discovered at 2:15 p.m. Mountain Standard Time on 26 March 2026 at a tenth of an acre. The record gives a final size of 7 acres, a human cause and containment at 6:08 p.m. Who detected it is not recorded. No official incident record that lists the camera has been found. The Associated Press reported on 4 May 2026 that artificial intelligence had detected something resembling smoke on a camera feed from Arizona's Coconino National Forest on a March afternoon. The report is by Dorany Pineda and Brittany Peterson, on record in the KPBS and Courthouse News republications. One of dozens of AI cameras installed for the utility Arizona Public Service had spotted early signs of the fire that came to be known as the Diamond Fire. The Associated Press says that human analysts verified the camera's detection before they alerted the state forest service and Arizona Public Service. Firefighters raced to the scene. They contained it before it grew past 7 acres (2.8 hectares). The Daily Sun and Associated Press accounts match on the fire's name, month and size. The Associated Press says that Arizona Public Service has nearly 40 active AI smoke-detection cameras. It says that the utility plans 71 by summer's end. Cindy Kobold, a meteorologist at Arizona Public Service, says that the technology notifies the utility about 45 minutes faster on average than the first 911 call. Pano AI, launched in 2020, charges around $50,000 a year per camera. It counts Arizona Public Service among its customers. It says that it detected 725 wildfires in the United States in the previous year. The Associated Press does not state outright which company made the camera that spotted the Diamond Fire.

data.retained_case_account: The Associated Press reported on 4 May 2026 that artificial intelligence detected something resembling smoke on a camera feed from Arizona's Coconino National Forest. The report is by Dorany Pineda and Brittany Peterson, on record in the KPBS and Courthouse News republications. The detection came on a March afternoon. One of dozens of AI cameras installed for the utility Arizona Public Service had spotted early signs. The fire came to be known as the Diamond Fire. Firefighters raced to the scene and contained it before it grew past 7 acres (2.8 hectares). AP says APS has nearly 40 active AI smoke-detection cameras and plans 71 by summer's end. APS meteorologist Cindy Kobold says the technology notifies the utility about 45 minutes faster on average than the first 911 call. Pano AI, launched in 2020 and charging around $50,000 a year per camera, counts APS among its customers. It says it detected 725 wildfires in the US last year. AP does not state outright which company made the camera that spotted the Diamond Fire. The Arizona Daily Sun (staff report, 26 March 2026) reports that a small fire later named the Diamond Fire began shortly after 2 p.m. on Thursday. It started just north of Lake Mary Road, about three miles south-east of Lake Mary Road and Beulah Boulevard. That is south of Pine Canyon Golf Club and east of Flagstaff Pulliam Airport. It reached seven acres by 3:16 p.m. according to WatchDuty. Its forward progress was stopped at 3:37 p.m., about 80 minutes after the first report, and it was 100% contained at 6:09 p.m. The Daily Sun does not mention a camera, the Coconino National Forest or who made the first report. The two accounts are matched by the fire's name, month and size. No official incident record naming the camera was found; InciWeb's “Diamond Fire” is a June 2023 Scottsdale fire. The Daily Sun reported the fire that Thursday.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: AP reports that the camera's AI detected something resembling smoke and spotted early signs of the fire. It does not say whether the alert was the first report or what the fire agencies did with it. The Daily Sun's timeline does not mention the camera: first report, 7 acres by 3:16 p.m., progress stopped 3:37 p.m., contained 6:09 p.m. The attribution to AI rests on one news report, and the camera's maker is implied rather than stated. No official record naming the camera was found.

It was 100% contained at 6:09 p.m. The Daily Sun does not mention a camera, the Coconino National Forest or who made the first report. In the interagency wildfire record (2026-AZCOF-000289), the Diamond Fire is on the Coconino National Forest. It was discovered at 2:15 p.m. Mountain Standard Time on 26 March 2026 at a tenth of an acre. The record gives a final size of 7 acres, a human cause and containment at 6:08 p.m. Who detected it is not recorded. No official incident record that lists the camera has been found. The Associated Press reported on 4 May 2026 that artificial intelligence had detected something resembling smoke on a camera feed from Arizona's Coconino National Forest on a March afternoon. The report is by Dorany Pineda and Brittany Peterson, on record in the KPBS and Courthouse News republications. One of dozens of AI cameras installed for the utility Arizona Public Service had spotted early signs of the fire that came to be known as the Diamond Fire. The Associated Press says that human analysts verified the camera's detection before they alerted the state forest service and Arizona Public Service. Firefighters raced to the scene. They contained it before it grew past 7 acres (2.8 hectares). The Daily Sun and Associated Press accounts match on the fire's name, month and size. The Associated Press says that Arizona Public Service has nearly 40 active AI smoke-detection cameras. It says that the utility plans 71 by summer's end. Cindy Kobold, a meteorologist at Arizona Public Service, says that the technology notifies the utility about 45 minutes faster on average than the first 911 call. Pano AI, launched in 2020, charges around $50,000 a year per camera. It counts Arizona Public Service among its customers. It says that it detected 725 wildfires in the United States in the previous year. The Associated Press does not state outright which company made the camera that spotted the Diamond Fire.

record.title: Wiz researchers use Claude Code and IDA MCP to find a critical remote code execution flaw in GitHub, which fixes github.com the same day before it reports finding no exploitation
record.summary: Wiz researchers used Claude Code and IDA MCP to reverse engineer GitHub's binaries. They found a critical remote code execution flaw, which GitHub fixed on github.com the same day.
record.account: On 4 March 2026, Wiz Research reported a critical remote code execution flaw to GitHub, later numbered CVE-2026-3854. The flaw sat in GitHub's internal git infrastructure. Git push options were not sanitized before being written into internal headers. Any authenticated user could therefore run arbitrary commands on GitHub's servers with a single git push. Wiz says that AI-augmented tooling made the research feasible, particularly automated reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries with IDA MCP. The Register reports that the team used Claude Code and went from idea to working exploit in under 48 hours. GitHub reproduced the bug within 40 minutes. It deployed a fix to github.com at 7:00 pm UTC that day. It released patches for GitHub Enterprise Server from 10 March 2026. The National Vulnerability Database entry, published on 10 March 2026, scores the flaw 8.8 (High) under version 3.1 of the Common Vulnerability Scoring System. On 28 April 2026, GitHub disclosed the flaw. It reported that its forensic investigation found no exploitation beyond the researchers' own testing. The same day, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency recorded no known exploitation in its enrichment of the entry. Wiz published its own account that day. It wrote that its data showed that 88% of GitHub Enterprise Server instances were still vulnerable.
record.purpose: Anthropic built Claude Code to read a codebase, edit files, run commands and connect to external tools over MCP. Wiz used it, with IDA MCP, to automate reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries. Analyzing code for flaws falls within that general purpose.

fields.account: On 4 March 2026, Wiz Research reported a critical remote code execution flaw to GitHub, later numbered CVE-2026-3854. The flaw sat in GitHub's internal git infrastructure. Git push options were not sanitized before being written into internal headers. Any authenticated user could therefore run arbitrary commands on GitHub's servers with a single git push. Wiz says that AI-augmented tooling made the research feasible, particularly automated reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries with IDA MCP. The Register reports that the team used Claude Code and went from idea to working exploit in under 48 hours. GitHub reproduced the bug within 40 minutes. It deployed a fix to github.com at 7:00 pm UTC that day. It released patches for GitHub Enterprise Server from 10 March 2026. The National Vulnerability Database entry, published on 10 March 2026, scores the flaw 8.8 (High) under version 3.1 of the Common Vulnerability Scoring System. On 28 April 2026, GitHub disclosed the flaw. It reported that its forensic investigation found no exploitation beyond the researchers' own testing. The same day, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency recorded no known exploitation in its enrichment of the entry. Wiz published its own account that day. It wrote that its data showed that 88% of GitHub Enterprise Server instances were still vulnerable.

value.text: GitHub fixed github.com on 4 March 2026. Self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server installations stayed exposed until administrators installed a patched release. Wiz wrote on 28 April 2026 that its data showed that 88% of GitHub Enterprise Server instances were still vulnerable.

ratings.reason: GitHub closed a remote code execution hole in its git push pipeline within hours of the report. The fix reached github.com at 7:00 pm UTC on 4 March 2026. GitHub also shipped patches for six GitHub Enterprise Server release lines. Wiz earned what GitHub calls one of the highest rewards in the history of its Bug Bounty program. The loss avoided is hypothetical. GitHub's forensic investigation found that no other account had triggered the code path, and CISA records no exploitation. Wiz wrote that its data showed that 88% of GitHub Enterprise Server instances were still vulnerable when it published on 28 April 2026, so many self-hosted servers stayed exposed. NIST rates the flaw High (8.8).

record.title: TrailGuard AI cameras trigger arrest of 39 armed poachers in Similipal Tiger Reserve
record.summary: TrailGuard AI cameras detected armed intruders in Similipal Tiger Reserve on 18 February 2026. The Field Director reports that at least 39 poachers surrendered, with nine guns seized.
record.account: Similipal Tiger Reserve in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha, runs a network of TrailGuard AI trail cameras. The cameras classify humans. They classify animals. They classify vehicles. They send images to a control room. The New Indian Express reports that camera monitoring in the reserve began in October 2024 with about 50 cameras. In May 2025 Ommcom News reported that TrailGuard photographs helped track three poachers, whom a court sent to judicial custody after it rejected their bail. Late on Wednesday 18 February 2026 the cameras detected a group of armed intruders entering the reserve. Field Director Prakash Chand Gogineni said that the real-time alerts mobilized the Similipal South Division. He said that three ranges turned out. Three units of the Special Tiger Protection Force turned out. After about 24 hours of combing, at least 39 poachers surrendered. Nine guns were recovered. Gunpowder was recovered. The Times of India in April 2026 reported 50 AI cameras in use, up from an initial 10, with 300 planned.

fields.summary: TrailGuard AI cameras detected armed intruders in Similipal Tiger Reserve on 18 February 2026. The Field Director reports that at least 39 poachers surrendered, with nine guns seized.
fields.account: Similipal Tiger Reserve in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha, runs a network of TrailGuard AI trail cameras. The cameras classify humans. They classify animals. They classify vehicles. They send images to a control room. The New Indian Express reports that camera monitoring in the reserve began in October 2024 with about 50 cameras. In May 2025 Ommcom News reported that TrailGuard photographs helped track three poachers, whom a court sent to judicial custody after it rejected their bail. Late on Wednesday 18 February 2026 the cameras detected a group of armed intruders entering the reserve. Field Director Prakash Chand Gogineni said that the real-time alerts mobilized the Similipal South Division. He said that three ranges turned out. Three units of the Special Tiger Protection Force turned out. After about 24 hours of combing, at least 39 poachers surrendered. Nine guns were recovered. Gunpowder was recovered. More than 20 bows and arrows were recovered. A case was registered at Jenabil Wildlife Range. On 27 February 2026 The New Indian Express reported that the network had grown to more than 220 cameras. The paper reported that the cameras had helped the reserve detect more than 110 intrusions. It reported that they helped the reserve arrest nearly 300 poachers and wildlife criminals. It added that the reserve was buying 450 more cameras. Gogineni said that the reserve planned to install cameras in at least half of its 1,375 monitoring grids. Later detections on 11 April, around 24 July and 23 September 2026 led to arrests. Courts refused bail to the July and September groups. The camera count varies by source. The Field Director gave “around 220” in February 2026. The Hans India gave “over 220” in July 2026. The Times of India reported in April 2026 that 50 AI cameras were in use, up from an initial 10, with 300 planned.

record.title: Istanbul police first use their AVCI messaging-analysis system in a drug operation across 14 provinces on 10 February 2026 that closes 69 groups of dealers, with 325 suspects remanded
record.summary: Istanbul police first used their AI-supported AVCI messaging-analysis system on 10 February 2026, in a drug operation across 14 provinces: 325 detained and remanded, 69 groups closed.
record.account: AVCI (Açık Kaynak İstihbaratı Analiz Sistemi, Open Source Intelligence Analysis System) is an AI-supported program. The Istanbul Police Department's narcotics and cybercrime divisions built it in-house with a special software team. Police chief Selami Yıldız ordered the work. It infiltrates closed groups and channels on end-to-end encrypted messaging apps. It analyzes messages. It analyzes voice notes. It analyzes photos. It analyzes location data. It decodes the slang of dealers. It links profiles. It maps the relationships inside groups. By copying traffic to its own servers while the traffic is accessible, it preserves material that users later delete. Police first used AVCI on 10 February 2026, in a drug operation that was centered on Istanbul and ran across 14 provinces. Anadolu Agency reported that day that the simultaneous raids had taken place that morning in 14 provinces and 35 districts. It reported that 305 of 346 sought suspects had been detained. On 13 February 2026 the Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor's Office said that 324 suspects had been caught, 21 of them group administrators. Criminal judgeships of peace had remanded all of them. Anadolu Agency reported on 6 April 2026 that 325 suspects had been detained in the operation. All 325 referred to court were remanded in custody. Police closed 69 groups on messaging apps.
record.purpose: Istanbul police built AVCI to infiltrate and analyze encrypted messaging groups used for drug dealing. It also identifies suspects, fake profiles and network hierarchies. The 10 February operation was that intended use.
record.system: AVCI (Açık Kaynak İstihbaratı Analiz Sistemi): AI-supported open-source intelligence analysis software that infiltrates closed groups on encrypted messaging apps and analyzes messages, media and location data with natural language processing

data.retained_case_account: AVCI (Açık Kaynak İstihbaratı Analiz Sistemi, Open Source Intelligence Analysis System) is an AI-supported program. The Istanbul Police Department's narcotics and cybercrime divisions built it in-house with a special software team. Police chief Selami Yıldız ordered the work. It infiltrates closed groups and channels on end-to-end encrypted messaging apps. It analyzes messages, voice notes, photos and location data. It analyzes dealer slang, links profiles, and maps group relationships. By copying traffic to its own servers while it is accessible, it preserves material that users later delete. Anadolu Agency reported on 6 April 2026 that AVCI was first used on 10 February 2026. The drug operation was centered on Istanbul and ran across 14 provinces. 325 suspects were detained. All 325 referred to court were remanded in custody. 69 messaging-app groups were closed.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: By the police account relayed by Anadolu Agency, AVCI infiltrated closed messaging groups and decoded slang and coded language. It preserved messages by recording group traffic before users deleted it, linked profiles through IP analysis, and mapped group relationships. That work produced the suspects and groups targeted on 10 February. Police and courts carried out the detentions, referrals and remands. The sources include no independent evaluation of the system. No official is quoted on how many of the 325 were identified by AVCI rather than by conventional work. The sources name no developer beyond the police's own software team.

fields.account: AVCI (Açık Kaynak İstihbaratı Analiz Sistemi, Open Source Intelligence Analysis System) is an AI-supported program. The Istanbul Police Department's narcotics and cybercrime divisions built it in-house with a special software team. Police chief Selami Yıldız ordered the work. It infiltrates closed groups and channels on end-to-end encrypted messaging apps. It analyzes messages. It analyzes voice notes. It analyzes photos. It analyzes location data. It decodes the slang of dealers. It links profiles. It maps the relationships inside groups. By copying traffic to its own servers while the traffic is accessible, it preserves material that users later delete. Police first used AVCI on 10 February 2026, in a drug operation that was centered on Istanbul and ran across 14 provinces. Anadolu Agency reported that day that the simultaneous raids had taken place that morning in 14 provinces and 35 districts. It reported that 305 of 346 sought suspects had been detained. On 13 February 2026 the Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor's Office said that 324 suspects had been caught, 21 of them group administrators. Criminal judgeships of peace had remanded all of them. Anadolu Agency reported on 6 April 2026 that 325 suspects had been detained in the operation. All 325 referred to court were remanded in custody. Police closed 69 groups on messaging apps.

fields.summary: Istanbul police first used their AI-supported AVCI messaging-analysis system on 10 February 2026, in a drug operation across 14 provinces: 325 detained and remanded, 69 groups closed.
fields.account: AVCI (Açık Kaynak İstihbaratı Analiz Sistemi, Open Source Intelligence Analysis System) is an AI-supported program. The Istanbul Police Department's narcotics and cybercrime divisions built it in-house with a special software team. Police chief Selami Yıldız ordered the work. It infiltrates closed groups and channels on end-to-end encrypted messaging apps. It analyzes messages. It analyzes voice notes. It analyzes photos. It analyzes location data. It decodes the slang of dealers. It links profiles. It maps the relationships inside groups. By copying traffic to its own servers while the traffic is accessible, it preserves material that users later delete. Police first used AVCI on 10 February 2026, in a drug operation that was centered on Istanbul and ran across 14 provinces. Anadolu Agency reported that day that the simultaneous raids had taken place that morning in 14 provinces and 35 districts. It reported that 305 of 346 sought suspects had been detained. On 13 February 2026 the Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor's Office said that 324 suspects had been caught, 21 of them group administrators. Criminal judgeships of peace had remanded all of them. Anadolu Agency reported on 6 April 2026 that 325 suspects had been detained in the operation. All 325 referred to court were remanded in custody. Police closed 69 groups on messaging apps.

details.label: Contribution of the AI
details.value: The system's documented contribution is the first alert. TVBS reports that the system detected smoke at 05:30. UDN reports that the lithium batteries burst at about 05:33, while repeating the chairman's claim of a one-minute lead. The precise warning interval remains unresolved. The system messaged the front desk, the general manager and the chairman in sequence over LINE. That is how a chairman asleep in Nara came to follow the fire on the temple's cameras. The suppression was human. The clerk's extinguisher failed once the batteries burst. The Yunlin County Fire Bureau's eight trucks and eighteen firefighters, called at 05:36, controlled the fire at 06:10. UDN reports that a residential smoke alarm (住警器) sounded as well. The Third Brigade commander 陳岳謄 attributed the containment to the building's reinforced-concrete structure and the crews' quick arrival without mentioning the AI. The account of the LINE relay from the vendor comes from the chairman, and the fire bureau does not mention it.

record.title: After LEADERG's “AI door god” camera analytics flag smoke in an empty office at Beigang Wude Temple, the night clerk holds the fire of 5 February 2026 to ten square meters with Yunlin firefighters
record.summary: LEADERG's AI door god cameras flagged smoke in an empty office at Beigang Wude Temple before a battery fire, and the fire burned ten square meters with nobody hurt.
record.account: At about 05:30 on 5 February 2026 the AI門神 (AI door god) system picked out smoke in a first-floor office and machine room, empty after hours. The system is run by 立達軟體 (LEADERG Inc.) over the closed-circuit television of Beigang Wude Temple, Yunlin County, Taiwan. It sent a LINE message to the front desk. It sent one to the general manager. It sent one to chairman 林安樂, in Japan. The night-duty clerk reached the room with an extinguisher within a minute. At 05:33 overheated lithium batteries beside a tool charger burst. Flames spread. UDN reports that a residential smoke alarm (住警器) sounded. Staff called the emergency number 119 at 05:36. Yunlin County Fire Bureau crews arrived at 05:44. They controlled the fire at 06:10. They put it out at 06:14. Ten square meters burned. Nobody was hurt. The main hall was untouched. The statues were untouched. The Third Brigade commander 陳岳謄 attributed the containment to the building's reinforced-concrete structure. He gave the crews' quick arrival as a second reason. He did not mention the AI. On 25 August 2026, after the Zhinan Temple fire in Taipei, UDN reported that Wude Temple still relied on its AI alarm system combined with the cameras.
record.purpose: A Taiwanese software firm built AI門神 (“AI door god: temple AI fire-and-theft prevention system”) to run image recognition over a temple's existing closed-circuit television. It detects excess smoke, flame and suspicious behavior and alerts staff by text message, LINE or email. CTS reported in December 2024 that Wude Temple's door-god system would sound an alarm at once on abnormal smoke.
record.system: AI門神：宮廟AI防火防盜系統 (AI Door God: temple AI fire-and-theft prevention system), AI image recognition over the temple's existing CCTV with alerts by SMS, LINE and email
record.model_version: Not named. Advantech's case study says the image-recognition algorithms were developed with a large language model as the basis and run on an Advantech IPC-730 with a SKY-QUAD-5000A-32 accelerator card at about five seconds per frame.

ratings.reason: The temple's loss was the contents of one first-floor office of about ten square meters (staff lockers, some tea, sweets, incense and joss paper). The main hall, statues and worship areas were untouched. The temple stayed open in the run-up to the Lunar New Year crowds. The fire bureau credited the reinforced-concrete structure and its own eight-minute arrival for the containment. A conventional smoke alarm sounded as well. The AI alert's share is an earlier warning, and how much earlier is unsettled.

produced_by: A camera-analytics system (AI門神) already watching the office over the temple's existing CCTV. It was set to alert on small amounts of smoke and to message a named chain of people (front desk, general manager, chairman) over LINE.
A staffed night watch. The temple has kept someone on duty every night since it moved to the site in 1980 (民國69年). So the alert had a clerk a minute away with an extinguisher.
Smoke appeared before the lithium batteries burst, allowing an alert before the fire intensified. The precise warning interval remains unresolved.
A fire brigade eight minutes away and a reinforced-concrete annex that held the fire to one room, as the Third Brigade commander said.
must_hold: The alert reaches a person who can act within minutes. At an unstaffed site the lead time is worth little.
The camera covers the rooms where fires start (here an office and machine room with chargers, beside stored joss paper), not only the shrine.
The AI alert complements conventional detectors rather than replacing them. A residential smoke alarm sounded here as well.

data.retained_case_account: At about 05:30 on 5 February 2026 the AI門神 (AI door god) system flagged smoke in a first-floor office and machine room, empty after hours. The system is run by 立達軟體 (LEADERG Inc.) over the closed-circuit television (CCTV) of Beigang Wude Temple, Yunlin County, Taiwan. It messaged the front desk, the general manager and chairman 林安樂, in Japan, by LINE. The night-duty clerk reached the room with an extinguisher within a minute. At 05:33 overheated lithium batteries beside a tool charger burst and flames spread. Staff called 119 at 05:36. Yunlin County Fire Bureau crews arrived at 05:44, controlled it at 06:10 and put it out at 06:14. Ten square meters burned. Nobody was hurt. The main hall and statues were untouched.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The system's documented contribution is the first alert. TVBS reports that the system detected smoke at 05:30. UDN reports that the lithium batteries burst at about 05:33, while repeating the chairman's claim of a one-minute lead. The precise warning interval remains unresolved. It messaged the front desk, the general manager and the chairman in sequence over LINE. That is how a chairman asleep in Nara came to follow the fire on the temple's cameras. The suppression was human. The clerk's extinguisher failed once the batteries burst. The Yunlin County Fire Bureau's eight trucks and eighteen firefighters, called at 05:36, controlled the fire at 06:10. UDN reports that a residential smoke alarm (住警器) sounded as well. The Third Brigade commander 陳岳謄 attributed the containment to the building's reinforced-concrete structure and the crews' quick arrival without mentioning the AI. The LINE relay from the vendor is the chairman's account, not the bureau's.

fields.summary: LEADERG's AI door god cameras flagged smoke in an empty office at Beigang Wude Temple before a battery fire, and the fire burned ten square meters with nobody hurt.
fields.account: At about 05:30 on 5 February 2026 the AI門神 (AI door god) system picked out smoke in a first-floor office and machine room, empty after hours. The system is run by 立達軟體 (LEADERG Inc.) over the closed-circuit television of Beigang Wude Temple, Yunlin County, Taiwan. It sent a LINE message to the front desk. It sent one to the general manager. It sent one to chairman 林安樂, in Japan. The night-duty clerk reached the room with an extinguisher within a minute. At 05:33 overheated lithium batteries beside a tool charger burst. Flames spread. UDN reports that a residential smoke alarm (住警器) sounded. Staff called the emergency number 119 at 05:36. Yunlin County Fire Bureau crews arrived at 05:44. They controlled the fire at 06:10. They put it out at 06:14. Ten square meters burned. Nobody was hurt. The main hall was untouched. The statues were untouched. The Third Brigade commander 陳岳謄 attributed the containment to the building's reinforced-concrete structure. He gave the crews' quick arrival as a second reason. He did not mention the AI. On 25 August 2026, after the Zhinan Temple fire in Taipei, UDN reported that Wude Temple still relied on its AI alarm system combined with the cameras.

The system is run by 立達軟體 (LEADERG Inc.) over the closed-circuit television of Beigang Wude Temple, Yunlin County, Taiwan. It sent a LINE message to the front desk. It sent one to the general manager. It sent one to chairman 林安樂, in Japan. The night-duty clerk reached the room with an extinguisher within a minute. At 05:33 overheated lithium batteries beside a tool charger burst. Flames spread. UDN reports that a residential smoke alarm (住警器) sounded. Staff called the emergency number 119 at 05:36. Yunlin County Fire Bureau crews arrived at 05:44. They controlled the fire at 06:10. They put it out at 06:14. Ten square meters burned. Nobody was hurt. The main hall was untouched. The statues were untouched. The Third Brigade commander 陳岳謄 attributed the containment to the building's reinforced-concrete structure. He gave the crews' quick arrival as a second reason. He did not mention the AI. On 25 August 2026, after the Zhinan Temple fire in Taipei, UDN reported that Wude Temple still relied on its AI alarm system combined with the cameras.

produced_by: A camera-analytics system (AI門神) already watching the office over the temple's existing CCTV. It was set to alert on small amounts of smoke and to message a named chain of people (front desk, general manager, chairman) over LINE.
A staffed night watch. The temple has kept someone on duty every night since it moved to the site in 1980 (民國69年). So the alert had a clerk a minute away with an extinguisher.
Smoke appeared before the lithium batteries burst, allowing an alert before the fire intensified. The precise warning interval remains unresolved.
A fire brigade eight minutes away and a reinforced-concrete annex that held the fire to one room, as the Third Brigade commander said.
must_hold: The alert reaches a person who can act within minutes. At an unstaffed site the lead time is worth little.
The camera covers the rooms where fires start (here an office and machine room with chargers, beside stored joss paper), not only the shrine.
The AI alert complements conventional detectors rather than replacing them. A residential smoke alarm sounded here as well.

record.title: After ChatGPT flags warning signs about a fake share adviser, a 77-year-old man in Bengaluru reports a Rs 67.10 lakh fraud to police
record.summary: After withdrawals were refused, a 77-year-old Bengaluru man checked the firm with ChatGPT. It flagged warning signs. He reported a Rs 67.10 lakh fraud to police.
record.account: The New Indian Express (6 January 2026) reported on a 77-year-old resident of Binnypet, Bengaluru. In November 2025 a man using a false name contacted him. He claimed to be an adviser with IIFL Wealth Management. He promised assured allotment of shares before an initial public offering (pre-IPO shares). The victim first transferred Rs 5 lakh for a supposed ICICI Prudential AMC pre-IPO. He was shown profits in a digital wallet. Over the following weeks he made multiple real-time gross settlement (RTGS) transfers totaling Rs 67.10 lakh. His requests to withdraw even part of the funds were denied. The fraudsters demanded more payments to repay a loan before any withdrawal. He then searched for details about the company and its representatives using ChatGPT. It reportedly showed complaints. It showed inconsistencies in the company's credentials. It showed indicators associated with investment fraud. He approached the police, who registered a case under the Information Technology Act. The police said that efforts were under way to trace the money. On 6 January 2026 the Deccan Herald published a report by Prajwal D'Souza. In its headline, the paper credits the ChatGPT response with saving him from losing more money to cybercriminals. No police official is named. The victim is not named. No arrest or recovery had been reported by 29 October 2026.

data.retained_case_account: The New Indian Express (6 January 2026) reported on a 77-year-old resident of Binnypet, Bengaluru. In November 2025 a man using a false name contacted him. He claimed to be an adviser with IIFL Wealth Management and promised assured allotment of pre-IPO shares. The victim first transferred Rs 5 lakh for a supposed ICICI Prudential AMC pre-IPO and was shown profits in a digital wallet. Over the following weeks he made multiple RTGS transfers totaling Rs 67.10 lakh. When requests to withdraw even part of the funds were denied, he searched for details about the company and its representatives using ChatGPT. It reportedly flagged complaints, inconsistencies in company credentials and indicators associated with investment fraud. He then approached the police, who registered a case under the Information Technology Act. The police said that efforts were under way to trace the money. Deccan Herald (Prajwal D'Souza, 6 January 2026) framed the ChatGPT response as saving him from losing more money. No police official is named, no recovery is reported and the victim is unnamed.

record.title: AI cameras in Ho Chi Minh City identify a masked burglar by features such as his gait before Tân Hưng ward police detain him within two days
record.summary: With unnamed AI street cameras, Ho Chi Minh City police identified a masked burglar who took two laptops on 23 December 2025. He took 14 million VND. Police detained him on 24 December.
record.account: Early on 23 December 2025 an intruder entered a rented room in Tân Hưng ward, Ho Chi Minh City. He took two laptops. He took the wallet of the tenant, a 33-year-old. He took the identity papers. He took the bank card. A withdrawal of 14 million VND was made from the tenant's bank account. The tenant reported the burglary that morning. Tân Hưng Ward Police and the Criminal Police Division used the street AI camera system. It analyzed the masked man's gait. It analyzed his build. It analyzed his clothing. It analyzed his movement. It analyzed his facial data. It identified him. It reconstructed his route. At 11 p.m. on 24 December officers found the suspect, a 23-year-old man, at an internet café on Tô Ký street. He had a previous conviction for theft. He confessed. VietNamNet reports that police held the suspect for investigation of theft on 25 December 2025. Dân trí reports that he told investigators that he had sold the stolen property. The police have not said that the property was recovered.
record.purpose: Ho Chi Minh City police run street AI cameras for security and investigation. VnExpress reports that the technology analyzes and matches biometric features. Identifying a suspect from footage is the use that the police describe. Neither the system nor its vendor has been named.

data.retained_case_account: Early on 23 December 2025 an intruder entered a rented room in Tân Hưng ward, Ho Chi Minh City. He took two laptops and the wallet, identity papers and bank card of the tenant, a 33-year-old. From his account, 14 million VND was withdrawn. He reported it that morning. Tân Hưng Ward Police and the Criminal Police Division used the street AI camera system. It analyzed the masked man's gait, build, clothing, movement and facial data, identified him and reconstructed his route. At 11 p.m. on 24 December officers found the suspect, a 23-year-old man, at an internet café on Tô Ký street. He was a convicted thief. He confessed. Property recovery is not reported.

fields.account: Early on 23 December 2025 an intruder entered a rented room in Tân Hưng ward, Ho Chi Minh City. He took two laptops. He took the wallet of the tenant, a 33-year-old. He took the identity papers. He took the bank card. A withdrawal of 14 million VND was made from the tenant's bank account. The tenant reported the burglary that morning. Tân Hưng Ward Police and the Criminal Police Division used the street AI camera system. It analyzed the masked man's gait. It analyzed his build. It analyzed his clothing. It analyzed his movement. It analyzed his facial data. It identified him. It reconstructed his route. At 11 p.m. on 24 December officers found the suspect, a 23-year-old man, at an internet café on Tô Ký street. He had a previous conviction for theft. He confessed. VietNamNet reports that police held the suspect for investigation of theft on 25 December 2025. Dân trí reports that he told investigators that he had sold the stolen property. The police have not said that the property was recovered.

fields.summary: With unnamed AI street cameras, Ho Chi Minh City police identified a masked burglar who took two laptops on 23 December 2025. He took 14 million VND. Police detained him on 24 December.
fields.account: Early on 23 December 2025 an intruder entered a rented room in Tân Hưng ward, Ho Chi Minh City. He took two laptops. He took the wallet of the tenant, a 33-year-old. He took the identity papers. He took the bank card. A withdrawal of 14 million VND was made from the tenant's bank account. The tenant reported the burglary that morning. Tân Hưng Ward Police and the Criminal Police Division used the street AI camera system. It analyzed the masked man's gait. It analyzed his build. It analyzed his clothing. It analyzed his movement. It analyzed his facial data. It identified him. It reconstructed his route. At 11 p.m. on 24 December officers found the suspect, a 23-year-old man, at an internet café on Tô Ký street. He had a previous conviction for theft. He confessed. VietNamNet reports that police held the suspect for investigation of theft on 25 December 2025. Dân trí reports that he told investigators that he had sold the stolen property. The police have not said that the property was recovered.

record.title: Garmin Autoland lands a King Air B200 at Broomfield, Colorado, in its first real emergency use after the plane loses cabin pressure at 23,000 feet
record.summary: Garmin Autoland engaged when a King Air B200 lost cabin pressure on 20 December 2025. It landed the plane at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport, with the two pilots unhurt.
record.account: On Saturday 20 December 2025 Buffalo River Aviation's Beechcraft Super King Air B200, N479BR, left Aspen-Pitkin County Airport at 1:43 p.m. It carried two pilots and no passengers. At about 23,000 feet it suffered a rapid, uncommanded loss of pressurization. When cabin altitude passed the safe limit, Garmin Autoland engaged automatically. It sent automated emergency broadcasts to air traffic control. The crew chose to leave it engaged. It flew the aircraft to a landing on Runway 30 at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport, Broomfield, Colorado, shortly after 2 p.m. Nobody was treated. The operator said that the aircraft returned to service the next day. The Federal Aviation Administration said that it was investigating. The National Transportation Safety Board said that it was gathering information. Garmin called it the first use of Autoland from start to finish in an actual emergency. On 27 December 2025 AvBrief reported audio that Max Trescott, a host of the NTSB NewsTalk podcast, recorded while flying nearby. The audio shows that with Autoland engaged the crew could transmit only on the guard frequency. It shows that they could not switch to the controllers' frequencies. The National Transportation Safety Board lists nothing for the aircraft in its database of investigations. On 14 October 2026 Garmin reported that more than 2,500 aircraft carry the system. In 2026 Autoland was certified on four more models, which included the first twin-engine jets. No second real-world activation had been reported by then. The two federal agencies had reported no finding on the Colorado flight.
record.purpose: Garmin built Autoland to take complete control of an aircraft and land it when the pilot cannot fly. It engages on its own when the cabin altitude exceeds a set level, as it did here. The two pilots were not incapacitated, though, and chose to let it finish.

fields.account: On Saturday 20 December 2025 Buffalo River Aviation's Beechcraft Super King Air B200, N479BR, left Aspen-Pitkin County Airport at 1:43 p.m. It carried two pilots and no passengers. At about 23,000 feet it suffered a rapid, uncommanded loss of pressurization. When cabin altitude passed the safe limit, Garmin Autoland engaged automatically. It sent automated emergency broadcasts to air traffic control. The crew chose to leave it engaged. It flew the aircraft to a landing on Runway 30 at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport, Broomfield, Colorado, shortly after 2 p.m. Nobody was treated. The operator said that the aircraft returned to service the next day. The Federal Aviation Administration said that it was investigating. The National Transportation Safety Board said that it was gathering information. Garmin called it the first use of Autoland from start to finish in an actual emergency. On 27 December 2025 AvBrief reported audio that Max Trescott, a host of the NTSB NewsTalk podcast, recorded while flying nearby. The audio shows that with Autoland engaged the crew could transmit only on the guard frequency. It shows that they could not switch to the controllers' frequencies. The National Transportation Safety Board lists nothing for the aircraft in its database of investigations. On 14 October 2026 Garmin reported that more than 2,500 aircraft carry the system. In 2026 Autoland was certified on four more models, which included the first twin-engine jets. No second real-world activation had been reported by then. The two federal agencies had reported no finding on the Colorado flight.

record.title: The World Bank's Independent Evaluation Group reports 133 monitoring points in nursing facilities linked to 17 categories of AI algorithms for safety in Anhui
record.summary: The World Bank's evaluation office counted 133 monitoring points in nursing homes among the efficiency gains of Anhui's aged care platform. They link to 17 kinds of AI-based algorithms for safety.
record.account: The Anhui Aged Care System Demonstration Project, financed by a World Bank loan, closed on 31 October 2025. Its first component supported the Anhui Provincial Department of Civil Affairs in building a unified provincial aged care information platform. The World Bank's Independent Evaluation Group reviewed the completion report on 24 June 2026. It rated efficiency substantial. The evaluators report that the completion report documented administrative and system-level efficiency gains from the platform that were left unquantified at appraisal. By closing, the platform had connected 133 nursing facility monitoring points with 17 categories of artificial intelligence-based safety algorithms. These gains were not included in the benefit-cost ratio or the economic rate of return. The evaluators judged the completion report's evidence base strong, drawn from the platform's administrative records. According to the Bank's own completion report of 23 March 2026, the algorithms provide real-time alerts for events such as falls, unoccupied beds and other safety risks. It contains the provincial government's statement that the tools have measurably reduced accidents in connected facilities. It contains a caveat that no precise quantification is available. The algorithms' supplier is not named in either document. The two documents give no figure for accidents.

fields.summary: The World Bank's evaluation office counted 133 monitoring points in nursing homes among the efficiency gains of Anhui's aged care platform. They link to 17 kinds of AI-based algorithms for safety.
fields.account: The Anhui Aged Care System Demonstration Project, financed by a World Bank loan, closed on 31 October 2025. Its first component supported the Anhui Provincial Department of Civil Affairs in building a unified provincial aged care information platform. The World Bank's Independent Evaluation Group reviewed the completion report on 24 June 2026. It rated efficiency substantial. The evaluators report that the completion report documented administrative and system-level efficiency gains from the platform that were left unquantified at appraisal. By closing, the platform had connected 133 nursing facility monitoring points with 17 categories of artificial intelligence-based safety algorithms. These gains were not included in the benefit-cost ratio or the economic rate of return. The evaluators judged the completion report's evidence base strong, drawn from the platform's administrative records. According to the Bank's own completion report of 23 March 2026, the algorithms provide real-time alerts for events such as falls, unoccupied beds and other safety risks. It contains the provincial government's statement that the tools have measurably reduced accidents in connected facilities. It contains a caveat that no precise quantification is available. The algorithms' supplier is not named in either document. The two documents give no figure for accidents.

record.title: NHC blended Google DeepMind's AI ensemble into official Hurricane Melissa forecasts before its Category 5 landfall in Jamaica
record.summary: The US National Hurricane Center blended Google DeepMind's AI ensemble into its Melissa forecasts from 21 October 2025. The center's track errors at 120 hours were less than half its five-year mean.
record.account: The US National Hurricane Center (NHC) blended Google DeepMind's experimental AI hurricane model into official forecasts for Tropical Storm Melissa from its first advisory on 21 October 2025. In NHC's guidance, the model's ensemble mean is labeled GDMI. In Discussion 1, the forecasters placed the official track between the DeepMind ensemble mean and the corrected consensus aid HCCA. In Discussion 2, they described the track as a blend of the DeepMind mean, HCCA and the simple consensus TVCA. In Discussion 8, on 23 October, they moved the track toward a blend of the DeepMind mean and HCCA. Later that day, in Discussion 10, they blended the HCCA and GDMI aids. They set an intensity forecast in best agreement with GDMI after all 50 DeepMind members showed a major hurricane. Also on 23 October, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) approved a CHF 80,000 Imminent DREF (Disaster Response Emergency Fund) allocation with a five-day lead time. On 24 October, in Discussion 13, they noted that every DeepMind member showed the system becoming a Category 4 hurricane or stronger. In Discussion 14, they put the intensity forecast closest to GDMI. On 28 October 2025 Melissa made landfall in southwestern Jamaica near New Hope with winds of 185 miles per hour and a pressure of 892 millibars. The IFRC reported 45 deaths and about 1.6 million people affected. It relayed an estimate by the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank of US$8.8 billion in physical damage. On 3 November 2025 Michael Lowry, a hurricane specialist, wrote that the model gave NHC forecasters extra confidence to issue uncharacteristically aggressive forecasts. CNN reported on 3 December 2025 that the DeepMind ensemble gave NHC forecasters an unusually high degree of confidence in Melissa's rapid intensification about three days before landfall. In its own report on Melissa, first issued on 25 February 2026, NHC says that this was the first time it had predicted Category 5 strength from a Category 1 start. Its errors in the track of Melissa at 120 hours were less than half its five-year mean. The DeepMind ensemble mean alone had lower track errors than the official forecast at 48 hours, 32.6 against 40.3 nautical miles. At 120 hours its errors were higher, 113.2 against 87.7 nautical miles. In its verification report for 2025, dated 30 March 2026, NHC says that its track errors were well below average for major hurricanes, including Melissa.

data.retained_case_account: The US National Hurricane Center (NHC) blended Google DeepMind's experimental AI hurricane model (ensemble mean GDMI) into official forecasts for Tropical Storm Melissa. It did so from its first advisory, 21 October 2025. Discussion 1 placed the official track between the DeepMind ensemble mean and the consensus aid HCCA. Discussion 2 described the track as a blend of the DeepMind mean, HCCA and TVCA. Discussion 8 (23 October) moved the track toward a blend of the DeepMind mean and HCCA. Discussion 10 blended the HCCA and GDMI aids. It set an intensity forecast in best agreement with GDMI after all 50 DeepMind members showed a major hurricane. On 28 October 2025 Melissa made landfall in southwestern Jamaica near New Hope with 185 mph winds and 892 mb pressure. IFRC reported 45 deaths and about 1.6 million people affected. It relayed a World Bank/IDB estimate of US$8.8 billion in physical damage. Its CHF 80,000 Imminent DREF was approved on 23 October with a five-day lead time.

fields.account: The US National Hurricane Center (NHC) blended Google DeepMind's experimental AI hurricane model into official forecasts for Tropical Storm Melissa from its first advisory on 21 October 2025. In NHC's guidance, the model's ensemble mean is labeled GDMI. In Discussion 1, the forecasters placed the official track between the DeepMind ensemble mean and the corrected consensus aid HCCA. In Discussion 2, they described the track as a blend of the DeepMind mean, HCCA and the simple consensus TVCA. In Discussion 8, on 23 October, they moved the track toward a blend of the DeepMind mean and HCCA. Later that day, in Discussion 10, they blended the HCCA and GDMI aids. They set an intensity forecast in best agreement with GDMI after all 50 DeepMind members showed a major hurricane. Also on 23 October, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) approved a CHF 80,000 Imminent DREF (Disaster Response Emergency Fund) allocation with a five-day lead time. On 24 October, in Discussion 13, they noted that every DeepMind member showed the system becoming a Category 4 hurricane or stronger. In Discussion 14, they put the intensity forecast closest to GDMI. On 28 October 2025 Melissa made landfall in southwestern Jamaica near New Hope with winds of 185 miles per hour and a pressure of 892 millibars. The IFRC reported 45 deaths and about 1.6 million people affected. It relayed an estimate by the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank of US$8.8 billion in physical damage. On 3 November 2025 Michael Lowry, a hurricane specialist, wrote that the model gave NHC forecasters extra confidence to issue uncharacteristically aggressive forecasts. CNN reported on 3 December 2025 that the DeepMind ensemble gave NHC forecasters an unusually high degree of confidence in Melissa's rapid intensification about three days before landfall. In its own report on Melissa, first issued on 25 February 2026, NHC says that this was the first time it had predicted Category 5 strength from a Category 1 start. Its errors in the track of Melissa at 120 hours were less than half its five-year mean. The DeepMind ensemble mean alone had lower track errors than the official forecast at 48 hours, 32.6 against 40.3 nautical miles. At 120 hours its errors were higher, 113.2 against 87.7 nautical miles. In its verification report for 2025, dated 30 March 2026, NHC says that its track errors were well below average for major hurricanes, including Melissa.

outcomes[].duration.reason: The duration of the claimed benefit is not separately established. Dated follow-up on the same outcome is needed to distinguish a one-time result from recurring or sustained benefit; later work on another system or population does not establish persistence here. The recorded follow-up says: NHC's 2025 verification report, five months after landfall, records low official track errors for Melissa and the DeepMind ensemble mean outperforming the official Atlantic track forecast at 12 to 72 hours.

ratings.reason: The National Hurricane Center has not credited the AI guidance with an outcome for any individual. The impacts reported cover only the population as a whole.

NHC forecasters blended the DeepMind ensemble into official track forecasts from Discussion 1 and set intensity forecasts closest to it from Discussion 10. Melissa's official track error at 120 hours was 87.7 nautical miles, against a five-year mean of 185.4 nautical miles. NHC's Science Operations Officer called the AI guidance very valuable for Melissa.

No cited report shows that the AI guidance changed preparations or losses in Jamaica. The forecasts covered a Category 5 landfall that affected about 1.6 million people, and the IFRC approved its emergency allocation five days ahead.

value.text: CNN and Lowry report that forecasters gained early confidence from the AI guidance and that NHC issued aggressive, accurate forecasts days before landfall. NHC's own report shows that its track errors for Melissa were far below its five-year mean.

display.answer: Ten of the twelve cited sources come from the deployer's side. They are six NHC forecast discussions, a landfall update, the 2025 verification report, the Melissa tropical cyclone report and a National Weather Service interview with NHC's Science Operations Officer. Both independent sources, CNN and Michael Lowry's newsletter, draw on retired NHC forecaster James Franklin. CNN also interviewed NHC staff. The figures on deaths and damage come from IFRC reports, which do not isolate the AI's effects.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: The US National Hurricane Center blended Google DeepMind's AI ensemble into its Melissa forecasts from 21 October 2025. The center's track errors at 120 hours were less than half its five-year mean.
fields.account: The US National Hurricane Center (NHC) blended Google DeepMind's experimental AI hurricane model into official forecasts for Tropical Storm Melissa from its first advisory on 21 October 2025. In NHC's guidance, the model's ensemble mean is labeled GDMI. In Discussion 1, the forecasters placed the official track between the DeepMind ensemble mean and the corrected consensus aid HCCA. In Discussion 2, they described the track as a blend of the DeepMind mean, HCCA and the simple consensus TVCA. In Discussion 8, on 23 October, they moved the track toward a blend of the DeepMind mean and HCCA. Later that day, in Discussion 10, they blended the HCCA and GDMI aids. They set an intensity forecast in best agreement with GDMI after all 50 DeepMind members showed a major hurricane. Also on 23 October, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) approved a CHF 80,000 Imminent DREF (Disaster Response Emergency Fund) allocation with a five-day lead time. On 24 October, in Discussion 13, they noted that every DeepMind member showed the system becoming a Category 4 hurricane or stronger. In Discussion 14, they put the intensity forecast closest to GDMI. On 28 October 2025 Melissa made landfall in southwestern Jamaica near New Hope with winds of 185 miles per hour and a pressure of 892 millibars. The IFRC reported 45 deaths and about 1.6 million people affected. It relayed an estimate by the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank of US$8.8 billion in physical damage. On 3 November 2025 Michael Lowry, a hurricane specialist, wrote that the model gave NHC forecasters extra confidence to issue uncharacteristically aggressive forecasts. CNN reported on 3 December 2025 that the DeepMind ensemble gave NHC forecasters an unusually high degree of confidence in Melissa's rapid intensification about three days before landfall. In its own report on Melissa, first issued on 25 February 2026, NHC says that this was the first time it had predicted Category 5 strength from a Category 1 start. Its errors in the track of Melissa at 120 hours were less than half its five-year mean. The DeepMind ensemble mean alone had lower track errors than the official forecast at 48 hours, 32.6 against 40.3 nautical miles. At 120 hours its errors were higher, 113.2 against 87.7 nautical miles. In its verification report for 2025, dated 30 March 2026, NHC says that its track errors were well below average for major hurricanes, including Melissa.

record.title: Coop Szeged's 247 Shop on Szent István tér is unstaffed at night. Its operators say that Veesion gesture-recognition cameras there flag a shopper hiding goods under clothing. They say that police catch the perpetrator within hours with the footage. It is one of three theft attempts exposed in the store's first four and a half months
record.summary: The operators said that Veesion's gesture-recognition software flagged a shopper hiding goods in their Szeged store at night. They said that police caught the perpetrator within hours.
record.account: Coop Szeged Zrt. and Laurel Kft. opened the 247 Shop on Szent István tér in Szeged at the end of May 2025. It is staffed by day. Outside normal hours it runs automatically with no staff. Cameras running the French company Veesion's software analyze shoppers' movements without identifying faces. They alert a remote dispatch service to gestures such as concealing goods. On 8 October 2025 the Szeged daily Délmagyar reported that a security guard had been placed in the store after closing because of thefts. Thieves had followed customers in and out after the customers opened the door with the app. A thief known to police came in at least twice. The thief was caught quickly with camera footage. The operators said that the guard was temporary while the system was fine-tuned. They said that the rate of abuse was no higher than in traditional shops. On 9 October 2025 the operators issued a press release, relayed by Index.hu and MTI. It said that over four and a half months the system had exposed three theft attempts. In one, a person hid products under their clothing during night mode. Police caught the perpetrator within hours using the footage. The dates are not reported. Recovered goods are not reported. No police statement is reported. The operators said that 8,500 people had shopped in the automated night system in four and a half months. They said that shrinkage had not risen despite the longer opening hours. On 30 September 2026 the two companies opened a second store that is unstaffed after hours, a full supermarket on Temesvári körút. The first store had recorded more than 27,000 unstaffed purchases in a year. Reporters at the opening describe monitoring by camera. They describe a remote dispatch service. They do not name Veesion.
record.purpose: Veesion built its gesture-recognition software to spot shoplifting movements, such as hiding goods, and to raise an immediate alert. In Laurel's 247 Shop it guards against losses when no staff are present.
record.system: Veesion AI gesture-recognition camera analysis integrated into Laurel Kft.'s 247 Shop hybrid-store platform, with alerts to a remote dispatch service
record.model_version: Not reported
record.deployer: Coop Szeged Zrt. (store operator), with Laurel Kft. as technology partner

ratings.reason: The store operator gained a flagged concealment and footage that led police to the perpetrator within hours. Three attempts were exposed over four and a half months of unstaffed night trading. The operators say that shrinkage did not rise. All figures are the companies' own. No loss amount or recovery is reported.

data.answer:
AI cameras in Szeged's unstaffed-at-night Coop flagged a shopper hiding goods; police caught them within hours, the operators said.

The retained press-release accounts do not establish whether the theft was prevented, goods were recovered, or losses fell overall. Independent police confirmation and false-alert information are missing from the reviewed material.

By the operators' account, the Veesion analysis flagged the shopper's concealment gesture in real time and alerted the remote dispatcher. The camera footage let police catch the perpetrator within hours. No police statement, loss figure or description of what the dispatcher did at the moment of the alert was found. Whether the theft was stopped in progress or only documented, and whether the goods came back, is unknown. The claim rests on a joint press release by the deployer and its integrator, relayed by independent outlets.

data.retained_case_account: Coop Szeged Zrt. and Laurel Kft. opened the 247 Shop on Szent István tér in Szeged at the end of May 2025. It is staffed by day, automated and unstaffed outside normal hours. Cameras running the French company Veesion's software analyze shoppers' movements without identifying faces. fields.account: Coop Szeged Zrt. and Laurel Kft. opened the 247 Shop on Szent István tér in Szeged at the end of May 2025. It is staffed by day. Outside normal hours it runs automatically with no staff. Cameras running the French company Veesion's software analyze shoppers' movements without identifying faces. They alert a remote dispatch service to gestures such as concealing goods. On 8 October 2025 the Szeged daily Délmagyar reported that a security guard had been placed in the store after closing because of thefts. Thieves had followed customers in and out after the customers opened the door with the app. A thief known to police came in at least twice. The thief was caught quickly with camera footage. The operators said that the guard was temporary while the system was fine-tuned. They said that the rate of abuse was no higher than in traditional shops. On 9 October 2025 the operators issued a press release, relayed by Index.hu and MTI. It said that over four and a half months the system had exposed three theft attempts. In one, a person hid products under their clothing during night mode. Police caught the perpetrator within hours using the footage. The dates are not reported. Recovered goods are not reported. No police statement is reported. The operators said that 8,500 people had shopped in the automated night system in four and a half months. They said that shrinkage had not risen despite the longer opening hours. On 30 September 2026 the two companies opened a second store that is unstaffed after hours, a full supermarket on Temesvári körút. The first store had recorded more than 27,000 unstaffed purchases in a year. Reporters at the opening describe monitoring by camera. They describe a remote dispatch service. They do not name Veesion.

fields.summary: The operators said that Veesion's gesture-recognition software flagged a shopper hiding goods in their Szeged store at night. They said that police caught the perpetrator within hours.
fields.account: Coop Szeged Zrt. and Laurel Kft. opened the 247 Shop on Szent István tér in Szeged at the end of May 2025. It is staffed by day. Outside normal hours it runs automatically with no staff. Cameras running the French company Veesion's software analyze shoppers' movements without identifying faces. They alert a remote dispatch service to gestures such as concealing goods. On 8 October 2025 the Szeged daily Délmagyar reported that a security guard had been placed in the store after closing because of thefts. Thieves had followed customers in and out after the customers opened the door with the app. A thief known to police came in at least twice. The thief was caught quickly with camera footage. The operators said that the guard was temporary while the system was fine-tuned. They said that the rate of abuse was no higher than in traditional shops. On 9 October 2025 the operators issued a press release, relayed by Index.hu and MTI. It said that over four and a half months the system had exposed three theft attempts. In one, a person hid products under their clothing during night mode. Police caught the perpetrator within hours using the footage. The dates are not reported. Recovered goods are not reported. No police statement is reported. The operators said that 8,500 people had shopped in the automated night system in four and a half months. They said that shrinkage had not risen despite the longer opening hours. On 30 September 2026 the two companies opened a second store that is unstaffed after hours, a full supermarket on Temesvári körút. The first store had recorded more than 27,000 unstaffed purchases in a year. Reporters at the opening describe monitoring by camera. They describe a remote dispatch service. They do not name Veesion.
