fields.account: The ALERTCalifornia AI, a machine-learned model run by the University of California San Diego, scans live feeds from more than 1,000 cameras. It began scanning the feeds at the end of June 2023 in a trial with Cal Fire. At about 3 a.m. on 5 August 2023, the AI picked out a column of smoke in the Cleveland National Forest near Mount Laguna. That is about 40 miles east of San Diego. Human operators verified the detection. They alerted Cal Fire. On 24 August 2023 the Los Angeles Times reported that Scott Slumpff, a battalion chief at Cal Fire, got the confirmed alert just before 3 a.m. The Times reported that crews held the fire to a spot 10 feet by 10 feet. Slumpff said that without the alert nobody would have known about the fire until the next morning. He judged that it would probably have reached hundreds of acres. On 12 September 2023 AFP reported that the operators had alerted Cal Fire Captain Kris Yeary. It reported that his crews put the fire out at less than a quarter acre. Yeary told AFP that it could have become a devastating fire had the AI not alerted them. By September 2023 the tool reached all 21 Cal Fire dispatch centers. According to Cal Fire's figures for 2024, the cameras picked up 1,668 of 7,553 wildfires in its jurisdiction, 636 of them before any 911 call.

fields.summary: ALERTCalifornia's AI flagged smoke on a Cleveland National Forest camera at about 3 a.m. on 5 August 2023. Cal Fire held the verified fire under a quarter acre.
fields.account: The ALERTCalifornia AI, a machine-learned model run by the University of California San Diego, scans live feeds from more than 1,000 cameras. It began scanning the feeds at the end of June 2023 in a trial with Cal Fire. At about 3 a.m. on 5 August 2023, the AI picked out a column of smoke in the Cleveland National Forest near Mount Laguna. That is about 40 miles east of San Diego. Human operators verified the detection. They alerted Cal Fire. On 24 August 2023 the Los Angeles Times reported that Scott Slumpff, a battalion chief at Cal Fire, got the confirmed alert just before 3 a.m. The Times reported that crews held the fire to a spot 10 feet by 10 feet. Slumpff said that without the alert nobody would have known about the fire until the next morning. He judged that it would probably have reached hundreds of acres. On 12 September 2023 AFP reported that the operators had alerted Cal Fire Captain Kris Yeary. It reported that his crews put the fire out at less than a quarter acre. Yeary told AFP that it could have become a devastating fire had the AI not alerted them. By September 2023 the tool reached all 21 Cal Fire dispatch centers. According to Cal Fire's figures for 2024, the cameras picked up 1,668 of 7,553 wildfires in its jurisdiction, 636 of them before any 911 call.

record.title: Chilean prosecutors credit the AI model “Fiscal Heredia” with identifying a 10-member gang. A court accredits 8 “encerrona” robberies
record.summary: In Operación Influencer (11 May 2023) the authorities detained a gang of 10 behind eight accredited violent robberies. Prosecutors credit the AI model Fiscal Heredia.
record.account: In the early hours of Thursday 11 May 2023, Focos Occidente and the Brigada de Investigación Criminal of Chile's Policía de Investigaciones carried out a joint investigation. They executed 30 search warrants across Maipú, Pudahuel, Cerro Navia and other comunas. There were 17 detentions. Ten of them were linked to “encerronas” (robbery with intimidation or violence) whose perpetrators posted their robberies on TikTok. On 12 May 2023 the television channel T13 quoted Fiscal Nacional Ángel Valencia saying that the algorithm accelerates criminal analysis. T13 reports that after three members were arrested, the model searched their links. It reports that the model raised persons of interest whom victims later identified. The Fiscalía de Chile issued a regional news release on 17 May 2023. It says that the ten were identified through the software Fiscal Heredia (Herramienta para el Estudio del Delito Usando Inteligencia Artificial). The Fiscalía describes it as an AI model that several universities developed. The Ministerio Público adopted it in March 2023. The model proposes probable participants from the records of the prosecution. It draws on police records. Prosecutors and police then work them up. The Noveno Juzgado de Garantía accredited the eight robberies. Four adults went to preventive detention. Four adolescents remained in provisional internment. On 25 August 2026 the Fiscalía named the developers as the Universidad de Chile, the Universidad del Biobío and the Universidad de los Andes. They worked with the Ministerio Público in a project, funded by the Fondo de Fomento al Desarrollo Científico y Tecnológico (Fondef), that began in 2020. The Fiscalía reported that the tool, now called Fiscal HeredIA, runs in 15 regional prosecutor's offices with more than 1,000 prosecutors and other users. It reported that the tool won second place in the IFORS Prize for OR in Development 2026.

fields.summary: In Operación Influencer (11 May 2023) the authorities detained a gang of 10 behind eight accredited violent robberies. Prosecutors credit the AI model Fiscal Heredia.
fields.account: In the early hours of Thursday 11 May 2023, Focos Occidente and the Brigada de Investigación Criminal of Chile's Policía de Investigaciones carried out a joint investigation. They executed 30 search warrants across Maipú, Pudahuel, Cerro Navia and other comunas. There were 17 detentions. Ten of them were linked to “encerronas” (robbery with intimidation or violence) whose perpetrators posted their robberies on TikTok. On 12 May 2023 the television channel T13 quoted Fiscal Nacional Ángel Valencia saying that the algorithm accelerates criminal analysis. T13 reports that after three members were arrested, the model searched their links. It reports that the model raised persons of interest whom victims later identified. The Fiscalía de Chile issued a regional news release on 17 May 2023. It says that the ten were identified through the software Fiscal Heredia (Herramienta para el Estudio del Delito Usando Inteligencia Artificial). The Fiscalía describes it as an AI model that several universities developed. The Ministerio Público adopted it in March 2023. The model proposes probable participants from the records of the prosecution. It draws on police records. Prosecutors and police then work them up. The Noveno Juzgado de Garantía accredited the eight robberies. Four adults went to preventive detention. Four adolescents remained in provisional internment. On 25 August 2026 the Fiscalía named the developers as the Universidad de Chile, the Universidad del Biobío and the Universidad de los Andes. They worked with the Ministerio Público in a project, funded by the Fondo de Fomento al Desarrollo Científico y Tecnológico (Fondef), that began in 2020. The Fiscalía reported that the tool, now called Fiscal HeredIA, runs in 15 regional prosecutor's offices with more than 1,000 prosecutors and other users. It reported that the tool won second place in the IFORS Prize for OR in Development 2026.

record.title: Responders in Türkiye used machine-learning maps of damage from xView2 after the earthquakes of 6 February 2023
record.summary: xView2 is a machine-learning model that grades building damage in satellite images. After the 2023 Türkiye earthquakes, it gave responders maps that UN rescue teams used in Adıyaman.
record.account: In 2019 the Pentagon's Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) and Carnegie Mellon University's Software Engineering Institute sponsored xView2, an open-source project to assess damage to buildings. The two bodies developed it. Partners included Microsoft and the University of California, Berkeley. It uses machine learning (semantic segmentation) on satellite imagery to identify damage to buildings. It grades the damage. The authors of Microsoft's February 2023 “Turkey Earthquake Report” include Microsoft AI for Good staff. Ritwik Gupta, DIU's principal AI scientist, is among them. They state that the team worked with Türkiye's Disaster and Emergency Management Presidency (AFAD) to deliver building-level damage estimates over four cities in southeast Türkiye. The report’s image dates range from 7 to 9 February 2023. The authors estimated 3,849 damaged buildings, including destroyed ones. Marash was the most affected, at 7.44% of buildings. MIT Technology Review reported on xView2 on 20 February 2023. Gupta told the magazine that at least two ground teams of search and rescue personnel from the UN's International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) had used xView2 in Adıyaman. Gupta said that it helped workers find damaged areas that they were unaware of. Gupta added that AFAD, the World Bank, the International Federation of the Red Cross (IFRC) and the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) had all used the platform. Atishay Abbhi, a World Bank disaster risk management specialist, said that the same degree of assessment would typically take weeks and now takes hours or minutes. The magazine gives 9 February 2023 as the first date with usable images. The technical report that it links includes 7 February imagery for Islahiye, with 9 February imagery for the other three cities. The magazine says that the model is up to 85 or 90% accurate. The World Bank does not mention xView2, AI or Microsoft in its GRADE report. No responder has described a decision taken on xView2 output. On 27 October 2025 researchers from Stanford University and Direct Relief published in PLOS Digital Health an outside test of the Microsoft model built on xBD, the dataset behind xView2. The test covered 38 facilities in three cities. Some were hospitals. The others were dialysis centers. The model found 42.86% of the damaged facilities. It correctly cleared 93.55% of the undamaged ones. The authors conclude that such models cannot yet replace ground surveys. In an article of 10 December 2025, Direct Relief describes this study of Microsoft and Google models. It does not describe a response decision.

data.retained_case_account: MIT Technology Review reported on 20 February 2023 on xView2, an open-source building-damage assessment project. It was sponsored and developed in 2019 by the Pentagon's Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) and Carnegie Mellon University's Software Engineering Institute. Partners included Microsoft and UC Berkeley. It uses machine-learning (semantic segmentation) on satellite imagery to identify and grade building damage. Ritwik Gupta, DIU's principal AI scientist, told the magazine about use in Türkiye. At least two ground teams of search and rescue personnel from the UN's International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) had used xView2 in Adıyaman. He said it helped workers find damaged areas they were unaware of. He said AFAD, the World Bank, the IFRC and WFP had all used the platform. Atishay Abbhi, a World Bank disaster risk management specialist, said the same degree of assessment would typically take weeks and now takes hours or minutes. The article gives February 9, 2023, as the first usable-image date. However, the linked technical report includes February 7 imagery for Islahiye and February 9 imagery for the other three cities. It says the model is up to 85 or 90% accurate. Microsoft's February 2023 “Turkey Earthquake Report” has authors including Gupta and Microsoft AI for Good staff. It states that the team partnered with AFAD to deliver building-level damage estimates over four cities in southeast Türkiye. The report’s image dates range from February 7 to February 9. It estimated 3,849 buildings damaged or destroyed, with Marash the most affected at 7.44% of buildings. The World Bank GRADE report does not mention xView2, AI or Microsoft. DLR's peer-reviewed account states its own AI damage products were not part of the viewer delivered to responders. Direct Relief's December 2025 article describes a research study on Microsoft and Google models rather than a response decision. No responder statement describing a decision taken on xView2 output is among the sources.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The AI produced the damage classifications that responders are said to have used. Which decisions changed is not documented. Sources: the developer (DIU's Gupta) and the World Bank specialist, quoted in one news report, and Microsoft's own report of delivering estimates to AFAD. World Bank's GRADE report and DLR's account do not corroborate operational use of AI products.

fields.account: In 2019 the Pentagon's Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) and Carnegie Mellon University's Software Engineering Institute sponsored xView2, an open-source project to assess damage to buildings. The two bodies developed it. Partners included Microsoft and the University of California, Berkeley. It uses machine learning (semantic segmentation) on satellite imagery to identify damage to buildings. It grades the damage. The authors of Microsoft's February 2023 “Turkey Earthquake Report” include Microsoft AI for Good staff. Ritwik Gupta, DIU's principal AI scientist, is among them. They state that the team worked with Türkiye's Disaster and Emergency Management Presidency (AFAD) to deliver building-level damage estimates over four cities in southeast Türkiye. The report’s image dates range from 7 to 9 February 2023. The authors estimated 3,849 damaged buildings, including destroyed ones. Marash was the most affected, at 7.44% of buildings. MIT Technology Review reported on xView2 on 20 February 2023. Gupta told the magazine that at least two ground teams of search and rescue personnel from the UN's International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) had used xView2 in Adıyaman. Gupta said that it helped workers find damaged areas that they were unaware of. Gupta added that AFAD, the World Bank, the International Federation of the Red Cross (IFRC) and the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) had all used the platform. Atishay Abbhi, a World Bank disaster risk management specialist, said that the same degree of assessment would typically take weeks and now takes hours or minutes. The magazine gives 9 February 2023 as the first date with usable images. The technical report that it links includes 7 February imagery for Islahiye, with 9 February imagery for the other three cities. The magazine says that the model is up to 85 or 90% accurate. The World Bank does not mention xView2, AI or Microsoft in its GRADE report. No responder has described a decision taken on xView2 output. On 27 October 2025 researchers from Stanford University and Direct Relief published in PLOS Digital Health an outside test of the Microsoft model built on xBD, the dataset behind xView2. fields.account: In 2019 the Pentagon's Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) and Carnegie Mellon University's Software Engineering Institute sponsored xView2, an open-source project to assess damage to buildings. The two bodies developed it. Partners included Microsoft and the University of California, Berkeley. It uses machine learning (semantic segmentation) on satellite imagery to identify damage to buildings. It grades the damage. The authors of Microsoft's February 2023 “Turkey Earthquake Report” include Microsoft AI for Good staff. Ritwik Gupta, DIU's principal AI scientist, is among them. They state that the team worked with Türkiye's Disaster and Emergency Management Presidency (AFAD) to deliver building-level damage estimates over four cities in southeast Türkiye. The report’s image dates range from 7 to 9 February 2023. The authors estimated 3,849 damaged buildings, including destroyed ones. Marash was the most affected, at 7.44% of buildings. MIT Technology Review reported on xView2 on 20 February 2023. Gupta told the magazine that at least two ground teams of search and rescue personnel from the UN's International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) had used xView2 in Adıyaman. Gupta said that it helped workers find damaged areas that they were unaware of. Gupta added that AFAD, the World Bank, the International Federation of the Red Cross (IFRC) and the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) had all used the platform. Atishay Abbhi, a World Bank disaster risk management specialist, said that the same degree of assessment would typically take weeks and now takes hours or minutes. The magazine gives 9 February 2023 as the first date with usable images. The technical report that it links includes 7 February imagery for Islahiye, with 9 February imagery for the other three cities. The magazine says that the model is up to 85 or 90% accurate. The World Bank does not mention xView2, AI or Microsoft in its GRADE report. No responder has described a decision taken on xView2 output. On 27 October 2025 researchers from Stanford University and Direct Relief published in PLOS Digital Health an outside test of the Microsoft model built on xBD, the dataset behind xView2. The test covered 38 facilities in three cities. Some were hospitals. The others were dialysis centers. The model found 42.86% of the damaged facilities. It correctly cleared 93.55% of the undamaged ones. The authors conclude that such models cannot yet replace ground surveys. In an article of 10 December 2025, Direct Relief describes this study of Microsoft and Google models. It does not describe a response decision.

record.title: An alert about self-harm from Instagram to the cyber police of Madhya Pradesh leads Satna officers within about an hour to a 17-year-old who goes home after counseling (3 November 2022)
record.summary: An alert from Instagram's self-harm detection led Madhya Pradesh police to a 17-year-old in Satna within about an hour on 3 November 2022. She went home after counseling.
record.account: On 3 November 2022 at about 5 pm, Madhya Pradesh's state cyber police received an alert emailed by Instagram's US office. It said that a user in the state had suffered a body injury. The Indore cyber-crime unit shared the “self-harm” alert with the cyber headquarters in Bhopal (ANI, 5 November 2022, as well as Times of India, 4 November 2022). The girl, 17, had uploaded two videos. In one, a packet of poison lay beside her as she acted as if drunk. In the other she appeared to cut a vein (ANI). The Times of India notes a small cut on her wrist. Vaibhav Shrivastava, superintendent of police with the state cyber police, said: “After an effort of one hour, we traced the location of the girl”. She was in Satna district, whose police were informed (ANI). Ashutosh Gupta, the Satna superintendent of police, said that officers located her. He said that they called her in with her mother. She said that she only wanted to scare her boyfriend. She was sent home after counseling (Times of India). In January 2026 Decode reported that Meta reviews flagged posts before it alerts police. It reported that Meta publishes no data on false alarms. Decode also interviewed police in Uttar Pradesh. It described a false alarm in Kanpur Dehat. There a student said that she had posted a video with tablets only to gain views.

fields.summary: An alert from Instagram's self-harm detection led Madhya Pradesh police to a 17-year-old in Satna within about an hour on 3 November 2022. She went home after counseling.
fields.account: On 3 November 2022 at about 5 pm, Madhya Pradesh's state cyber police received an alert emailed by Instagram's US office. It said that a user in the state had suffered a body injury. The Indore cyber-crime unit shared the “self-harm” alert with the cyber headquarters in Bhopal (ANI, 5 November 2022, as well as Times of India, 4 November 2022). The girl, 17, had uploaded two videos. In one, a packet of poison lay beside her as she acted as if drunk. In the other she appeared to cut a vein (ANI). The Times of India notes a small cut on her wrist. Vaibhav Shrivastava, superintendent of police with the state cyber police, said: “After an effort of one hour, we traced the location of the girl”. She was in Satna district, whose police were informed (ANI). Ashutosh Gupta, the Satna superintendent of police, said that officers located her. He said that they called her in with her mother. She said that she only wanted to scare her boyfriend. She was sent home after counseling (Times of India). In January 2026 Decode reported that Meta reviews flagged posts before it alerts police. It reported that Meta publishes no data on false alarms. Decode also interviewed police in Uttar Pradesh. It described a false alarm in Kanpur Dehat. There a student said that she had posted a video with tablets only to gain views.

record.title: Software at Gazi University in Ankara flags a brain tumor while a woman is still in the scanner the day before her biopsy
record.summary: On the hospital network of Gazi University, an algorithm of the Turkish Brain Project alerted physicians to a mass in a woman's brain during her scan. A biopsy the next day confirmed a glioma.
record.account: In October 2022, a 46-year-old woman with a nonspecific headache had brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at Gazi University Faculty of Medicine Hospital, Ankara. An algorithm built within the Turkish Brain Project detected an intraparenchymal mass. It is a region-based convolutional neural network that runs on the hospital network in real time. It alerted the research team while she was still in the scanner. Physicians read the images. They judged the finding consistent with a diffuse glioma. They admitted her. A stereotactic biopsy the next day confirmed a diffuse glioma of the isocitrate dehydrogenase wild type. She was referred to oncology for immediate treatment. The report was published on 8 May 2023. Anadolu Agency reported it on 22 May 2023. Members of the same team at Gazi University published a paper on 10 June 2025. They state that their models later ran in real time at the hospitals of the Gazi, Baskent and Ankara university medical schools. Elsewhere in the paper they say that the system is deployed to two hospitals. They publish no outcome data from that use.
record.purpose: A team at Gazi University built the algorithm in the Turkish Brain Project to detect abnormalities in brain magnetic resonance images as they are taken and to warn physicians at once. The authors say that radiology typically needs days to report a scan and that treatment comes later still. Anadolu Agency reports that the algorithm was trained on cases of stroke, hemorrhage and tumor.

data.retained_case_account: In October 2022, a 46-year-old woman with a nonspecific headache had brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). This was at Gazi University Faculty of Medicine Hospital, Ankara. A region-based convolutional neural network algorithm, built within the Turkish Brain Project and running on the hospital network in real time, detected an intraparenchymal mass. It alerted the research team while she was still in the scanner. Physicians read the images, judged the finding consistent with a diffuse glioma and admitted her. A stereotactic biopsy next day confirmed an isocitrate dehydrogenase wild-type diffuse glioma; she was referred to oncology for immediate treatment. The case was published 8 May 2023 and reported by Anadolu Agency 22 May 2023.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The algorithm detected the mass on the real-time MRI data and raised the alert while the patient was still in the scanner. Physicians then read the images, judged the finding consistent with a diffuse glioma and admitted her. The diagnosis itself came from the pathology report after the stereotactic biopsy. What the AI contributed is detection and speed, not a different diagnosis or treatment. The counterfactual is unproven. The authors say radiology would typically take days to report and that further investigations are needed on the advantages of earlier treatment. They give no evidence of what delay this patient would otherwise have faced. The case is reported by the team that built and deployed the algorithm, and the Anadolu Agency coverage carries that team's account. No independent clinical review is cited.

Neither mentions machine learning. On the ministry's account, the software's contribution was speed: an email address resolved in fractions of a second, and about 20 minutes per shooting participant. record.title: The Palantir-based DAR software identifies the author of an emailed amok threat against Siegen's city administration in fractions of a second. It identifies 51 of about 100 participants in a Duisburg shooting (28 October 2022)
record.summary: North Rhine-Westphalia's interior ministry says that its Palantir software traced an amok threat in Siegen in fractions of a second. The tool identified 51 of about 100 people at a Duisburg shooting.
record.account: In October 2022 someone emailed the city administration of Siegen announcing an amok attack. The threat was over the city's “topless” permission for swimming pools. A shooting in Duisburg-Hamborn between a Turkish-Arab clan and the Hells Angels injured four people. Interior Minister Herbert Reul addressed the Landtag's interior committee on 27 October. He said that DAR, the police's Palantir software, links the weapons register, residents' registration, the police case system and the wanted-persons portal. On 28 October 2022 the Interior Ministry of North Rhine-Westphalia said that DAR was central in several recent cases (WELT and RP Online). The ministry said that the email address revealed the suspect via Palantir in fractions of a second. A Duisburg investigator said that police quickly identified 51 of the roughly 100 participants in the shooting, at about 20 minutes each (RP Online and WELT). Of these, 49 were assigned to rival groups. The ministry puts the 2019–2025 cost at about 39 million euros. The opposition attacks the software on grounds of data protection, with its cost as a second ground (WELT). In October 2022 the civil-rights group Gesellschaft für Freiheitsrechte (GFF) filed a constitutional complaint against the state police law that allowed this data analysis. North Rhine-Westphalia rewrote the legal basis at the end of 2025. In February 2026 the Federal Constitutional Court declined to decide the complaint. It ordered the state to pay the complainants' costs (GFF).
record.purpose: Palantir built the software, and North Rhine-Westphalia procured it as DAR so that its police can search and link entries across police and administrative databases during investigations.

fields.summary: North Rhine-Westphalia's interior ministry says that its Palantir software traced an amok threat in Siegen in fractions of a second. The tool identified 51 of about 100 people at a Duisburg shooting.
fields.account: In October 2022 someone emailed the city administration of Siegen announcing an amok attack. The threat was over the city's “topless” permission for swimming pools. A shooting in Duisburg-Hamborn between a Turkish-Arab clan and the Hells Angels injured four people. Interior Minister Herbert Reul addressed the Landtag's interior committee on 27 October. He said that DAR, the police's Palantir software, links the weapons register, residents' registration, the police case system and the wanted-persons portal. On 28 October 2022 the Interior Ministry of North Rhine-Westphalia said that DAR was central in several recent cases (WELT and RP Online). The ministry said that the email address revealed the suspect via Palantir in fractions of a second. A Duisburg investigator said that police quickly identified 51 of the roughly 100 participants in the shooting, at about 20 minutes each (RP Online and WELT). Of these, 49 were assigned to rival groups. The ministry puts the 2019–2025 cost at about 39 million euros. The opposition attacks the software on grounds of data protection, with its cost as a second ground (WELT). In October 2022 the civil-rights group Gesellschaft für Freiheitsrechte (GFF) filed a constitutional complaint against the state police law that allowed this data analysis. North Rhine-Westphalia rewrote the legal basis at the end of 2025. In February 2026 the Federal Constitutional Court declined to decide the complaint. It ordered the state to pay the complainants' costs (GFF).

Per a prosecutor filing cited by Forbes, it showed nine trips from Massachusetts between October 2020 and August 2021 on known trafficking routes with short stays. record.title: Westchester County police use Rekor's analysis of plate-reader patterns to stop a man in Scarsdale. Officers find crack cocaine. He is convicted
record.summary: Rekor Scout software flagged a man's trips past Westchester County's 480 plate-reader cameras. Officers who stopped him in Scarsdale on 10 March 2022 found crack cocaine. They found a pistol.
record.account: Carscoops reports that the Westchester County Police Department, New York, used technology provided by Rekor. It examined the driving patterns of anyone passing its 480 license-plate-reader cameras over a two-year period. It showed that a man had made several trips along routes typically used by drug traffickers. He had then turned around quickly to go home. According to The Star's AFP Relaxnews item, police took an interest in a vehicle registered to the man in March 2022. On 10 March 2022 the man was driving a gray Chevrolet in Scarsdale. Officers pulled him over. They searched the car. Carscoops reports that they found crack cocaine, cash and a pistol. Forbes reported that the search found 112 grams of crack cocaine, a semiautomatic pistol and $34,000 in cash. On 10 March 2023 the defense filed a motion to suppress the evidence from the location-data searches. The court never decided it. The federal docket shows that the man pleaded guilty on 28 June 2023. Forbes reported the story on 17 July 2023. Carscoops followed on 18 July 2023, drawing on Forbes. Carscoops quotes ACLU lawyer Brett Max Kaufman and defense attorney Ben Gold, who criticized the surveillance. On 24 January 2024 the man received 48 months, with a $34,000 forfeiture. A presidential commutation filed on 17 January 2025 ended his prison term on 16 May 2025. The conviction stands, with three years of supervised release.

fields.account: Carscoops reports that the Westchester County Police Department, New York, used technology provided by Rekor. It examined the driving patterns of anyone passing its 480 license-plate-reader cameras over a two-year period. It showed that a man had made several trips along routes typically used by drug traffickers. He had then turned around quickly to go home. According to The Star's AFP Relaxnews item, police took an interest in a vehicle registered to the man in March 2022. On 10 March 2022 the man was driving a gray Chevrolet in Scarsdale. Officers pulled him over. They searched the car. Carscoops reports that they found crack cocaine, cash and a pistol. Forbes reported that the search found 112 grams of crack cocaine, a semiautomatic pistol and $34,000 in cash. On 10 March 2023 the defense filed a motion to suppress the evidence from the location-data searches. The court never decided it. The federal docket shows that the man pleaded guilty on 28 June 2023. Forbes reported the story on 17 July 2023. Carscoops followed on 18 July 2023, drawing on Forbes. Carscoops quotes ACLU lawyer Brett Max Kaufman and defense attorney Ben Gold, who criticized the surveillance. On 24 January 2024 the man received 48 months, with a $34,000 forfeiture. A presidential commutation filed on 17 January 2025 ended his prison term on 16 May 2025. The conviction stands, with three years of supervised release.

record.title: FATF and APG assessors relay that Bank Negara Malaysia's MSB Customer Anomaly Detection tool flagged two firms whose due diligence proved weak
record.summary: In a report of December 2025, FATF-APG assessors relay that in 2022 Bank Negara Malaysia's anomaly detection tool flagged two money services businesses, where examiners found weak due diligence.
record.account: At the end of 2024, Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) supervised 258 money services businesses (MSBs), most of them money changers. MSBs send BNM their transaction data every month. Each quarter, BNM's MSB Customer Anomaly Detection tool looks for customers with outlier transaction behavior. It combines machine learning models with rule-based parameters. FATF and Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) assessors visited Malaysia from 3 to 21 February 2025. Their mutual evaluation report of December 2025 describes BNM's supervisory technology in a box. According to that box, the tool flagged two MSBs in 2022 for facilitating abnormal customer transactions. On-site examinations then uncovered weaknesses in their ongoing due diligence. The same box gives 292 MSB licensees flagged by BNM's technology solutions from 2020 to 2024. In the main text, the assessors judged that BNM's use of supervisory technology to automate risk ratings had been particularly effective for the MSB sector. The report does not show how the assessors checked the results in the box. It does not show what followed the examinations.
record.purpose: Bank Negara Malaysia built the MSB Customer Anomaly Detection tool to find MSB customers with outlier transaction behavior. Supervisors use its results to focus on the MSBs concerned and to refer suspicions to Malaysia's financial intelligence unit.

fields.summary: In a report of December 2025, FATF-APG assessors relay that in 2022 Bank Negara Malaysia's anomaly detection tool flagged two money services businesses, where examiners found weak due diligence.
fields.account: At the end of 2024, Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) supervised 258 money services businesses (MSBs), most of them money changers. MSBs send BNM their transaction data every month. Each quarter, BNM's MSB Customer Anomaly Detection tool looks for customers with outlier transaction behavior. It combines machine learning models with rule-based parameters. FATF and Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) assessors visited Malaysia from 3 to 21 February 2025. Their mutual evaluation report of December 2025 describes BNM's supervisory technology in a box. According to that box, the tool flagged two MSBs in 2022 for facilitating abnormal customer transactions. On-site examinations then uncovered weaknesses in their ongoing due diligence. The same box gives 292 MSB licensees flagged by BNM's technology solutions from 2020 to 2024. In the main text, the assessors judged that BNM's use of supervisory technology to automate risk ratings had been particularly effective for the MSB sector. The report does not show how the assessors checked the results in the box. It does not show what followed the examinations.

record.title: Kenneth Van Hoesen's Tesla Model 3 straightens its course after he swerves around a wild boar at 4 am on the Kazernelaan in Houthalen-Helchteren. Elon Musk calls the system superhuman (30 May 2020)
record.summary: Kenneth Van Hoesen says that his Tesla Model 3 straightened its course after he swerved around a wild boar in Belgium on 30 May 2020. Reporters credit Tesla's Autopilot.
record.account: Kenneth Van Hoesen, a Flemish baker, was driving his Tesla Model 3 on the Kazernelaan in Houthalen-Helchteren, Belgium, at 4 a.m. on 30 May 2020. A wild boar walked into his path (Daily Star, 9 June 2020). He told Het Laatste Nieuws that he pulled the steering wheel himself. He said that the car then took over. He said that it straightened its course. He felt the wheel working against him (Daily Star and DH.be, 11 June 2020). The Daily Star reports that he had once had a bad crash in a normal car without Autopilot. The Daily Star says that the boar was barely touched, if at all. Electrek reads the footage as a possible strike on the car's side. No injury is reported. TV Limburg (10 June 2020) reports that he posted the video to warn local residents about wildlife crossing the road. Pranay Pathole shared the video on Twitter. The post drew Musk's reply that Autopilot's “prime directive” is not to crash (Electrek, 8 June 2020). He added that its sensors make it “superhuman”. One kind is cameras. Another is sonar. The third is radar. Le Figaro (12 June 2020) credited the swerve to Autopilot. That reading contradicts the driver's own account, in which he steered first. No Tesla data is reported.
record.purpose: Tesla built Autopilot as a driver-assistance system that steers, accelerates and brakes within a lane, with features for avoiding collisions. Keeping the car under control after an evasive swerve fits that use, as the driver and Musk describe it.

record.model_version: Tesla Model 3 per the Daily Star; Autopilot hardware and software version not reported

fields.summary: Kenneth Van Hoesen says that his Tesla Model 3 straightened its course after he swerved around a wild boar in Belgium on 30 May 2020. Reporters credit Tesla's Autopilot.
fields.account: Kenneth Van Hoesen, a Flemish baker, was driving his Tesla Model 3 on the Kazernelaan in Houthalen-Helchteren, Belgium, at 4 a.m. on 30 May 2020. A wild boar walked into his path (Daily Star, 9 June 2020). He told Het Laatste Nieuws that he pulled the steering wheel himself. He said that the car then took over. He said that it straightened its course. He felt the wheel working against him (Daily Star and DH.be, 11 June 2020). The Daily Star reports that he had once had a bad crash in a normal car without Autopilot. The Daily Star says that the boar was barely touched, if at all. Electrek reads the footage as a possible strike on the car's side. No injury is reported. TV Limburg (10 June 2020) reports that he posted the video to warn local residents about wildlife crossing the road. Pranay Pathole shared the video on Twitter. The post drew Musk's reply that Autopilot's “prime directive” is not to crash (Electrek, 8 June 2020). He added that its sensors make it “superhuman”. One kind is cameras. Another is sonar. The third is radar. Le Figaro (12 June 2020) credited the swerve to Autopilot. That reading contradicts the driver's own account, in which he steered first. No Tesla data is reported.

record.summary: Bret Peters's Model S on Autopilot braked while moving right as a wrong-way car came at him on Highway 49 in North Carolina. TeslaCam recorded the near miss.
record.account: Before dawn on 27 February 2020, by the Daily Mail's date, Bret Peters was driving his 2020 Tesla Model S on Autopilot. He is a father. He is a former state trooper. He was on Highway 49 near Cabarrus Arena in Concord, Cabarrus County, North Carolina. A car traveling the wrong way at about 60 miles per hour came toward him in his lane. He wrote on Facebook that he did not see it until after Autopilot hit the brakes and started steering away. In the TeslaCam footage, the Tesla moves into the right lane while the oncoming car swerves onto the grassy median. There was no collision. FOX 46 Charlotte first reported the near miss on 5 March 2020 from its own interview with Peters. It aired his footage. He told the station that he drives the route for an hour each way twice a day. The station places the drive early on a Friday, a day later than the Daily Mail's 27 February. On 8 March 2020 CleanTechnica relayed a since-deleted Reddit post and the station's report. On 9 March 2020 Electrek and the Daily Mail described the footage. No statement from the police or Tesla has been reported.

data.retained_case_account: Before dawn on 27 February 2020, Bret Peters, a father and former state trooper, was driving his 2020 Tesla Model S on Autopilot. He was on Highway 49 near Cabarrus Arena in Concord, Cabarrus County, North Carolina. A car traveling the wrong way at about 60 mph came toward him in his lane. He wrote on Facebook that he did not see it until after Autopilot hit the brakes and started steering away. TeslaCam footage, aired by Fox 46 Charlotte and described by Electrek and the Daily Mail, shows the Tesla moving into the right lane. The oncoming car swerves onto the grassy median. There was no collision, and no police or Tesla statement is reported.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: By Peters's account Autopilot braked and began a lane change to the right before he had seen the oncoming car. The TeslaCam footage, as described by Electrek and the Daily Mail, shows the Tesla moving right while the wrong-way car veers off-road. The claim rests on the driver's statements and the footage. Neither Tesla nor police is quoted, and the oncoming driver's own swerve means the system's action cannot be shown to have been decisive.

record.title: TCU auditors identify overlapping tenders for maintenance of BR-153 after an email from Alice
record.summary: Alice, the federal audit court's robot that reads tenders, emailed tender details to auditors. They found road-maintenance notices that overlapped a concession. The court ordered them annulled.
record.account: Alice (Análise de Licitações e Editais) is the Tribunal de Contas da União's robot. It reads every tender notice published on Comprasnet and the Diário Oficial da União. It reads every auction record published there. It had been running for about ten months when the Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) presented it on 25–26 September 2017. The occasion was a joint data-analysis seminar of the TCU and the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU). Inforchannel (27 September 2017), quoting TCU auditor Valéria Nakano, reported that in Goiás the court, via Alice, found that DNIT's state unit had published two notices. They were worth R$39 million for maintenance of the BR-153 on stretches under concession, where maintenance falls to the concessionaire. Within two months an acórdão blocked both tenders. In an article of 22 November 2017, JOTA states that Alice was decisive in Acórdão-TCU 1.116/2017 (rapporteur Minister Walton Alencar Rodrigues). It ordered cancellation of the BR-153 tender budgeted at R$20 million. Inforchannel and JOTA give different numbers of notices, with different amounts. The complete acórdão is not public on the court's site. Its date has not been reported. The author of a firsthand report on a July 2018 visit to TCU states that Alice's email contained no irregularity alert. The author adds that auditors identified the concession overlap after receiving the information. The report reproduces the order to annul notices 88/2017 and 102/2017. The author puts their combined value at R$39 million. The operative part of Acórdão 1.116/2017-Plenário, reproduced in the visit report, gave DNIT's Goiás and Federal District unit fifteen days to annul pregões 88/2017-12 and 102/2017-12. Fernanda Odilla (Crime, Law and Social Change, 2023) reports, citing an interviewee, that TCU added a random forest classifier to the rules that CGU first wrote for Alice. Odilla lists alert overflow among the main weaknesses of the procurement tools that include Alice. False positives are on the same list.
record.purpose: Brazil's federal audit court and comptroller general built Alice to screen federal tender notices daily for signs of irregularity. Auditors can then act during the public phase of a tender.

The outcome is material to DNIT and TCU. Inforchannel and JOTA report that an acórdão blocked or canceled the tenders, and the July 2018 visit report reproduces the order to annul notices 88/2017 and 102/2017. Inforchannel gives R$39 million for two notices, and JOTA gives R$20 million for one.
This is a single highway tender among some 60,000 federal tenders a year, small at national scale.

ai_role.statement: Alice delivered tender information to auditors. The author of a firsthand visit report states that Alice's email contained no irregularity alert for this case. fields.account: Alice (Análise de Licitações e Editais) is the Tribunal de Contas da União's robot. It reads every tender notice published on Comprasnet and the Diário Oficial da União. It reads every auction record published there. It had been running for about ten months when the Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) presented it on 25–26 September 2017. The occasion was a joint data-analysis seminar of the TCU and the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU). Inforchannel (27 September 2017), quoting TCU auditor Valéria Nakano, reported that in Goiás the court, via Alice, found that DNIT's state unit had published two notices. They were worth R$39 million for maintenance of the BR-153 on stretches under concession, where maintenance falls to the concessionaire. Within two months an acórdão blocked both tenders. In an article of 22 November 2017, JOTA states that Alice was decisive in Acórdão-TCU 1.116/2017 (rapporteur Minister Walton Alencar Rodrigues). It ordered cancellation of the BR-153 tender budgeted at R$20 million. Inforchannel and JOTA give different numbers of notices, with different amounts. The complete acórdão is not public on the court's site. Its date has not been reported. The author of a firsthand report on a July 2018 visit to TCU states that Alice's email contained no irregularity alert. The author adds that auditors identified the concession overlap after receiving the information. The report reproduces the order to annul notices 88/2017 and 102/2017. The author puts their combined value at R$39 million. The operative part of Acórdão 1.116/2017-Plenário, reproduced in the visit report, gave DNIT's Goiás and Federal District unit fifteen days to annul pregões 88/2017-12 and 102/2017-12. Fernanda Odilla (Crime, Law and Social Change, 2023) reports, citing an interviewee, that TCU added a random forest classifier to the rules that CGU first wrote for Alice. Odilla lists alert overflow among the main weaknesses of the procurement tools that include Alice. False positives are on the same list.

fields.summary: Alice, the federal audit court's robot that reads tenders, emailed tender details to auditors. They found road-maintenance notices that overlapped a concession. The court ordered them annulled.
fields.account: Alice (Análise de Licitações e Editais) is the Tribunal de Contas da União's robot. It reads every tender notice published on Comprasnet and the Diário Oficial da União. It reads every auction record published there. It had been running for about ten months when the Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) presented it on 25–26 September 2017. The occasion was a joint data-analysis seminar of the TCU and the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU). Inforchannel (27 September 2017), quoting TCU auditor Valéria Nakano, reported that in Goiás the court, via Alice, found that DNIT's state unit had published two notices. They were worth R$39 million for maintenance of the BR-153 on stretches under concession, where maintenance falls to the concessionaire. Within two months an acórdão blocked both tenders. In an article of 22 November 2017, JOTA states that Alice was decisive in Acórdão-TCU 1.116/2017 (rapporteur Minister Walton Alencar Rodrigues). It ordered cancellation of the BR-153 tender budgeted at R$20 million. Inforchannel and JOTA give different numbers of notices, with different amounts. The complete acórdão is not public on the court's site. Its date has not been reported. The author of a firsthand report on a July 2018 visit to TCU states that Alice's email contained no irregularity alert. The author adds that auditors identified the concession overlap after receiving the information. The report reproduces the order to annul notices 88/2017 and 102/2017. The author puts their combined value at R$39 million. The operative part of Acórdão 1.116/2017-Plenário, reproduced in the visit report, gave DNIT's Goiás and Federal District unit fifteen days to annul pregões 88/2017-12 and 102/2017-12. Fernanda Odilla (Crime, Law and Social Change, 2023) reports, citing an interviewee, that TCU added a random forest classifier to the rules that CGU first wrote for Alice. Odilla lists alert overflow among the main weaknesses of the procurement tools that include Alice. False positives are on the same list.

record.title: Bank F's tool for network analytics links a third company to a suspected network for trade-based money laundering in Hong Kong
record.summary: Bank F's unnamed tool for network analytics linked a third company to a suspected money laundering network through shared phone numbers.
record.account: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's report “AML/CFT Regtech: Case Studies and Insights” presents anonymized case studies of banks. It appeared in January 2021, with a press release on 21 January 2021. The authors describe Bank F as a subsidiary and regional head office of a large global bank in Asia-Pacific. They state that before the tool, manual reviews of documentation for signatories were the only means to make such connections. Bank F implemented a network (graph) analytics solution in Hong Kong in 2013. The solution identifies high-risk customers from the data. It identifies high-risk transactions. The data cover wholesale clients. They cover correspondent banking. They cover trade. They cover payments. They cover external registries. In an example from 2015, a relationship manager gathered intelligence about trade-based money laundering related to a drug cartel in one account. The manager linked it to a second account through the customer relationship management tool. The network tool then found more companies linked to the first two parties through shared phone numbers. It used shared email addresses. Reviews of the accounts of Companies A, B and C revealed potential money laundering concerns. The authors give no day for the example of 2015. They state that by 2016 Bank F covered its top 20 commercial banking sites and about 80% of its trade lending book. They say that the tool has led to the review of around 100 customer relationships holding around USD 500 million in clean or unsecured exposures. For their figure of USD 50 million, they assume that 10% of those exposures would otherwise be unrecoverable. They document no realized savings of USD 50 million. They add that by January 2021 a successor tool, built with an outside vendor, was in production in several jurisdictions. It drew on a data lake of over 40 billion rows. In the foreword, the authority adds that such techniques are already neutralizing networks of mule accounts linked to face mask scams.

fields.summary: Bank F's unnamed tool for network analytics linked a third company to a suspected money laundering network through shared phone numbers.
fields.account: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's report “AML/CFT Regtech: Case Studies and Insights” presents anonymized case studies of banks. It appeared in January 2021, with a press release on 21 January 2021. The authors describe Bank F as a subsidiary and regional head office of a large global bank in Asia-Pacific. They state that before the tool, manual reviews of documentation for signatories were the only means to make such connections. Bank F implemented a network (graph) analytics solution in Hong Kong in 2013. The solution identifies high-risk customers from the data. It identifies high-risk transactions. The data cover wholesale clients. They cover correspondent banking. They cover trade. They cover payments. They cover external registries. In an example from 2015, a relationship manager gathered intelligence about trade-based money laundering related to a drug cartel in one account. The manager linked it to a second account through the customer relationship management tool. The network tool then found more companies linked to the first two parties through shared phone numbers. It used shared email addresses. Reviews of the accounts of Companies A, B and C revealed potential money laundering concerns. The authors give no day for the example of 2015. They state that by 2016 Bank F covered its top 20 commercial banking sites and about 80% of its trade lending book. They say that the tool has led to the review of around 100 customer relationships holding around USD 500 million in clean or unsecured exposures. For their figure of USD 50 million, they assume that 10% of those exposures would otherwise be unrecoverable. They document no realized savings of USD 50 million. They add that by January 2021 a successor tool, built with an outside vendor, was in production in several jurisdictions. It drew on a data lake of over 40 billion rows. In the foreword, the authority adds that such techniques are already neutralizing networks of mule accounts linked to face mask scams.

details.value: In the arrest report, the detective writes that the platform “utilizes safety and security measures designed to monitor for key phrases and potentially threatening content”. The detective writes that the messages were “escalated to a human review team”. So an automated layer surfaced the two messages, and people judged their severity and made the referral. Anthropic has not said whether the flag came from a classifier or a keyword rule. Straight Arrow News, citing court records, says that the review team escalated to the FBI, which notified the sheriff's office. Lee County deputies and Intelligence Detective Thomas Alejo identified the user, visited her home, interviewed her under Miranda and decided on the charge. In the arrest report, the platform is called “Anthropic Artificial Intelligence”. Reporters name Claude, and according to court records the user told the detective that she used Perplexity.

record.title: After Anthropic's threat monitoring flags a Bonita Springs woman's messages about shooting up the Lee County Sheriff's Office, human reviewers tip police, who detain her without incident
record.summary: Anthropic's safety monitoring flagged a chat user's threat to shoot up a Florida sheriff's office. After human review, the tip led deputies to detain her. No weapon was seized.
record.account: A user of Anthropic's AI chat service wrote at about 05:10 on 26 September 2026. She said that she was going to “shoot up” the Lee County Sheriff's Office in Florida. At 01:07 on 27 September she wrote that she had got a new gun. Anthropic's safety monitoring picked out the messages. Because of their severity a human review team reported them to law enforcement. Straight Arrow News, citing court records, reported that the review team escalated to the FBI, which notified the sheriff's office. The sheriff's office logged the tip on 29 September. It identified the user as a 30-year-old woman from Bonita Springs. Deputies detained her at home without incident at 00:51 on 30 September. A detective charged her under Florida Statute 836.10, written threats of violence. No weapon was seized. She described the AI as a personal diary. In the arrest report, the platform is called “Anthropic Artificial Intelligence”. Press reports name Claude. Court records note that the user told the detective that she used Perplexity. The arrest form set a $10,000 bond and a 20 October 2026 appearance date. The woman pleaded not guilty. Her arraignment was set for 2 November 2026, while prosecutors had not yet filed a formal charge. The First Amendment scholar Eugene Volokh doubts that the charge will hold.
record.purpose: In its consumer terms (effective 8 October 2025), Anthropic reserves the right “at our sole discretion” to report Inputs to law enforcement. Its privacy policy (effective 10 September 2026) allows disclosure that the company believes “reasonably necessary” to “prevent serious harm to any person or to property”. In the arrest report, the platform's safety measures are described as “designed to monitor for key phrases and potentially threatening content”. Of a referral in August 2026, Anthropic said: “This is our safeguards process working as intended”.

data.retained_case_account: A user of Anthropic's AI chat service wrote at about 05:10 on 26 September 2026. She said she was going to “shoot up” the Lee County Sheriff's Office in Florida. At 01:07 on 27 September she wrote that she had got a new gun. Anthropic's safety monitoring flagged the messages, and because of their severity a human review team reported them to law enforcement. The sheriff's office logged the tip on 29 September and identified the user as a 30-year-old woman from Bonita Springs. Deputies detained her at home without incident at 00:51 on 30 September. A detective charged her under Florida Statute 836.10, written threats of violence. No weapon was seized, and she described the AI as a personal diary.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The arrest report says the platform “utilizes safety and security measures designed to monitor for key phrases and potentially threatening content”. It says the messages were “escalated to a human review team”. An automated layer therefore surfaced the two messages, and people judged their severity and made the referral. The sources do not say whether the flag came from a classifier or a keyword rule. Straight Arrow News, citing court records, says the review team escalated to the FBI, which notified the sheriff's office. Identifying the user, the home visit, the Miranda interview and the charging decision were the work of Lee County deputies and Intelligence Detective Thomas Alejo. The arrest report calls the platform “Anthropic Artificial Intelligence”. Press reports name Claude, and court records note the user told the detective she used Perplexity.

details.value: The passenger's phone detected the impact and called the fire service on its own at 11:04, from near the Nakadake crater. That was about 46 minutes before the operator reported the helicopter missing. A police helicopter then found the wreck in the crater that afternoon. The helicopter's own GPS track also ended near the crater, so the sources do not show that the phone's location guided the find. No one was rescued alive.

record.title: A passenger's iPhone Crash Detection sends a “strong impact” alert to the local fire service before a sightseeing helicopter near Mount Aso goes missing, 20 January 2026
record.summary: Apple Crash Detection on a passenger's iPhone called the fire service about 46 minutes before the operator reported a sightseeing helicopter missing near Mount Aso. All three aboard died.
record.account: On 20 January 2026 a sightseeing helicopter operated by Takumi Aviation of Okayama took off from Aso Cadre Dominion at 10:52 Japan time and lost contact at 11:04. It carried a pilot in his sixties and two Taiwanese passengers (a 41-year-old man and a 36-year-old woman). Police told Jiji Press that the automatic call reached the fire service at 11:04 on 20 January 2026. They said that the operator's agent reported the helicopter missing at about 11:50. The Asahi Shimbun cited the fire service as saying that the call came from near the Nakadake crater. Jiji reported that the helicopter's GPS track also ended near the crater. Storm Media Japan, drawing on fire-service information, wrote that the phone function gave the search its first important lead. That afternoon a police helicopter found an object believed to be the helicopter around the first crater of Mount Aso's Nakadake. On 21 January 2026 Taiwan's SETN, citing Japanese media, reported that the local fire department had received a “strong impact” notification from a passenger's phone. It came before contact was lost. The notification apparently came from the iPhone Crash Detection feature. Callbacks to the phone failed. SETN does not cite a named Japanese agency. It quotes a firefighter on crash detection in general. It quotes a nurse. On 18 February 2026 the fire department said that bodies believed to be those of the three occupants had been found inside the crater. Apple's feature, on iPhone 14 and later, uses motion sensors with an algorithm on the device. It calls emergency services after a countdown if the user does not respond. The device alerted responders to an aviation crash that it did not prevent.

ai_role.statement: The passenger's phone detected the impact and called the fire service on its own at 11:04, from near the Nakadake crater. That was about 46 minutes before the operator reported the helicopter missing. A police helicopter then found the wreck in the crater that afternoon. The helicopter's own GPS track also ended near the crater, so the sources do not show that the phone's location guided the find. No one was rescued alive.

Jiji Press reports police information on the times of the automatic call and of the operator's report, and the Asahi Shimbun and Storm Media Japan cite the fire service. The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: Apple Crash Detection on a passenger's iPhone called the fire service about 46 minutes before the operator reported a sightseeing helicopter missing near Mount Aso. All three aboard died.
fields.account: On 20 January 2026 a sightseeing helicopter operated by Takumi Aviation of Okayama took off from Aso Cadre Dominion at 10:52 Japan time and lost contact at 11:04. It carried a pilot in his sixties and two Taiwanese passengers (a 41-year-old man and a 36-year-old woman). Police told Jiji Press that the automatic call reached the fire service at 11:04 on 20 January 2026. They said that the operator's agent reported the helicopter missing at about 11:50. The Asahi Shimbun cited the fire service as saying that the call came from near the Nakadake crater. Jiji reported that the helicopter's GPS track also ended near the crater. Storm Media Japan, drawing on fire-service information, wrote that the phone function gave the search its first important lead. That afternoon a police helicopter found an object believed to be the helicopter around the first crater of Mount Aso's Nakadake. On 21 January 2026 Taiwan's SETN, citing Japanese media, reported that the local fire department had received a “strong impact” notification from a passenger's phone. It came before contact was lost. The notification apparently came from the iPhone Crash Detection feature. Callbacks to the phone failed. SETN does not cite a named Japanese agency. It quotes a firefighter on crash detection in general. It quotes a nurse. On 18 February 2026 the fire department said that bodies believed to be those of the three occupants had been found inside the crater. Apple's feature, on iPhone 14 and later, uses motion sensors with an algorithm on the device. It calls emergency services after a countdown if the user does not respond. The device alerted responders to an aviation crash that it did not prevent.

record.title: Hanoi traffic police trace a missing 78-year-old on the city's new AI cameras before a passer-by finds him hypoglycemic at 3 a.m. in Dịch Vọng
record.summary: Hanoi police traced a lost 78-year-old on AI traffic cameras on 15 December 2025. A passer-by who found him at 3 a.m. the next day took him home.
record.account: Hanoi's AI traffic-camera network began official operation on 13 December 2025. A 78-year-old man from Thanh Xuân ward, Hanoi, went out to exercise at 3:30 p.m. on 15 December 2025. He did not return. At 8:15 p.m. his family reported him to Thanh Xuân Ward Police. Ward officers worked with the Hanoi Traffic Police Department. Major Nguyễn Tá Khanh's team there searched the AI traffic-camera system in the direction that the family gave. It traced him along Nguyễn Tuân street toward Thanh Xuân Park and other streets. VietNamNet and Tiền Phong say that the images were posted on social media. At about 3 a.m. on 16 December a passing resident found him in Dịch Vọng. He was hypoglycemic. He was close to fainting. The resident took him home. The police have not linked the finder to the camera trace. They have not linked him to the appeal on social media. Sức khỏe & Đời sống reports that the family said that his health was stable. It reports that they sent thanks to the police and residents. By 29 June 2026 Hanoi had nearly 5,000 AI cameras.
record.purpose: Hanoi's Traffic Police run the AI traffic-camera system, in VOV's words, “to ensure security and order and support the people” as well as to manage traffic. VOV reported that it has 1,837 cameras with signals controlled by AI and was due to enter official operation in December 2025. Tracing a lost resident for a search by the ward police falls within that remit.

data.retained_case_account: A 78-year-old man from Thanh Xuân ward, Hanoi, went out to exercise at 3:30 p.m. on 15 December 2025 and did not return. At 8:15 p.m. his family reported him to Thanh Xuân Ward Police. Ward officers worked with the Hanoi Traffic Police Department. Major Nguyễn Tá Khanh's team there searched the AI traffic-camera system in the direction the family gave. It traced him along Nguyễn Tuân street toward Thanh Xuân Park and other streets. VietNamNet and Tiền Phong say the images were posted on social media. At about 3 a.m. on 16 December a passing resident found him in Dịch Vọng, hypoglycemic and close to fainting, and took him home. No source links the finder to the appeal.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The system's contribution was the trace. Police searched it in the direction the family gave. It returned images of the man walking along Nguyễn Tuân street toward Thanh Xuân Park and across other streets. That gave the police a route and pictures for a public appeal. A passing resident found him in Dịch Vọng about six hours and 45 minutes after the report. No source says the finder had seen the appeal or that officers reached him. So the discovery itself is not attributable to the system. The vendor is not named and every account comes from the police.

fields.title: Hanoi traffic police trace a missing 78-year-old on the city's new AI cameras before a passer-by finds him hypoglycemic at 3 a.m. in Dịch Vọng
fields.headline: Hanoi traffic police trace a lost 78-year-old on AI cameras

fields.account: Hanoi's AI traffic-camera network began official operation on 13 December 2025. A 78-year-old man from Thanh Xuân ward, Hanoi, went out to exercise at 3:30 p.m. on 15 December 2025. He did not return. At 8:15 p.m. his family reported him to Thanh Xuân Ward Police. Ward officers worked with the Hanoi Traffic Police Department. Major Nguyễn Tá Khanh's team there searched the AI traffic-camera system in the direction that the family gave. It traced him along Nguyễn Tuân street toward Thanh Xuân Park and other streets. VietNamNet and Tiền Phong say that the images were posted on social media. At about 3 a.m. on 16 December a passing resident found him in Dịch Vọng. He was hypoglycemic. He was close to fainting. The resident took him home. The police have not linked the finder to the camera trace. They have not linked him to the appeal on social media. Sức khỏe & Đời sống reports that the family said that his health was stable. It reports that they sent thanks to the police and residents. By 29 June 2026 Hanoi had nearly 5,000 AI cameras.

produced_by: A dense AI camera network along the route the person walked, here 1,837 cameras across Hanoi, with footage searchable by appearance and direction of travel.
A family report the same evening giving a starting point and a direction for the camera search.
A ward police unit able to hand the search to the Traffic Police's camera-control team the same night.
must_hold: The missing person stays within camera coverage. Here the trace ended at a route, not at the man, and a passer-by made the find.
Someone acts on the trace or the appeal. The sources do not establish that link in this case.
The vendor and the matching method are undisclosed, so the trace cannot be checked beyond the police account.

record.title: On ChatGPT's advice, a woman from Wolfforth, Texas, goes with a week-old spider bite to an emergency room whose staff say that she should be there
record.summary: On ChatGPT's advice, a woman from Wolfforth, Texas, went to the emergency room with a worsening spider bite. She says that staff there told her that the skin tissue had begun to die.
record.account: A woman from Wolfforth, Texas, posts videos on TikTok. She said that a spider had bitten her “a little over a week ago”. The bite was getting worse. She had vomited for days. She could not keep water down. She woke with a numb arm. She asked ChatGPT whether she should go to the emergency room. It answered that her symptoms were “a ton of red flags”. It said that she should go immediately. At the emergency room, she said, staff told her “Yeah, you should be here”. They said that the skin tissue was dying or dead. Her video, recorded at the emergency room, was posted on 27 August 2025. The Express and the Daily Star retold it on 2 September 2025. The Hindustan Times and The Economic Times retold it on 3 September 2025. The hospital was not reported. The diagnosis was not reported. The treatment was not reported. No clinician has made a public statement. Researchers at the University of Oxford and other institutions published a randomized study in Nature Medicine on 9 February 2026. Members of the public used GPT-4o. Others used two other chatbots. They chose the right level of care no more often than people who used their usual sources. The study does not concern this woman.
record.purpose: OpenAI built ChatGPT to answer users' questions in conversation, and here the question was whether to go to the emergency room. OpenAI told the Mirror that its services “are not intended for use in the diagnosis or treatment of any health condition”, and The Economic Times quoted it. Its answer was advice on where to seek care, with no diagnosis.

fields.summary: On ChatGPT's advice, a woman from Wolfforth, Texas, went to the emergency room with a worsening spider bite. She says that staff there told her that the skin tissue had begun to die.
fields.account: A woman from Wolfforth, Texas, posts videos on TikTok. She said that a spider had bitten her “a little over a week ago”. The bite was getting worse. She had vomited for days. She could not keep water down. She woke with a numb arm. She asked ChatGPT whether she should go to the emergency room. It answered that her symptoms were “a ton of red flags”. It said that she should go immediately. At the emergency room, she said, staff told her “Yeah, you should be here”. They said that the skin tissue was dying or dead. Her video, recorded at the emergency room, was posted on 27 August 2025. The Express and the Daily Star retold it on 2 September 2025. The Hindustan Times and The Economic Times retold it on 3 September 2025. The hospital was not reported. The diagnosis was not reported. The treatment was not reported. No clinician has made a public statement. Researchers at the University of Oxford and other institutions published a randomized study in Nature Medicine on 9 February 2026. Members of the public used GPT-4o. Others used two other chatbots. They chose the right level of care no more often than people who used their usual sources. The study does not concern this woman.

value.text: The chatbot recommended escalation. The woman chose to attend the ER, where clinicians examined her.

display.answer: The chatbot recommended escalation. The woman chose to attend the ER, where clinicians examined her.

record.title: Karadeniz Technical University students' AI early-warning app alerts their phones about 30 seconds before a Kulu quake is felt at the Turkish parliament, 15 May 2025
record.summary: Erken Uyarı Merkezi, an AI-based app built by Karadeniz Technical University students, alerted their phones about 30 seconds before a quake was felt at Turkey's parliament.
record.account: On 15 May 2025 software-engineering students from Karadeniz Technical University were presenting their Erken Uyarı Merkezi (Early Warning Center) to members of parliament. The news agency DHA describes it as an AI-based system that warns of earthquakes early. The presentation took place in the Public Relations building of the Turkish parliament (TBMM) in Ankara. During it, a quake centered in Kulu, Konya, was felt in the capital. DHA gave the magnitude as 5.2. The U.S. Geological Survey recorded M5.0 at 15:46 local time (12:46:37 UTC), 14 km east-north-east of Kulu at 10 km depth. Student Birkan Yılmaz said that notifications had reached their phones 30 seconds before the quake. Students went outside. Some members of parliament went outside. Building staff went outside. None of the cited reports mentions damage or injuries.
record.purpose: Students at Karadeniz Technical University built the system to warn phones of an earthquake before the shaking arrives. The alert came during the team's own presentation to members of parliament, before the Kulu quake was felt.

fields.account: On 15 May 2025 software-engineering students from Karadeniz Technical University were presenting their Erken Uyarı Merkezi (Early Warning Center) to members of parliament. The news agency DHA describes it as an AI-based system that warns of earthquakes early. The presentation took place in the Public Relations building of the Turkish parliament (TBMM) in Ankara. During it, a quake centered in Kulu, Konya, was felt in the capital. DHA gave the magnitude as 5.2. The U.S. Geological Survey recorded M5.0 at 15:46 local time (12:46:37 UTC), 14 km east-north-east of Kulu at 10 km depth. Student Birkan Yılmaz said that notifications had reached their phones 30 seconds before the quake. Students went outside. Some members of parliament went outside. Building staff went outside. None of the cited reports mentions damage or injuries.

value.text: The benefit was a single warning on 15 May 2025. No later report on the system was found, and the team's planned meetings with ministers have no reported outcome.

record.title: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System reached phones in Crete and the Dodecanese seconds before a magnitude 6.0 quake near Kasos on 14 May 2025
record.summary: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System sent Android users in Crete and the Dodecanese a warning seconds before a magnitude 6.0 quake near Kasos on 14 May 2025.
record.account: Google switched on its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Greece on 28 April 2021. In Europe the system detects quakes with the accelerometers in phones and uses no seismographs. On 23 April 2025 the magnitude 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake struck Türkiye. Google's team reports that the system detected it 5.31 seconds after it began. They report that it alerted more than 16 million users. Three weeks later, at 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May), an earthquake struck between Kasos and Karpathos. The U.S. Geological Survey put its magnitude at 6.0. Greek reporters put it at 6.1. It was centered 20 km south-south-east of Fry on Kasos, at 76 km depth. The U.S. Geological Survey logged 931 felt reports and a green alert level. On 14 and 15 May Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress reported that the system notified users in Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away seconds before the shaking. Notice came by message with an audible signal similar to the 112 alert. None of the reports names a recipient. None gives a lead time in seconds. None mentions damage or injuries. On 15 October 2026 Google extended the service to more than 200 regions.
record.purpose: Google built the system to detect earthquakes with the accelerometers of Android phones, combining their signals on its servers. It alerts users where shaking is expected, ahead of the slower seismic waves, for quakes of magnitude 4.5 and above.

data.retained_case_account: At 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May) a magnitude 6.0 (USGS; Greek outlets 6.1) earthquake struck. It struck 20 km south-south-east of Fry on Kasos, between Kasos and Karpathos, at 76 km depth. USGS logged 931 felt reports and a green alert level. Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress reported on 14 and 15 May on Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System. In Europe it detects quakes from phone accelerometers rather than seismographs. It notified users in Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away seconds before the shaking. Notice came by message and an audible signal similar to the 112 alert. None of the reports names a recipient, gives a lead time in seconds, or mentions damage or injuries.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: If the reports are right, the alert was produced end to end by Google's system. Accelerometer triggers from many phones were combined on Google's servers to detect the quake. Alerts were then pushed ahead of the slower waves, as Google's 2020 description and the 2025 Science paper set out. Google's own pages do not use the words AI or machine learning. The Science abstract speaks of smartphone-based earthquake detection algorithms. That alerts arrived seconds before shaking rests on unattributed statements in four Greek outlets published within a day of the quake. None quotes a recipient, a seismologist or Google. No Google per-event confirmation was found.

fields.account: Google switched on its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Greece on 28 April 2021. In Europe the system detects quakes with the accelerometers in phones and uses no seismographs. On 23 April 2025 the magnitude 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake struck Türkiye. Google's team reports that the system detected it 5.31 seconds after it began. They report that it alerted more than 16 million users. Three weeks later, at 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May), an earthquake struck between Kasos and Karpathos. The U.S. Geological Survey put its magnitude at 6.0. Greek reporters put it at 6.1. It was centered 20 km south-south-east of Fry on Kasos, at 76 km depth. The U.S. Geological Survey logged 931 felt reports and a green alert level. On 14 and 15 May Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress reported that the system notified users in Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away seconds before the shaking. Notice came by message with an audible signal similar to the 112 alert. None of the reports names a recipient. None gives a lead time in seconds. None mentions damage or injuries. On 15 October 2026 Google extended the service to more than 200 regions.

display.answer: Observed 14 May 2025. The quake struck at 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May, per USGS), and the alerts went out seconds before the shaking. In.gr, writing on Thursday 15 May, places the quake in the early hours of Wednesday.

produced_by: A magnitude 6.0 (USGS) quake above the system's 4.5 alert threshold, centered offshore south of Kasos at about 76 km depth. A push alert could therefore outrun the slower waves to Crete and the Dodecanese.

The phone must have the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled (Alphafreepress: Settings > Safety & Emergency > Earthquake Alerts). The feature must be supported in the region.
