Google's pages, the Science paper and the study of the Marmara Ereğlisi quake come from Google's team. The U.S. Geological Survey confirms the quake on its event page.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System sent Android users in Crete and the Dodecanese a warning seconds before a magnitude 6.0 quake near Kasos on 14 May 2025.
fields.account: Google switched on its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Greece on 28 April 2021. In Europe the system detects quakes with the accelerometers in phones and uses no seismographs. On 23 April 2025 the magnitude 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake struck Türkiye. Google's team reports that the system detected it 5.31 seconds after it began. They report that it alerted more than 16 million users. Three weeks later, at 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May), an earthquake struck between Kasos and Karpathos. The U.S. Geological Survey put its magnitude at 6.0. Greek reporters put it at 6.1. It was centered 20 km south-south-east of Fry on Kasos, at 76 km depth. The U.S. Geological Survey logged 931 felt reports and a green alert level. On 14 and 15 May Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress reported that the system notified users in Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away seconds before the shaking. Notice came by message with an audible signal similar to the 112 alert. None of the reports names a recipient. None gives a lead time in seconds. None mentions damage or injuries. On 15 October 2026 Google extended the service to more than 200 regions.

produced_by: A magnitude 6.0 (USGS) quake above the system's 4.5 alert threshold, centered offshore south of Kasos at about 76 km depth. A push alert could therefore outrun the slower waves to Crete and the Dodecanese.

Enough Android phones near the epicentre with the Earthquake Alerts setting on to trigger Google's server-side detection. In Europe the system uses the accelerometers in phones instead of seismographs (in.gr).
Receiving phones with location (GPS) enabled and an internet connection, which Alphafreepress lists as requirements for the alerts
must_hold: The server's magnitude and location estimate must be right and early. The 2025 Science paper reports that only 36% of alert recipients got the alert before shaking.
Recipients must know what to do with seconds of notice. The Greek reports document no protective action by anyone who received the alert.
The phone must have the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled (Alphafreepress: Settings > Safety & Emergency > Earthquake Alerts). The feature must be supported in the region.

record.title: Dudhwa Tiger Reserve officials identify armed poachers from images that a TrailGuard AI camera in Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary transmits on two dates
record.summary: A TrailGuard AI camera in Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary sent officials images of armed poachers on two dates in 2022. Officials identified them. Its makers later claimed arrests.
record.account: Dertien, Negi, Dinerstein and colleagues (BioScience 73(10):748–757, published online 14 September 2023) report deploying the TrailGuard AI camera-alert system. The system “runs on-the-edge artificial intelligence algorithms to detect tigers and poachers and transmit real-time images”. It was deployed in the Kanha-Pench corridor and in Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh. The authors state that the seven Dudhwa units ran from early September 2022 to mid-December 2022. All seven transmitted images. Three sent objects of interest to forest department officials. “One unit within Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary captured a group of poachers carrying a gun and knives on two separate dates, and a presumably poached chital (Axis axis) on the second detection”. The authors do not give the dates of the detections, so the two detections of poachers can be placed only within the deployment period. Tigers were detected at the same spot three days before the second poacher detection. “Authorities were able to quickly identify the individuals via the transmitted images and were investigating the matter”. The authors include RESOLVE and CVEDIA staff (the system's developers) alongside Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Wildlife Institute of India and Global Tiger Forum co-authors. A Clemson University release of 15 September 2023 carries Nightjar and RESOLVE boilerplate. In the release, Clemson University states that the alerts “led the authorities to the arrest of these individuals for poaching a few weeks later”. Clemson quotes Sanjay Kumar Pathak, former field director of Dudhwa, as saying that the system “led to the detection and arrest of poachers in Dudhwa”. The Hindu (16 September 2023) cited a person involved in the experiment as saying that poachers caught on camera had helped forest authorities secure a conviction a year later. It quoted Piyush Yadav of Nightjar, the manufacturer: “A year down, these poachers were arrested with images from TrailGuard playing a key role”. The article's lead puts the capture in Kanha-Pench. It puts the Yadav quote in Dudhwa. Agence France-Presse (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the authors' claim of “identifying a team of poachers”. It names no reserve. It does not name a case. No statement from the forest department about an arrest was found. No court record of one was found.

data.retained_case_account: Dertien, Negi, Dinerstein and colleagues (BioScience 73(10):748–757, published online 14 September 2023) report deploying the TrailGuard AI camera-alert system. The paper does not date the detections. The system “runs on-the-edge artificial intelligence algorithms to detect tigers and poachers and transmit real-time images”. It was deployed in the Kanha-Pench corridor and in Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh. All seven Dudhwa units transmitted images; three transmitted objects of interest to forest department officials. “One unit within Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary captured a group of poachers carrying a gun and knives on two separate dates, and a presumably poached chital (Axis axis) on the second detection”. “Authorities were able to quickly identify the individuals via the transmitted images and were investigating the matter”. Tigers were detected at the same spot three days before the second poacher detection. The authors include RESOLVE and CVEDIA staff (the system's developers) alongside Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Wildlife Institute of India and Global Tiger Forum co-authors. AFP (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the study's claim of “identifying a team of poachers”. A Clemson University release of 15 September 2023 carries Nightjar/RESOLVE boilerplate. It states that the alerts “led the authorities to the arrest of these individuals for poaching a few weeks later”. It quotes Sanjay Kumar Pathak, former field director of Dudhwa, that the system “led to the detection and arrest of poachers in Dudhwa”. The Hindu (16 September 2023) cited a person involved in the experiment. Poachers caught on camera had a year later helped forest authorities secure a conviction. It quoted Piyush Yadav of Nightjar, the manufacturer, that “A year down, these poachers were arrested with images from TrailGuard playing a key role”. The article's lead puts the capture in Kanha-Pench and the Yadav quote in Dudhwa. No forest-department statement or court record of an arrest was found.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The camera's on-board classifier filtered motion triggers to people and tigers and transmitted the poachers' images to officials' phones within about a minute. Identification and investigation were done by officials. The peer-reviewed account is co-authored by the developers (RESOLVE, CVEDIA) with Dudhwa and Wildlife Institute of India staff and stops at “investigating”. The arrest claim rests on a Clemson release quoting the ex-field director, developer press releases and The Hindu quoting the manufacturer and an unnamed participant.

record.title: TrailGuard AI cameras in the Kanha-Pench corridor transmit tiger alerts to forest officials 30 to 42 seconds after detection in a pilot in 2022
record.summary: TrailGuard AI cameras sent tiger alerts to forest officials within 30 to 42 seconds. Officials later warned village leaders by text chat, though not rapidly.
record.account: Dertien et al. reported in BioScience (published 14 September 2023) that 12 TrailGuard AI camera-alert systems ran in the Kanha-Pench corridor, Madhya Pradesh. They ran from mid-May to mid-July 2022 (591 trap nights). The cameras run embedded AI on an Intel Myriad chip to detect tigers. The AI detects humans. The cameras transmit only images of interest. Researchers, with forest department officials, received tiger notifications 30 to 42 seconds after detection. The authors report that forest officials sent text-chat warnings to village leaders after detections that concerned them, although these messages were not rapid. They report that the sample was too small to determine an effect on human–wildlife conflict. The paper's second site is Dudhwa Tiger Reserve in Uttar Pradesh, where a unit captured armed poachers. That deployment is covered as a separate benefit. The Hindu (16 September 2023) reported the Madhya Pradesh deployment. It quoted H.S. Negi of the Global Tiger Forum on plans to incorporate the system in other tiger reserves. fields.account: Dertien et al. reported in BioScience (published 14 September 2023) that 12 TrailGuard AI camera-alert systems ran in the Kanha-Pench corridor, Madhya Pradesh. They ran from mid-May to mid-July 2022 (591 trap nights). The cameras run embedded AI on an Intel Myriad chip to detect tigers. The AI detects humans. The cameras transmit only images of interest. Researchers, with forest department officials, received tiger notifications 30 to 42 seconds after detection. The authors report that forest officials sent text-chat warnings to village leaders after detections that concerned them, although these messages were not rapid. They report that the sample was too small to determine an effect on human–wildlife conflict. The paper's second site is Dudhwa Tiger Reserve in Uttar Pradesh, where a unit captured armed poachers. That deployment is covered as a separate benefit. The Hindu (16 September 2023) reported the Madhya Pradesh deployment. It quoted H.S. Negi of the Global Tiger Forum on plans to incorporate the system in other tiger reserves. AFP (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the authors' claim that the cameras were “immediately effective, picking up a tiger just 300 meters from a village”. No forest department document on the pilot has been found.

record.title: Rainforest Connection's Guardian, an acoustic AI, flags chainsaws to patrollers in West Sumatra, one of whom says that logging stopped
record.summary: Rainforest Connection's Guardian sensors use AI to detect chainsaws. They alert patrols. In West Sumatra an alert led a patrol to a logger in August 2019. A patroller said that logging stopped.
record.account: Rainforest Connection (RFCx), a US non-profit founded by Topher White, deploys solar-powered “Guardian” acoustic sensors. In its own words, they use “sound & artificial intelligence” to track chainsaws. The sensors pick out vehicle engines. Hunting dogs are tracked. They track gunshots. They send real-time alerts to a mobile app so that “an agent nearby” can respond. On its impact page, RFCx states that it has protected over 726,000 hectares across 8,662+ projects in 137 countries. Its guardian page gives 750,000 hectares. Antara reported on a KKI Warsi press conference on 16 July 2020. There, Warsi said that the first 12 Guardian units went up in July 2019 in Sirukam and other nagari forests. In August 2019, a Guardian alert led the Sirukam patrol to a logger. The patrol caught the logger, who then escaped. Warsi counted 12 chainsaw alerts from sensors at 17 sites. It said that not all of them were illegal. A Thomson Reuters Foundation report published by The Straits Times on 11 February 2021 is the one independent account. It is from Solok regency, West Sumatra, Indonesia, where 27 Guardian sensors had been installed more than a year earlier. Audio streams are analyzed by AI trained to pick out chainsaw sounds. An alert goes to community patrols. Patroller Jasrialdi said that logging “has totally stopped” in the area. The head of West Sumatra's forestry department, Yozarwardi Usama Putra, said that he would like to expand the “early-warning system”. The reporters credit the decline in logging partly to a wider enforcement crackdown. They report that about 200 of Sirukam's 6,000 residents had worked in illegal logging. One former logger quit in 2018, before the sensors, because of the crackdown. The reporters add that RFCx planned to collect data for peer review to prove that the system curbs logging. No document from a park authority shows an alert that led to an interception. Ministries have published no such document. Courts have issued none.

fields.summary: Rainforest Connection's Guardian sensors use AI to detect chainsaws. They alert patrols. In West Sumatra an alert led a patrol to a logger in August 2019. A patroller said that logging stopped.
fields.account: Rainforest Connection (RFCx), a US non-profit founded by Topher White, deploys solar-powered “Guardian” acoustic sensors. In its own words, they use “sound & artificial intelligence” to track chainsaws. The sensors pick out vehicle engines. Hunting dogs are tracked. They track gunshots. They send real-time alerts to a mobile app so that “an agent nearby” can respond. On its impact page, RFCx states that it has protected over 726,000 hectares across 8,662+ projects in 137 countries. Its guardian page gives 750,000 hectares. Antara reported on a KKI Warsi press conference on 16 July 2020. There, Warsi said that the first 12 Guardian units went up in July 2019 in Sirukam and other nagari forests. In August 2019, a Guardian alert led the Sirukam patrol to a logger. The patrol caught the logger, who then escaped. Warsi counted 12 chainsaw alerts from sensors at 17 sites. It said that not all of them were illegal. A Thomson Reuters Foundation report published by The Straits Times on 11 February 2021 is the one independent account. It is from Solok regency, West Sumatra, Indonesia, where 27 Guardian sensors had been installed more than a year earlier. Audio streams are analyzed by AI trained to pick out chainsaw sounds. An alert goes to community patrols. Patroller Jasrialdi said that logging “has totally stopped” in the area. The head of West Sumatra's forestry department, Yozarwardi Usama Putra, said that he would like to expand the “early-warning system”. The reporters credit the decline in logging partly to a wider enforcement crackdown. They report that about 200 of Sirukam's 6,000 residents had worked in illegal logging. One former logger quit in 2018, before the sensors, because of the crackdown. The reporters add that RFCx planned to collect data for peer review to prove that the system curbs logging. No document from a park authority shows an alert that led to an interception. Ministries have published no such document. Courts have issued none.

record.title: Odakyu Electric Railway starts an AI crossing image-analysis system at four Odawara Line crossings that signals approaching trains to stop when people are left inside
record.summary: Odakyu's AI crossing image-analysis system reads existing crossing cameras. It signals approaching trains to stop when someone is left inside. Trains made 17 emergency stops in two months.
record.account: Meitetsu EI Engineer, Toyota Systems and Toho Electric Industries developed a system that analyzes images of crossings with AI. It was tested from January 2023. The work covered the accuracy of detection at night. It covered accuracy in rain. ITmedia's 岡田有花 reported on 22 June 2026 that Odakyu Electric Railway would introduce an “AI踏切画像解析システム” from 24 June 2026. It covers four crossings on its Odawara Line. They are Minami-Shinjuku Nos. 2, 4 and 5 between Minami-Shinjuku and Sangubashi stations. The fourth is Mukogaoka-Yuen No. 9 between Mukogaoka-Yuen and Ikuta stations. The AI analyzes footage from the existing safety-confirmation cameras in real time. It identifies pedestrians. It identifies wheelchair users. It identifies bicycles. It identifies motorcycles. It tracks them. When it detects someone left inside after the barriers come down, it sends a signal through the signaling equipment. That signal applies the brakes of approaching trains. It lights the crossing's special signal lamps to alert crews. Both are released automatically once the crossing is clear. Images are used only for hazard detection. The system does not identify individuals. Analysis data are destroyed within a year. railf.jp carried the same announcement on 25 June 2026. Yomiuri reported on 19 September 2026 that trains made 17 emergency stops on detected anomalies in the system's first two months. Yomiuri does not say whether any stop averted an accident. It adds that the transport ministry now pays up to half the installation cost of such systems. Professor Ryo Takagi of Kogakuin University told the paper that such systems are very effective for accident prevention. He warned that AI does not make crossings fully safe.

data.retained_case_account: ITmedia's 岡田有花 reported on 22 Jun 2026 that Odakyu Electric Railway would introduce an “AI踏切画像解析システム” from 24 June 2026. It covers four crossings on its Odawara Line. They are Minami-Shinjuku Nos. 2, 4 and 5 between Minami-Shinjuku and Sangubashi stations, and Mukogaoka-Yuen No. 9 between Mukogaoka-Yuen and Ikuta stations. The AI analyzes footage from the existing safety-confirmation cameras in real time. It identifies and tracks pedestrians, wheelchair users, bicycles and motorcycles. When it detects someone left inside after the barriers come down, it sends a signal through the signaling equipment. That applies the brakes of approaching trains and lights the crossing's special signal lamps to alert crews. Both are released automatically once the crossing is clear. Images are used only for hazard detection, not to identify individuals, and analysis data are destroyed within a year. The system was developed by Meitetsu EI Engineer, Toyota Systems and Toho Electric Industries. It was trialed from January 2023, with work on detection accuracy at night and in rain. railf.jp carried the same announcement on 25 Jun 2026. No detection events or outcomes are reported.

fields.account: Meitetsu EI Engineer, Toyota Systems and Toho Electric Industries developed a system that analyzes images of crossings with AI. It was tested from January 2023. The work covered the accuracy of detection at night. It covered accuracy in rain. ITmedia's 岡田有花 reported on 22 June 2026 that Odakyu Electric Railway would introduce an “AI踏切画像解析システム” from 24 June 2026. It covers four crossings on its Odawara Line. They are Minami-Shinjuku Nos. 2, 4 and 5 between Minami-Shinjuku and Sangubashi stations. The fourth is Mukogaoka-Yuen No. 9 between Mukogaoka-Yuen and Ikuta stations. The AI analyzes footage from the existing safety-confirmation cameras in real time. It identifies pedestrians. It identifies wheelchair users. It identifies bicycles. It identifies motorcycles. It tracks them. When it detects someone left inside after the barriers come down, it sends a signal through the signaling equipment. That signal applies the brakes of approaching trains. It lights the crossing's special signal lamps to alert crews. Both are released automatically once the crossing is clear. Images are used only for hazard detection. The system does not identify individuals. Analysis data are destroyed within a year. railf.jp carried the same announcement on 25 June 2026. Yomiuri reported on 19 September 2026 that trains made 17 emergency stops on detected anomalies in the system's first two months. Yomiuri does not say whether any stop averted an accident. record.title: Qualcomm's Dragonwing IQ10-powered humanoid may have run a “safe-collapse” sequence to protect its surroundings when it fell during a Computex 2026 demo in Taipei
record.summary: Qualcomm says that a humanoid on its Dragonwing IQ10 platform ran a designed “safe-collapse” sequence when it fell at Computex 2026. Reporters disagree on the direction of the fall.
record.account: Computex 2026 ran in Taipei from 2 to 5 June 2026. The COMPUTEX 2026 program lists a Qualcomm keynote by Cristiano Amon on 1 June 2026 at TaiNEX 2. Creative Bloq says that the robot was to co-present a keynote at Qualcomm's Computex event. The outlets say that the fall happened during Qualcomm's keynote presentation. During the live demo, a humanoid robot on Qualcomm's Dragonwing IQ10 AI platform collapsed on stage after a communication glitch. Qualcomm has not given the day of the fall. Gadget Review places it in July, after the show had ended. TechSpot identifies the robot as Neura Robotics' 4NE1 Gen 3.5 on Qualcomm's Dragonwing IQ10 robotics reference design. That design is listed at up to 700 TOPS, 6–8 hours' runtime, 100 kg payload, 5 ft 9 in. Gadget Review instead places the 4NE1 Gen 3.5's debut in Munich. It calls the Taipei unit “Qualcomm's Dragonwing IQ10 humanoid”. The video appeared on social media on 22 July 2026, in a post that Deccan Chronicle embeds. It spread from 27 to 30 July. Creative Bloq (27 July 2026, updated with a Qualcomm statement) quotes the company: “Live demos involve risk. At Computex in Taipei, a brief communication glitch triggered a fault in the prototype humanoid and initiated a controlled shutdown. The robot performed its designed safe-collapse sequence, lowering itself to its knees to protect the environment around it. The safety systems worked as intended.” The protective claim is Qualcomm's alone. NDTV (30 July), NDTV Profit (30 July, via The Indian Express) and Deccan Chronicle (30 July, “according to a news report”) relay the same statement. Asianet (31 July) and TechSpot (31 July) relay it. Gadget Review (28 July) says that the explanation “has not been independently confirmed”. It says that Qualcomm had issued no official public statement at its time of publication. Neura Robotics has posted no statement on the incident on its news page. No statement appears in Qualcomm's newsroom. The independent descriptions of the footage do not match a controlled kneel. NDTV says that the robot “tumbled face-first onto the stage”. Asianet says that it “crashed face-first”. Creative Bloq describes “a crashing heap of plastic and metal”. TechSpot says that it “collapsed like it had been shot”, “folding backwards on itself like a gymnast”. It says that the robot was “dropped onto the floor” while being carried off. data.retained_case_account: A humanoid robot on Qualcomm's Dragonwing IQ10 AI platform collapsed on stage during a live demo at Computex 2026 in Taipei after a communication glitch. The entry says it “executed a safe shutdown sequence, preventing harm”. The protective claim is Qualcomm's alone. Creative Bloq (27 July 2026, updated with a Qualcomm statement) quotes the company: “Live demos involve risk. At Computex in Taipei, a brief communication glitch triggered a fault in the prototype humanoid and initiated a controlled shutdown. The robot performed its designed safe-collapse sequence, lowering itself to its knees to protect the environment around it. The safety systems worked as intended.” NDTV (30 Jul), NDTV Profit (30 Jul, via The Indian Express) and Deccan Chronicle (30 Jul, “according to a news report”) relay the same statement. So do Asianet (31 Jul) and TechSpot (31 Jul). Gadget Review (28 Jul) says that the explanation “has not been independently confirmed”. It says Qualcomm had issued no official public statement at its time of publication. No statement was found on Qualcomm's or Neura Robotics' newsrooms. Qualcomm's release page rendered empty here, and Neura's news page lists no such item. The independent descriptions of the footage do not match a controlled kneel. NDTV says the robot “tumbled face-first onto the stage”, Asianet “crashed face-first”, and Creative Bloq “a crashing heap of plastic and metal”. TechSpot says it “collapsed like it had been shot”, “folding backwards on itself like a gymnast”, and was “dropped onto the floor” while being carried off. No person or object is reported at risk, and no beneficiary is identifiable. TechSpot identifies the robot as Neura Robotics' 4NE1 Gen 3.5 on Qualcomm's Dragonwing IQ10 robotics reference design. That design is listed at up to 700 TOPS, 6–8 hours' runtime, 100 kg payload, 5 ft 9 in. Gadget Review instead places the 4NE1 Gen 3.5's debut in Munich and calls the Taipei unit “Qualcomm's Dragonwing IQ10 humanoid”. The outlets say the fall happened during Qualcomm's keynote presentation. The Computex schedule lists Cristiano Amon's keynote on 1 June 2026 at TaiNEX 2, and the show ran 2–5 June. The sources do not give the exact day of the keynote. The video surfaced on social media on 22 July 2026 (a post embedded by Deccan Chronicle) and spread from 27–30 July. TechSpot's embedded November 2025 post is the Moscow AIdol clip cited for comparison.

display.answer: The protective claim traces to one Qualcomm statement, which Creative Bloq added in an update to its 27 July 2026 article. NDTV, NDTV Profit, Deccan Chronicle, Asianet and TechSpot relay the same statement. The descriptions of the fall come from the outlets that report the video posted on 22 July 2026.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: Qualcomm says that a humanoid on its Dragonwing IQ10 platform ran a designed “safe-collapse” sequence when it fell at Computex 2026. Reporters disagree on the direction of the fall.
fields.account: Computex 2026 ran in Taipei from 2 to 5 June 2026. The COMPUTEX 2026 program lists a Qualcomm keynote by Cristiano Amon on 1 June 2026 at TaiNEX 2. Creative Bloq says that the robot was to co-present a keynote at Qualcomm's Computex event. The outlets say that the fall happened during Qualcomm's keynote presentation. During the live demo, a humanoid robot on Qualcomm's Dragonwing IQ10 AI platform collapsed on stage after a communication glitch. Qualcomm has not given the day of the fall. Gadget Review places it in July, after the show had ended. TechSpot identifies the robot as Neura Robotics' 4NE1 Gen 3.5 on Qualcomm's Dragonwing IQ10 robotics reference design. That design is listed at up to 700 TOPS, 6–8 hours' runtime, 100 kg payload, 5 ft 9 in. Gadget Review instead places the 4NE1 Gen 3.5's debut in Munich. It calls the Taipei unit “Qualcomm's Dragonwing IQ10 humanoid”. The video appeared on social media on 22 July 2026, in a post that Deccan Chronicle embeds. It spread from 27 to 30 July. Creative Bloq (27 July 2026, updated with a Qualcomm statement) quotes the company: “Live demos involve risk. At Computex in Taipei, a brief communication glitch triggered a fault in the prototype humanoid and initiated a controlled shutdown. The robot performed its designed safe-collapse sequence, lowering itself to its knees to protect the environment around it. The safety systems worked as intended.” The protective claim is Qualcomm's alone. NDTV (30 July), NDTV Profit (30 July, via The Indian Express) and Deccan Chronicle (30 July, “according to a news report”) relay the same statement. Asianet (31 July) and TechSpot (31 July) relay it. Gadget Review (28 July) says that the explanation “has not been independently confirmed”. It says that Qualcomm had issued no official public statement at its time of publication. Neura Robotics has posted no statement on the incident on its news page. No statement appears in Qualcomm's newsroom. The independent descriptions of the footage do not match a controlled kneel. NDTV says that the robot “tumbled face-first onto the stage”. Asianet says that it “crashed face-first”. Creative Bloq describes “a crashing heap of plastic and metal”. TechSpot says that it “collapsed like it had been shot”, “folding backwards on itself like a gymnast”. It says that the robot was “dropped onto the floor” while being carried off. No person is reported at risk. No object is reported at risk. No beneficiary is identifiable.

record.title: UNDP's evaluation office reports that at three Zimbabwean irrigation schemes, drones with AI monitored crops, enabling earlier responses to threats
record.summary: UNDP's evaluation office reported that drones with AI monitored crop health at three Zimbabwean irrigation schemes. This sped up responses to threats of crop loss. The responses were more precise.
record.account: With the Government of Zimbabwe, UNDP runs a Green Climate Fund project to build the climate resilience of farm livelihoods in southern Zimbabwe. In June 2026, UNDP's Independent Evaluation Office published its evaluation of UNDP's country program from 2022 to July 2025. The evaluation drew on documents. Interviews with 228 stakeholders were among its sources. The office found that UNDP combined artificial intelligence, drone technology and machine-learning models to monitor crop health at the Midlo, Pikinini/Jawanda and Bindamombe irrigation schemes. It found that this enabled earlier responses to threats of crop loss. By its account, the responses were more precise. The office names no product. No developer is named. It gives no figure, date or source for this finding. It lists field visits in Chimanimani, Chipinge and Mutare, none of them to the three schemes. In an interim evaluation of the project dated 6 September 2024, two evaluators found that none of its irrigation schemes were ready for production at the time of their survey. They named Bindamombe, Midlo and Pikinini-Jawanda among the schemes whose civil works were complete but which had not started crop production. They do not mention drones. Artificial intelligence does not appear in their report.

fields.summary: UNDP's evaluation office reported that drones with AI monitored crop health at three Zimbabwean irrigation schemes. This sped up responses to threats of crop loss. The responses were more precise.
fields.account: With the Government of Zimbabwe, UNDP runs a Green Climate Fund project to build the climate resilience of farm livelihoods in southern Zimbabwe. In June 2026, UNDP's Independent Evaluation Office published its evaluation of UNDP's country program from 2022 to July 2025. The evaluation drew on documents. Interviews with 228 stakeholders were among its sources. The office found that UNDP combined artificial intelligence, drone technology and machine-learning models to monitor crop health at the Midlo, Pikinini/Jawanda and Bindamombe irrigation schemes. It found that this enabled earlier responses to threats of crop loss. By its account, the responses were more precise. The office names no product. No developer is named. It gives no figure, date or source for this finding. It lists field visits in Chimanimani, Chipinge and Mutare, none of them to the three schemes. In an interim evaluation of the project dated 6 September 2024, two evaluators found that none of its irrigation schemes were ready for production at the time of their survey. They named Bindamombe, Midlo and Pikinini-Jawanda among the schemes whose civil works were complete but which had not started crop production. They do not mention drones. Artificial intelligence does not appear in their report.

record.summary: Troopers said that the eye detection of a Tesla on Autopilot halted the car on I-75 after its intoxicated driver fell asleep. No vehicle data have been published to confirm it.
record.account: On 25 April 2024 the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration closed an engineering analysis that found that Autopilot's driver engagement system was weak for the system's permissive operation. ABC 7's WWSB reported on 24 April 2026 that a Tesla had stopped in the middle lane of Interstate 75 near Sarasota. At about 2 a.m., Florida Highway Patrol officers found a 37-year-old woman asleep behind the wheel. The station quotes Trooper Kenn Watson. It reports that she was arrested for driving under the influence. It reports that the car came to a halt in the middle lane when the woman stopped responding to the vehicle's alerts. The station reports that she had expected Autopilot to take her home. Alistair Weaver, an analyst at Edmunds, explains the general warning for driver attention. He explains the mechanism that stops the car. The station published no vehicle logs that establish the precise sequence in this car. Gray News, citing state police, reported that troopers found the woman at about 2 a.m. on Friday, 24 April 2026. It reported that the troopers credited the car's eye detection with bringing it to a halt. Ouest-France reported on 3 May 2026 that her blood alcohol level was more than twice the legal limit.
record.purpose: Tesla built Autopilot's monitoring of driver attention to warn an inattentive driver and to stop the car if the driver does not respond. It is not designed to drive an impaired person home.

fields.summary: Troopers said that the eye detection of a Tesla on Autopilot halted the car on I-75 after its intoxicated driver fell asleep. No vehicle data have been published to confirm it.
fields.account: On 25 April 2024 the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration closed an engineering analysis that found that Autopilot's driver engagement system was weak for the system's permissive operation. ABC 7's WWSB reported on 24 April 2026 that a Tesla had stopped in the middle lane of Interstate 75 near Sarasota. At about 2 a.m., Florida Highway Patrol officers found a 37-year-old woman asleep behind the wheel. The station quotes Trooper Kenn Watson. It reports that she was arrested for driving under the influence. It reports that the car came to a halt in the middle lane when the woman stopped responding to the vehicle's alerts. The station reports that she had expected Autopilot to take her home. Alistair Weaver, an analyst at Edmunds, explains the general warning for driver attention. He explains the mechanism that stops the car. The station published no vehicle logs that establish the precise sequence in this car. Gray News, citing state police, reported that troopers found the woman at about 2 a.m. on Friday, 24 April 2026. It reported that the troopers credited the car's eye detection with bringing it to a halt. Ouest-France reported on 3 May 2026 that her blood alcohol level was more than twice the legal limit.

value.text: The vehicle reportedly stopped after the driver failed to respond to alerts. That was a fallback response within driver assistance. It was not evidence that the vehicle could complete the trip safely without a driver.

record.title: Israel's Iron Beam laser may have made its first combat interception, of a Hezbollah drone, in footage of 2 March 2026, though the military said on 12 March that Iron Beam had not been used
record.summary: Footage of 2 March 2026 may show Israel's Iron Beam laser downing a Hezbollah drone. On 12 March the military said that Iron Beam had not been used. No cited source lists the laser as AI.
record.account: None of the cited outlets describes Iron Beam as an AI system. The only other mention of AI is Rafael's chief executive describing artificial intelligence as a next step for the system (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). The only confirmed combat use of a laser came earlier. It is reported only in aggregate. A lower-powered, shorter-range variant shot down some 35 drones from Lebanon in 2024 (Times of Israel/AFP). The Ministry of Defense announced it in May 2025 (The Jerusalem Post). The ministry said that no Iron Beam components were involved (Wikipedia). The Times of Israel reports the Defense Ministry's handover of the first operational system on 28 December 2025, after tests against rockets, mortars and drones. The Iron Beam claim rests on social-media footage from Monday 2 March 2026. Ynet (Yair Kraus) reports that the footage “appeared to show the first operational use” of the system. It was delivered to the Israeli Air Force in late December 2025. Hezbollah fired rockets from Lebanon after the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader. It fired drones, with one drone intercepted near Shlomi. The Jerusalem Post (Seth Frantzman, 2 March 2026) says that the circulated video “did not show lasers intercepting rockets”. TimesNow (2 March 2026) says that whether this was Iron Beam's first combat use “awaits official confirmation”. Army Recognition (3 March 2026) says that officials “have not formally confirmed the specific engagements”. It says that the system appears in no authoritative combat log. The Conversation (4 March 2026) calls the reports unconfirmed. The Jerusalem Post reported on 12 March 2026 that the Israel Defense Forces said that Iron Beam had not been used. They said that it was not ready for regular use in the war. Times of Israel/AFP (16 March 2026) reports that the military “has so far refused to comment on its use during the ongoing war”. Times of Israel (Stav Levaton, 27 March 2026) reports that “military officials said it has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. On 1 May 2026 the Israel Air Force said that the system saw less use because it needs 14 batteries to have much effect. Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian, 30 June 2026) reports that the one deployed system “has seen limited use and has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. A senior officer called its coverage partial. A senior defense official told Ynetnews on 9 August 2026 that the one system delivered in December 2025 was still not operational.
record.purpose: Rafael and Israel's Ministry of Defense built Iron Beam, a high-energy laser, to intercept rockets, mortars and drones at short range. It is a low-cost complement to Iron Dome, David's Sling and Arrow.

data.retained_case_account: It separately bundles a Hankyoreh item (dated 10 October 2023) on Hamas rockets penetrating Iron Dome. The Iron Beam claim rests on social-media footage from Monday 2 March 2026, not 28 February. Ynet (Yair Kraus) reports that the footage “appeared to show the first operational use” of the system. It was delivered to the Israeli Air Force in late December 2025. Hezbollah fired rockets and drones from Lebanon after the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader, with one drone intercepted near Shlomi. The Jerusalem Post (Seth Frantzman, 2 March 2026) says that the circulated video “did not show lasers intercepting rockets”. TimesNow (2 March 2026) says that whether this was Iron Beam's first combat use “awaits official confirmation”. Army Recognition (3 March 2026) says that officials “have not formally confirmed the specific engagements” and that no authoritative combat log names the system. The Conversation (4 March 2026) calls the reports unconfirmed. Moneycontrol (3 March 2026) sources its “first-ever use” to an “Israel War Room” social-media video. The Times of Israel reports the Defense Ministry's handover of the first operational system on 28 December 2025, after tests against rockets, mortars and drones. Times of Israel/AFP (16 March 2026) reports that the IDF “has so far refused to comment on its use during the ongoing war”. Times of Israel (Stav Levaton, 27 March 2026) reports that “military officials said it has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian, 30 June 2026) reports that the one deployed system “has seen limited use and has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. A senior officer called its coverage partial. The only confirmed laser combat use is aggregate and earlier. A lower-powered, shorter-range variant shot down some 35 drones from Lebanon in 2024 (Times of Israel/AFP). The Ministry of Defense announced it in May 2025 (JPost). The MoD said that no Iron Beam components were involved (Wikipedia). No cited source describes Iron Beam as an AI system. The only AI mention found is Rafael's CEO framing machine learning as a future capability (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). That piece is not among the sources.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: No cited source describes Iron Beam as an AI or machine-learning system. Those sources are Ynet, JPost, Army Recognition, TimesNow, The Conversation and Moneycontrol. They also include Times of Israel 28 December 2025, 16 Mar, 27 Mar and 30 June 2026, and Wikipedia. They describe a high-power laser with a beam director and electro-optical targeting. Rafael's CEO described machine learning as a future capability (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). The IDF has not confirmed the engagement itself, so neither an AI role nor a contribution can be assessed.

fields.account: None of the cited outlets describes Iron Beam as an AI system. The only other mention of AI is Rafael's chief executive describing artificial intelligence as a next step for the system (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). The only confirmed combat use of a laser came earlier. It is reported only in aggregate. A lower-powered, shorter-range variant shot down some 35 drones from Lebanon in 2024 (Times of Israel/AFP). The Ministry of Defense announced it in May 2025 (The Jerusalem Post). The ministry said that no Iron Beam components were involved (Wikipedia). The Times of Israel reports the Defense Ministry's handover of the first operational system on 28 December 2025, after tests against rockets, mortars and drones. The Iron Beam claim rests on social-media footage from Monday 2 March 2026. Ynet (Yair Kraus) reports that the footage “appeared to show the first operational use” of the system. It was delivered to the Israeli Air Force in late December 2025. Hezbollah fired rockets from Lebanon after the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader. It fired drones, with one drone intercepted near Shlomi. The Jerusalem Post (Seth Frantzman, 2 March 2026) says that the circulated video “did not show lasers intercepting rockets”. TimesNow (2 March 2026) says that whether this was Iron Beam's first combat use “awaits official confirmation”. Army Recognition (3 March 2026) says that officials “have not formally confirmed the specific engagements”. It says that the system appears in no authoritative combat log. The Conversation (4 March 2026) calls the reports unconfirmed. The Jerusalem Post reported on 12 March 2026 that the Israel Defense Forces said that Iron Beam had not been used. They said that it was not ready for regular use in the war. Times of Israel/AFP (16 March 2026) reports that the military “has so far refused to comment on its use during the ongoing war”. Times of Israel (Stav Levaton, 27 March 2026) reports that “military officials said it has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. On 1 May 2026 the Israel Air Force said that the system saw less use because it needs 14 batteries to have much effect. Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian, 30 June 2026) reports that the one deployed system “has seen limited use and has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. A senior officer called its coverage partial. A senior defense official told Ynetnews on 9 August 2026 that the one system delivered in December 2025 was still not operational.

The Times of Israel reports the Defense Ministry's handover of the first operational system on 28 December 2025, after tests against rockets, mortars and drones. The Iron Beam claim rests on social-media footage from Monday 2 March 2026. Ynet (Yair Kraus) reports that the footage “appeared to show the first operational use” of the system. It was delivered to the Israeli Air Force in late December 2025. Hezbollah fired rockets from Lebanon after the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader. It fired drones, with one drone intercepted near Shlomi. The Jerusalem Post (Seth Frantzman, 2 March 2026) says that the circulated video “did not show lasers intercepting rockets”. TimesNow (2 March 2026) says that whether this was Iron Beam's first combat use “awaits official confirmation”. Army Recognition (3 March 2026) says that officials “have not formally confirmed the specific engagements”. It says that the system appears in no authoritative combat log. The Conversation (4 March 2026) calls the reports unconfirmed. The Jerusalem Post reported on 12 March 2026 that the Israel Defense Forces said that Iron Beam had not been used. They said that it was not ready for regular use in the war. Times of Israel/AFP (16 March 2026) reports that the military “has so far refused to comment on its use during the ongoing war”. Times of Israel (Stav Levaton, 27 March 2026) reports that “military officials said it has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. On 1 May 2026 the Israel Air Force said that the system saw less use because it needs 14 batteries to have much effect. Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian, 30 June 2026) reports that the one deployed system “has seen limited use and has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. A senior officer called its coverage partial. A senior defense official told Ynetnews on 9 August 2026 that the one system delivered in December 2025 was still not operational.

record.title: A hospital's account conflicts with a relative’s claim that ChatGPT helped save a teenager from poisoning
record.summary: A relative credited ChatGPT's advice to drink paraffin oil with saving a teenager from a grain pill. The medical dean at Assiut University said that the teenager showed no signs of poisoning.
record.account: A commercial-control inspector wrote a Facebook post at 1 a.m., “24 hours” after his 17-year-old cousin swallowed part of a “grain pill” (aluminum phosphide). The post does not give the date of ingestion. No press report gives it. The pill came from samples that the inspector had seized. He had kept them at the family's old house. The cousin took it after a quarrel with his father. The inspector writes that the Abnoub central hospital refused the case. He writes that within minutes he asked ChatGPT for the best course. It gave paraffin oil as the answer. The oil would coat the pill to limit the release of phosphine. The youth drank a bottle from a pharmacy before they went to the poison reception of Assiut University Hospital. Doctors there said that there was no treatment protocol. They said that the case would die. He then gave instructions from “an advanced AI model and a limited-use trial version of GPT-5”. Nine bottles of paraffin oil were given in turn with breathing exercises. The inspector writes that the youth stayed fully conscious through the night, without acute toxic symptoms. He writes that a blood test for mitochondrial poisoning came back negative. The youth, who stayed conscious, vomited for hours. He was discharged stable. El Balad reproduces the post (24 May 2025, 12:39). Dostor (24 May 2025, 22:40) reports the post with the reply of Dr. Alaa Attia, dean of the Faculty of Medicine at Assiut University. He said that precise medical examinations showed nothing to suggest that the youth had swallowed the pill. The youth denied taking it. He admitted throwing it into a water basin. The dean added that the hospital is researching paraffin oil with acetylcysteine as an adjunct. The protocol is experimental. It has not been officially adopted. Masrawy (25 May 2025) quotes the dean as saying that the youth, about 17, showed no clinical symptoms of phosphine poisoning. The team questioned him. He categorically denied swallowing the pill. He cited a family dispute over travel to Italy. Dostor (25 May 2025) adds the views of the toxicologist Dr. Mahmoud Amr, founder of the National Poison Center. He says that oils are a necessary first aid in grain-pill poisoning. Al Jazeera Mubasher (26 May 2025) quotes Amr as saying that the claim that paraffin oil rescues such a case “has no scientific basis”. It quotes Dr. Nermin Hamdi, a toxicologist at Cairo University, as saying that Assiut University denied that the case involved the grain pill. Hamdi adds that giving oil counts only as first aid. Hamdi says that it does not treat the poisoning. In a meta-analysis of randomized trials, published in 2024, the authors found that paraffin-oil gastric lavage in hospital lowers mortality from aluminum phosphide poisoning, on low-quality evidence.
record.purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose assistant. The cousin used it for emergency first-aid advice and, by his account, for instructions during hospital care. The claimed benefit (a survival) is outside any stated purpose of the system.
record.system: ChatGPT, according to the patient's cousin. He described the model as an advanced AI model and a limited-use trial version of GPT-5, but that identification is unverified. OpenAI publicly introduced GPT-5 on 7 August 2025, after the May report.

fields.account: A commercial-control inspector wrote a Facebook post at 1 a.m., “24 hours” after his 17-year-old cousin swallowed part of a “grain pill” (aluminum phosphide). The post does not give the date of ingestion. No press report gives it. The pill came from samples that the inspector had seized. He had kept them at the family's old house. The cousin took it after a quarrel with his father. The inspector writes that the Abnoub central hospital refused the case. He writes that within minutes he asked ChatGPT for the best course. It gave paraffin oil as the answer. The oil would coat the pill to limit the release of phosphine. The youth drank a bottle from a pharmacy before they went to the poison reception of Assiut University Hospital. Doctors there said that there was no treatment protocol. They said that the case would die. He then gave instructions from “an advanced AI model and a limited-use trial version of GPT-5”. Nine bottles of paraffin oil were given in turn with breathing exercises. The inspector writes that the youth stayed fully conscious through the night, without acute toxic symptoms. He writes that a blood test for mitochondrial poisoning came back negative. The youth, who stayed conscious, vomited for hours. He was discharged stable. El Balad reproduces the post (24 May 2025, 12:39). Dostor (24 May 2025, 22:40) reports the post with the reply of Dr. Alaa Attia, dean of the Faculty of Medicine at Assiut University. He said that precise medical examinations showed nothing to suggest that the youth had swallowed the pill. The youth denied taking it. He admitted throwing it into a water basin. The dean added that the hospital is researching paraffin oil with acetylcysteine as an adjunct. The protocol is experimental. It has not been officially adopted. Masrawy (25 May 2025) quotes the dean as saying that the youth, about 17, showed no clinical symptoms of phosphine poisoning. The team questioned him. He categorically denied swallowing the pill. He cited a family dispute over travel to Italy. Dostor (25 May 2025) adds the views of the toxicologist Dr. Mahmoud Amr, founder of the National Poison Center. He says that oils are a necessary first aid in grain-pill poisoning. Al Jazeera Mubasher (26 May 2025) quotes Amr as saying that the claim that paraffin oil rescues such a case “has no scientific basis”. It quotes Dr. Nermin Hamdi, a toxicologist at Cairo University, as saying that Assiut University denied that the case involved the grain pill. Hamdi adds that giving oil counts only as first aid. Hamdi says that it does not treat the poisoning. In a meta-analysis of randomized trials, published in 2024, the authors found that paraffin-oil gastric lavage in hospital lowers mortality from aluminum phosphide poisoning, on low-quality evidence.

They said that the case would die. He then gave instructions from “an advanced AI model and a limited-use trial version of GPT-5”. Nine bottles of paraffin oil were given in turn with breathing exercises. The inspector writes that the youth stayed fully conscious through the night, without acute toxic symptoms. He writes that a blood test for mitochondrial poisoning came back negative. The youth, who stayed conscious, vomited for hours. He was discharged stable. El Balad reproduces the post (24 May 2025, 12:39). Dostor (24 May 2025, 22:40) reports the post with the reply of Dr. Alaa Attia, dean of the Faculty of Medicine at Assiut University. He said that precise medical examinations showed nothing to suggest that the youth had swallowed the pill. The youth denied taking it. He admitted throwing it into a water basin. The dean added that the hospital is researching paraffin oil with acetylcysteine as an adjunct. The protocol is experimental. It has not been officially adopted. Masrawy (25 May 2025) quotes the dean as saying that the youth, about 17, showed no clinical symptoms of phosphine poisoning. The team questioned him. He categorically denied swallowing the pill. He cited a family dispute over travel to Italy. Dostor (25 May 2025) adds the views of the toxicologist Dr. Mahmoud Amr, founder of the National Poison Center. He says that oils are a necessary first aid in grain-pill poisoning. Al Jazeera Mubasher (26 May 2025) quotes Amr as saying that the claim that paraffin oil rescues such a case “has no scientific basis”. It quotes Dr. Nermin Hamdi, a toxicologist at Cairo University, as saying that Assiut University denied that the case involved the grain pill. Hamdi adds that giving oil counts only as first aid. Hamdi says that it does not treat the poisoning. In a meta-analysis of randomized trials, published in 2024, the authors found that paraffin-oil gastric lavage in hospital lowers mortality from aluminum phosphide poisoning, on low-quality evidence.

record.title: Rafael's X-Guard towed decoy, labeled “AI-powered”, may have diverted Pakistani missiles from Indian Rafales in Operation Sindoor (7–10 May 2025). India's defense chief reports Indian aircraft losses. So does France's air force chief
record.summary: Commentators credit Rafael's X-Guard towed decoy, labeled “AI-powered”, with diverting Pakistani missiles from Indian Rafales. No official has confirmed its use. India admitted jet losses.
record.account: In its product brochure of March 2024, Rafael describes a reusable fiber-optic towed decoy. Rafael identifies no AI model in it. The company does not confirm deployment in Operation Sindoor. Operation Sindoor began on 7 May 2025. It lasted four days (India TV). At the Shangri-La Dialogue on 31 May 2025, India's Chief of Defence Staff, General Anil Chauhan, admitted that an unspecified number of Indian jets were shot down. He rejected Pakistan's claim of six (Al Jazeera, 1 June 2025, as well as Wikipedia citing Bloomberg). He placed India's air losses on the first day of fighting. The claim for the decoy first appears in an idrw.org post of 6 July 2025, credited to “AFI”, an outsourced content partner. In the post, idrw quotes Ryan Bodenheimer, a former US Air Force F-15E and F-16 pilot. Bodenheimer calls the Indian Air Force's tactics “the best spoofing and deception we've ever seen”. He credits “the Rafale's X-Guard AI-enhanced jamming decoy system”. idrw itself writes that the system “likely played a pivotal role”. It adds, citing Jane's Defence Weekly, that Pakistani claims of downed Rafales were “likely X-Guard decoys”. On the same day the Associated Press quoted General Jérôme Bellanger, chief of the French air force. Bellanger reported seeing evidence of three Indian aircraft losses, one of them a Rafale. The Economic Times writes on 8 July 2025 that the Indian Air Force “reportedly used artificial intelligence-powered technology”. On 9 July LatestLY says that it “allegedly used” it. India TV, on 9 July, attributes a finding that Pakistani kills were hits on towed decoys to “a recent Jane's Defence Weekly investigation”. idrw had cited the same investigation on 6 July. No outlet corroborates it independently. The Jane's Defence Weekly investigation itself is not among the sources. Oneindia (9 July) says that false claims of downed Rafales “may have been decoys”. TFIPOST (9 July) says that the Indian Air Force “reportedly deployed” the system. It names the maker correctly as Rafael Advanced Defense Systems. The Economic Times, India TV, LatestLY, Oneindia and idrw write “Rafale Advanced Defense Systems”. The Indian Air Force, the Ministry of Defence, Dassault and Rafael have not confirmed that X-Guard was carried. They have not confirmed that it was deployed. The claimed outcome of no losses is contradicted by India's Chief of Defence Staff.
record.purpose: Rafael built X-Guard to present a false target to enemy radars and radar-guided missiles, which then engage the decoy and spare the aircraft. News outlets describe a 30 kg body on a 100 m fiber-optic cable that emits a 500 W jamming signal.

He calls the IAF's tactics “the best spoofing and deception we've ever seen” and credits “the Rafale's X-Guard AI-enhanced jamming decoy system”. idrw itself writes that the system “likely played a pivotal role”. fields.account: In its product brochure of March 2024, Rafael describes a reusable fiber-optic towed decoy. Rafael identifies no AI model in it. The company does not confirm deployment in Operation Sindoor. Operation Sindoor began on 7 May 2025. It lasted four days (India TV). At the Shangri-La Dialogue on 31 May 2025, India's Chief of Defence Staff, General Anil Chauhan, admitted that an unspecified number of Indian jets were shot down. He rejected Pakistan's claim of six (Al Jazeera, 1 June 2025, as well as Wikipedia citing Bloomberg). He placed India's air losses on the first day of fighting. The claim for the decoy first appears in an idrw.org post of 6 July 2025, credited to “AFI”, an outsourced content partner. In the post, idrw quotes Ryan Bodenheimer, a former US Air Force F-15E and F-16 pilot. Bodenheimer calls the Indian Air Force's tactics “the best spoofing and deception we've ever seen”. He credits “the Rafale's X-Guard AI-enhanced jamming decoy system”. idrw itself writes that the system “likely played a pivotal role”. It adds, citing Jane's Defence Weekly, that Pakistani claims of downed Rafales were “likely X-Guard decoys”. On the same day the Associated Press quoted General Jérôme Bellanger, chief of the French air force. Bellanger reported seeing evidence of three Indian aircraft losses, one of them a Rafale. The Economic Times writes on 8 July 2025 that the Indian Air Force “reportedly used artificial intelligence-powered technology”. On 9 July LatestLY says that it “allegedly used” it. India TV, on 9 July, attributes a finding that Pakistani kills were hits on towed decoys to “a recent Jane's Defence Weekly investigation”. idrw had cited the same investigation on 6 July. No outlet corroborates it independently. The Jane's Defence Weekly investigation itself is not among the sources. Oneindia (9 July) says that false claims of downed Rafales “may have been decoys”. TFIPOST (9 July) says that the Indian Air Force “reportedly deployed” the system. It names the maker correctly as Rafael Advanced Defense Systems. The Economic Times, India TV, LatestLY, Oneindia and idrw write “Rafale Advanced Defense Systems”. The Indian Air Force, the Ministry of Defence, Dassault and Rafael have not confirmed that X-Guard was carried. They have not confirmed that it was deployed. The claimed outcome of no losses is contradicted by India's Chief of Defence Staff.

record.title: RFI’s AlpEW seismic-warning system reportedly stops Rome–Naples trains during a magnitude 4.4 earthquake
record.summary: Rete Ferroviaria Italiana's AlpEW seismic early-warning system reportedly stopped Rome–Naples trains during a magnitude 4.4 earthquake. Its developers describe no learned AI model.
record.account: According to Euronews, Rete Ferroviaria Italiana's seismic early-warning system on the Rome-Naples high-speed line had been operational since 3 May 2025. Euronews reported that in the following weeks it was tested by a magnitude 4.4 earthquake, during which trains on the Rome-Naples line were stopped preventively. A magnitude 4.4 earthquake struck Campi Flegrei on 13 May 2025. Quotidiano Nazionale reported that high-speed trains in the Naples node were suspended that day. No source shows that the warning system made that stop. ANSA reported on 14 July 2025 that Ferrovie dello Stato's infrastructure company Rete Ferroviaria Italiana had activated Italy's first seismic early-warning system on the line. It was developed with the Physics Department of the University of Naples Federico II. Technical support came from the Railway Technical Research Institute of the Japanese railways. A network of latest-generation sensors detects the earliest seismic waves. Within seconds it automatically activates safety protocols to slow or stop trains. ANSA does not mention artificial intelligence. Euronews added on 15 July 2025 that the system comprises about 20 seismic stations along 200 km, on the surface and in deep boreholes. They are linked by a synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH) fiber network. According to Euronews, an advanced software intelligence instantly analyzes the data and assesses the danger of the quake. Euronews attributes the magnitude 4.4 episode to RailTech and places it within two weeks of the 3 May 2025 start. The two outlets give no exact date for that earthquake. In January 2026 the developers published a peer-reviewed study of the system in Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences. They describe signal processing with empirical prediction of ground motion. They describe probabilistic thresholds for alerts. They describe no learned AI model in the deployed system. Their operational observations cover March 2020 to January 2022. They do not verify the magnitude 4.4 stop. The developers wrote that Rete Ferroviaria Italiana had decided to extend the system to other high-speed lines. Wired Italia reported on 24 May 2026 that the system was still in use. It reported that its developers were studying machine learning to refine it. No report shows a second line in service by October 2026.
record.purpose: Rete Ferroviaria Italiana built the system to detect the first seismic waves and slow or stop high-speed trains automatically before stronger shaking arrives.
record.system: AlpEW (Array lineare per Early Warning), RFI’s seismic early-warning platform for the Rome–Naples high-speed railway.
record.developer: Rete Ferroviaria Italiana with the Physics Department of the University of Naples Federico II and JR RTRI
record.deployer: Rete Ferroviaria Italiana (Gruppo FS)

ratings.reason: Euronews reports that trains were stopped as a precaution during a magnitude 4.4 earthquake. Rete Ferroviaria Italiana has reported no damage avoided or delay or cost saved for the railway, and the stop itself is the protective action.

fields.account: According to Euronews, Rete Ferroviaria Italiana's seismic early-warning system on the Rome-Naples high-speed line had been operational since 3 May 2025. Euronews reported that in the following weeks it was tested by a magnitude 4.4 earthquake, during which trains on the Rome-Naples line were stopped preventively. A magnitude 4.4 earthquake struck Campi Flegrei on 13 May 2025. Quotidiano Nazionale reported that high-speed trains in the Naples node were suspended that day. No source shows that the warning system made that stop. ANSA reported on 14 July 2025 that Ferrovie dello Stato's infrastructure company Rete Ferroviaria Italiana had activated Italy's first seismic early-warning system on the line. It was developed with the Physics Department of the University of Naples Federico II. Technical support came from the Railway Technical Research Institute of the Japanese railways. A network of latest-generation sensors detects the earliest seismic waves. Within seconds it automatically activates safety protocols to slow or stop trains. ANSA does not mention artificial intelligence. Euronews added on 15 July 2025 that the system comprises about 20 seismic stations along 200 km, on the surface and in deep boreholes. They are linked by a synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH) fiber network. According to Euronews, an advanced software intelligence instantly analyzes the data and assesses the danger of the quake. Euronews attributes the magnitude 4.4 episode to RailTech and places it within two weeks of the 3 May 2025 start. The two outlets give no exact date for that earthquake. In January 2026 the developers published a peer-reviewed study of the system in Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences. They describe signal processing with empirical prediction of ground motion. They describe probabilistic thresholds for alerts. They describe no learned AI model in the deployed system. Their operational observations cover March 2020 to January 2022. They do not verify the magnitude 4.4 stop. The developers wrote that Rete Ferroviaria Italiana had decided to extend the system to other high-speed lines. Wired Italia reported on 24 May 2026 that the system was still in use. It reported that its developers were studying machine learning to refine it. No report shows a second line in service by October 2026.

The developers wrote in January 2026 that Rete Ferroviaria Italiana had decided to extend it to other high-speed lines. No report shows a second line in service by October 2026.

fields.summary: Rete Ferroviaria Italiana's AlpEW seismic early-warning system reportedly stopped Rome–Naples trains during a magnitude 4.4 earthquake. Its developers describe no learned AI model.
fields.account: According to Euronews, Rete Ferroviaria Italiana's seismic early-warning system on the Rome-Naples high-speed line had been operational since 3 May 2025. Euronews reported that in the following weeks it was tested by a magnitude 4.4 earthquake, during which trains on the Rome-Naples line were stopped preventively. A magnitude 4.4 earthquake struck Campi Flegrei on 13 May 2025. Quotidiano Nazionale reported that high-speed trains in the Naples node were suspended that day. No source shows that the warning system made that stop. ANSA reported on 14 July 2025 that Ferrovie dello Stato's infrastructure company Rete Ferroviaria Italiana had activated Italy's first seismic early-warning system on the line. It was developed with the Physics Department of the University of Naples Federico II. Technical support came from the Railway Technical Research Institute of the Japanese railways. A network of latest-generation sensors detects the earliest seismic waves. Within seconds it automatically activates safety protocols to slow or stop trains. ANSA does not mention artificial intelligence. Euronews added on 15 July 2025 that the system comprises about 20 seismic stations along 200 km, on the surface and in deep boreholes. They are linked by a synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH) fiber network. According to Euronews, an advanced software intelligence instantly analyzes the data and assesses the danger of the quake. Euronews attributes the magnitude 4.4 episode to RailTech and places it within two weeks of the 3 May 2025 start. The two outlets give no exact date for that earthquake. In January 2026 the developers published a peer-reviewed study of the system in Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences. They describe signal processing with empirical prediction of ground motion. They describe probabilistic thresholds for alerts. They describe no learned AI model in the deployed system. Their operational observations cover March 2020 to January 2022. They do not verify the magnitude 4.4 stop. The developers wrote that Rete Ferroviaria Italiana had decided to extend the system to other high-speed lines. Wired Italia reported on 24 May 2026 that the system was still in use. It reported that its developers were studying machine learning to refine it. No report shows a second line in service by October 2026.

details.label: Contribution of the AI
details.value: PTI reports that the chain starts with a red-flag tag on Meta's system when a student posts suicide or self-harm content. Account information is then shared with police. PTI does not say whether Meta's classifier or a user report raised the flag in the Jhunjhunu case, or what happened on arrival. In its own description (2018, updated 2021), Meta says that machine-learning detection is followed by human review before authorities are contacted. The intervention itself was police work. PTI also notes that no red-flag tags had been reported in Kota city since the launch.

record.title: Within a week of tying up with Meta to route flags of self-harm from Facebook and Instagram to Abhay Command Centre, Kota police say that they prevented a possible suicide by a Jhunjhunu student
record.summary: Kota police receive Meta's red-flag tags for posts about self-harm on Facebook and Instagram. Within a week, police said that they had prevented a possible suicide by a Jhunjhunu student.
record.account: In its newsroom, Meta describes machine-learning detection of posts about suicide. The detection covers posts about self-injury. Human review comes before authorities are contacted (Card, 2018). PTI reported from Kota on 28 May 2024 that city police under Superintendent Amrita Duhan had tied up with Meta. Its aim is to identify students exhibiting suicidal tendencies on Facebook and Instagram. When a student posts content about suicide or self-harm, a red-flag tag appears on Meta's system. Account information is then shared with Kota police. For students outside Kota it goes to Abhay Command Centre. It may instead go to the district control room. There a dedicated team works round the clock in eight-hour shifts. By PTI's account, the tie-up started about a week before 28 May 2024. Within a week of the launch, police said that they had prevented a possible suicide by a student from Jhunjhunu district. The intervention therefore took place in May 2024, on a date that PTI does not give. No red-flag tags had yet been reported in the city. PTI counted nine suicides among coaching students in 2024 to date. It counted 26 in 2023. Duhan planned to extend the arrangement to Jaipur (PTI via LatestLY). No later report covers the Kota arrangement. None covers its planned extension to Jaipur. The same chain of a Meta alert routed to police has been reported in Uttar Pradesh, in Raebareli on 29 March 2026 and in Meerut on 7 June 2026.
record.purpose: Meta built its pipeline to find posts that indicate a risk of suicide or self-injury and route them to trained reviewers, who contact local authorities in imminent cases. The Kota arrangement routes those flags to police.

fields.account: In its newsroom, Meta describes machine-learning detection of posts about suicide. The detection covers posts about self-injury. Human review comes before authorities are contacted (Card, 2018). PTI reported from Kota on 28 May 2024 that city police under Superintendent Amrita Duhan had tied up with Meta. Its aim is to identify students exhibiting suicidal tendencies on Facebook and Instagram. When a student posts content about suicide or self-harm, a red-flag tag appears on Meta's system. Account information is then shared with Kota police. For students outside Kota it goes to Abhay Command Centre. It may instead go to the district control room. There a dedicated team works round the clock in eight-hour shifts. By PTI's account, the tie-up started about a week before 28 May 2024. Within a week of the launch, police said that they had prevented a possible suicide by a student from Jhunjhunu district. The intervention therefore took place in May 2024, on a date that PTI does not give. No red-flag tags had yet been reported in the city. PTI counted nine suicides among coaching students in 2024 to date. It counted 26 in 2023. Duhan planned to extend the arrangement to Jaipur (PTI via LatestLY). No later report covers the Kota arrangement. None covers its planned extension to Jaipur. The same chain of a Meta alert routed to police has been reported in Uttar Pradesh, in Raebareli on 29 March 2026 and in Meerut on 7 June 2026.

record.title: A threat alert from Meta, relayed through the FBI, brings Paraguayan police with psychologists to a bullied 17-year-old who praised the Uvalde shooter
record.summary: Meta flagged a post in which a Paraguayan teenager praised the Uvalde shooter. After the FBI relayed the alert, police visited him with psychologists.
record.account: On Thursday 26 May 2022, two days after the Uvalde school shooting, Paraguay's Policía Nacional and Ministerio Público received an alert. It came from Meta's platform and the FBI office in Buenos Aires. A user in Paraguay had tagged the shooter. He called himself his “fan”. He said that something similar could happen in Paraguay with more victims. Comisario Diosnel Alarcón's cybercrime department identified the owner of the Instagram profile as a 17-year-old in the “zona central”. He lived with a relative. Officials treated him as a victim of bullying. Police visited the home. Prosecutors went with them. The children's defender went. Psychologists went. They recommended urgent psychological support. They visited a friend who knew of the posts. No weapon was reported. No plan was reported.
record.purpose: Meta built its process to find posts that threaten violence or self-harm and to pass credible threats to the authorities of the user's country. This post went through that process.

data.retained_case_account: On Thursday 26 May 2022, two days after the Uvalde school shooting, Paraguay's Policía Nacional and Ministerio Público received an alert. It came from Meta's platform and the FBI office in Buenos Aires. A user in Paraguay had tagged the shooter, called himself his “fan” and said something similar could happen in Paraguay with more victims. Comisario Diosnel Alarcón's cybercrime department identified the Instagram profile as a 17-year-old in the “zona central”. He lived with a relative and was treated as a bullying victim. Police, prosecutors, the children's defender and psychologists visited the home and recommended urgent psychological support, and also visited a friend who knew of the posts. No weapon or plan was reported.

record.title: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts reached phones in Alanya seconds before a quake of magnitude 5.1 in the Mediterranean on 5 January 2022
record.summary: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System sent Android users near Alanya, Turkey, a warning seconds before a magnitude 5.1 offshore quake on 5 January 2022.
record.account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 an earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey, at a depth of roughly 40 km. The U.S. Geological Survey put its magnitude at 5.1. AFAD, Turkey's disaster and emergency agency, put it at 5.3. Google had introduced its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Turkey in June 2021. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day that the system sent Android users an alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake seconds before the shaking. The alert was a visual message with a sound. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage. They reported no injuries. İndigo Dergisi claimed on 5 January that the alert came about a minute ahead. On 7 January 2022 Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds. It reported that most users who posted about the alert said that they panicked. On 18 January 2022 NTV repeated the figure of about a minute. On 3 February 2022 Google said that the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir. In July 2023 BBC Newsnight reported that its reporters had spoken with hundreds of Android users in Adana, Iskenderun and Osmaniye. They found no one who received a warning from the same system before the main shock of 6 February 2023. Google's product lead told the BBC that he was confident that the system fired and sent alerts. Google staff published a study on 11 August 2026. They report that the system sent alerts to more than 16 million users for the magnitude 6.2 earthquake at Marmara Ereğlisi on 23 April 2025.
record.purpose: Google built the system to detect earthquakes with the accelerometers in Android phones and to warn users where shaking is expected, seconds before the slower destructive waves arrive. It covers quakes of magnitude 4.5 and above.
record.system: Android Earthquake Alerts System (crowdsourced phone-accelerometer detection; alerts for magnitude 4.5 and above)

data.retained_case_account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 a magnitude 5.1 (USGS; AFAD 5.3) earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey. Depth: roughly 40 km. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day on Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System, introduced in Turkey in June 2021. It sent an audible and visual alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake to Android users seconds before the shaking. Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds, while NTV and İndigo Dergisi claimed about a minute. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage or injuries. On 3 February 2022 Google said the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The alert was produced end to end by Google's system. Accelerometer triggers from many phones were combined on Google's servers to detect the quake and estimate its size. Alerts were pushed to phones in the expected shaking zone ahead of the slower S-waves. Google's own descriptions of this process do not use the words AI or machine learning. The reported lead time varies by outlet (seconds, about 10 seconds, about one minute); Google promises seconds.

fields.account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 an earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey, at a depth of roughly 40 km. The U.S. Geological Survey put its magnitude at 5.1. AFAD, Turkey's disaster and emergency agency, put it at 5.3. Google had introduced its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Turkey in June 2021. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day that the system sent Android users an alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake seconds before the shaking. The alert was a visual message with a sound. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage. They reported no injuries. İndigo Dergisi claimed on 5 January that the alert came about a minute ahead. On 7 January 2022 Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds. It reported that most users who posted about the alert said that they panicked. On 18 January 2022 NTV repeated the figure of about a minute. On 3 February 2022 Google said that the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir. In July 2023 BBC Newsnight reported that its reporters had spoken with hundreds of Android users in Adana, Iskenderun and Osmaniye. They found no one who received a warning from the same system before the main shock of 6 February 2023. Google's product lead told the BBC that he was confident that the system fired and sent alerts. Google staff published a study on 11 August 2026. They report that the system sent alerts to more than 16 million users for the magnitude 6.2 earthquake at Marmara Ereğlisi on 23 April 2025.

value.text: The alert was a single warning before one quake. The recorded follow-up is a BBC Newsnight investigation of July 2023. Its reporters found no one in three Turkish cities who received a warning from the same system before the main shock of 6 February 2023.
