produced_by: A magnitude 5.1 (AFAD 5.3) quake above the 4.5 alert threshold, centered about 57 km offshore and roughly 40 km deep. So the push alert could outrun the slower S-waves to the coast.

Enough Android phones near the epicenter with Earthquake Alerts on to trigger Google's server-side detection. Per Google's 3 February 2022 presentation it runs on Android 5.0 and later and users can switch it off.
Crowdsourced phone detection was the only input: Google partners with the ShakeAlert seismic network only in California, Oregon and Washington
must_hold: The server's magnitude and location estimate must be right and early. The 2025 Science paper reports only 36% of alert recipients got the alert before shaking.

The phone must have location and the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled

fields.summary: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System sent Android users near Alanya, Turkey, a warning seconds before a magnitude 5.1 offshore quake on 5 January 2022.
fields.account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 an earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey, at a depth of roughly 40 km. The U.S. Geological Survey put its magnitude at 5.1. AFAD, Turkey's disaster and emergency agency, put it at 5.3. Google had introduced its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Turkey in June 2021. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day that the system sent Android users an alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake seconds before the shaking. The alert was a visual message with a sound. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage. They reported no injuries. İndigo Dergisi claimed on 5 January that the alert came about a minute ahead. On 7 January 2022 Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds. It reported that most users who posted about the alert said that they panicked. On 18 January 2022 NTV repeated the figure of about a minute. On 3 February 2022 Google said that the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir. In July 2023 BBC Newsnight reported that its reporters had spoken with hundreds of Android users in Adana, Iskenderun and Osmaniye. They found no one who received a warning from the same system before the main shock of 6 February 2023. Google's product lead told the BBC that he was confident that the system fired and sent alerts. Google staff published a study on 11 August 2026. They report that the system sent alerts to more than 16 million users for the magnitude 6.2 earthquake at Marmara Ereğlisi on 23 April 2025.

produced_by: A magnitude 5.1 (AFAD 5.3) quake above the 4.5 alert threshold, centered about 57 km offshore and roughly 40 km deep. So the push alert could outrun the slower S-waves to the coast.

Enough Android phones near the epicenter with Earthquake Alerts on to trigger Google's server-side detection. Per Google's 3 February 2022 presentation it runs on Android 5.0 and later and users can switch it off.
Crowdsourced phone detection was the only input: Google partners with the ShakeAlert seismic network only in California, Oregon and Washington
must_hold: The server's magnitude and location estimate must be right and early. The 2025 Science paper reports only 36% of alert recipients got the alert before shaking.
Recipients must know what to do with seconds of notice. Hürriyet reported on 7 January 2022 that most users who posted about the Alanya alert said they panicked
The phone must have location and the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled

record.title: Houston Audubon times Lights Out alerts with BirdCast migration forecasts. The City of Houston proclaims Lights Out Nights in April 2021
record.summary: Houston Audubon issues Lights Out alerts when BirdCast's model forecasts heavy migration. Houston proclaimed Lights Out Nights on 9 April 2021. The sources show no drop in collisions.
record.account: BirdCast is produced by the Cornell Lab of Ornithology with Colorado State University and now Purdue University and the University of Illinois. It forecasts the nocturnal migration of birds from a model. The model was trained on 23 years of bird detections by weather radar, with reanalysis data on weather. Houston Audubon states that its staff use the BirdCast forecast maps to track migration predictions. They issue Lights Out Action Alerts when a chance of high migration coincides with weather events. Alerts ask residents to turn off nonessential lights from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. during spring and fall migration. They ask businesses to do the same. On 9 April 2021 the City of Houston proclaimed “Lights Out Nights” to help migrating birds. The Houston Chronicle reported on 19 April 2021 that Mayor Sylvester Turner had proclaimed Lights Out Nights for 19 April to 7 May, the span that Houston Audubon recommended. The Chronicle reported that the Cornell Lab and Colorado State University share BirdCast maps with Houston Audubon to predict when birds will pass through. In June 2021 BirdCast scientists and their co-authors published a separate study of 21 years of collisions in Chicago. They estimated that halving the lighted area of windows cuts collisions 11-fold in spring. In fall it cuts them 6-fold. On 17 April 2022 Houston-area cities asked businesses to go Lights Out for birds. The request extended to residents. On 25 August 2023 a statewide Lights Out gathering took place at Texas A&M University. Houston Audubon has not documented fewer collisions in Houston.
record.purpose: Cornell and its partners built BirdCast to forecast how many birds migrate each night, from weather radar and weather models. Cities, building owners and residents can then dim lights on busy nights.

fields.account: BirdCast is produced by the Cornell Lab of Ornithology with Colorado State University and now Purdue University and the University of Illinois. It forecasts the nocturnal migration of birds from a model. The model was trained on 23 years of bird detections by weather radar, with reanalysis data on weather. Houston Audubon states that its staff use the BirdCast forecast maps to track migration predictions. They issue Lights Out Action Alerts when a chance of high migration coincides with weather events. Alerts ask residents to turn off nonessential lights from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. during spring and fall migration. They ask businesses to do the same. On 9 April 2021 the City of Houston proclaimed “Lights Out Nights” to help migrating birds. The Houston Chronicle reported on 19 April 2021 that Mayor Sylvester Turner had proclaimed Lights Out Nights for 19 April to 7 May, the span that Houston Audubon recommended. The Chronicle reported that the Cornell Lab and Colorado State University share BirdCast maps with Houston Audubon to predict when birds will pass through. In June 2021 BirdCast scientists and their co-authors published a separate study of 21 years of collisions in Chicago. They estimated that halving the lighted area of windows cuts collisions 11-fold in spring. In fall it cuts them 6-fold. On 17 April 2022 Houston-area cities asked businesses to go Lights Out for birds. The request extended to residents. On 25 August 2023 a statewide Lights Out gathering took place at Texas A&M University. Houston Audubon has not documented fewer collisions in Houston.

record.title: Mayo Clinic credits AI with finding a woman's ruptured brain aneurysm in minutes before her emergency treatment
record.summary: Mayo Clinic says that unnamed AI algorithms let its care team find a woman's ruptured aneurysm in minutes. After surgery, the woman recovered.
record.account: On 24 February 2022, a woman became unresponsive after an aneurysm ruptured. Her care team at Mayo Clinic in Jacksonville, Florida, located the aneurysm within minutes. She underwent surgery, although her husband was initially told that she was unlikely to survive. After weeks of stabilization, she recovered. She spent 24 days in the hospital. On 28 October 2022 Mayo Clinic News Network reported the date of the stroke. It reported the length of her stay. That account does not mention AI. On 13 January 2025 Mayo Clinic Magazine reported that AI algorithms had allowed the care team to find her aneurysm in minutes. It reported that, two years after the stroke, she had resumed an active family life. It reported that she was taking part in the DISCOVERY study of post-stroke cognitive impairment. The software is not named in any source. No source holds a comparison of her care with care without it.

record.title: Staff stop a 76-year-old’s retirement savings from moving after TIAA’s AI flags a suspected scam
record.summary: TIAA's CEO said that an unnamed AI tool flagged a 76-year-old's unusual withdrawal. Staff then kept his retirement savings of more than $3 million from moving.
record.account: In a Forbes piece of 8 March 2026, Sastry Durvasula describes AI alerts that send suspected scams to customer care staff. The fraud department receives the alerts. Durvasula is TIAA's chief operating, information and digital officer. He does not mention the 76-year-old participant. On 17 June 2026 TIAA's CEO, Thasunda Brown Duckett, spoke on Fortune's podcast Fortune 500: Titans and Disruptors of Industry. She told Fortune that an AI alert helped staff stop a scam involving a 76-year-old participant’s retirement savings. Fortune's first article on the podcast, published the same day, reports that the participant was trying to withdraw his entire $3 million portfolio. It quotes Duckett as saying that AI by itself would not necessarily have protected him. Fortune published a lightly edited transcript of the interview on 22 June 2026. In the interview, Duckett says that a portfolio manager referred the concern to the fraud team, which spent hours with the participant and contacted his daughter. She says that the money did not move. In the transcript, she describes retirement holdings above $3 million and does not itemize an attempted transfer. No statement from the participant is supplied. No record of a transaction is supplied. No separate investigation is supplied.

fields.account: In a Forbes piece of 8 March 2026, Sastry Durvasula describes AI alerts that send suspected scams to customer care staff. The fraud department receives the alerts. Durvasula is TIAA's chief operating, information and digital officer. He does not mention the 76-year-old participant. On 17 June 2026 TIAA's CEO, Thasunda Brown Duckett, spoke on Fortune's podcast Fortune 500: Titans and Disruptors of Industry. She told Fortune that an AI alert helped staff stop a scam involving a 76-year-old participant’s retirement savings. Fortune's first article on the podcast, published the same day, reports that the participant was trying to withdraw his entire $3 million portfolio. It quotes Duckett as saying that AI by itself would not necessarily have protected him. Fortune published a lightly edited transcript of the interview on 22 June 2026. In the interview, Duckett says that a portfolio manager referred the concern to the fraud team, which spent hours with the participant and contacted his daughter. She says that the money did not move. In the transcript, she describes retirement holdings above $3 million and does not itemize an attempted transfer. No statement from the participant is supplied. No record of a transaction is supplied. No separate investigation is supplied.

record.title: A Tesla Cybertruck on Full Self-Driving (Supervised) may have detected that its driver had passed out on a freeway. It may have pulled onto the shoulder with its hazards on. It may then have driven him to an emergency room (18 February 2026)
record.summary: Rishi Vohra wrote that Tesla's Full Self-Driving pulled his Cybertruck onto a freeway shoulder after he passed out on 18 February 2026. No vehicle data has been published.
record.account: In an X post of 19 February 2026, Rishi Vohra wrote that he passed out while driving on 18 February. He was on a freeway in his Tesla Cybertruck, mid-call with his wife. He wrote that he had passed out after a severe allergic reaction. It followed a 17-hour unintentional fast. He had also taken medicine. He wrote that Full Self-Driving was engaged. He wrote that its driver monitoring system detected his loss of consciousness. By his account the truck slowed. It put on hazards. It pulled onto the shoulder without a crash. His wife used Life360 to send emergency services, who reached him in five minutes. He wrote that the car then drove him to an emergency room. He was stabilized there overnight. He was discharged on 19 February. Elon Musk replied “Glad you're ok!”. By 29 October 2026 no vehicle data had been published. No official confirmation had appeared. No account of the event had come from the police. None had come from a hospital. None had come from Tesla.
record.purpose: Tesla built Full Self-Driving (Supervised) to assist a driver, and Storyboard18 notes that the system still requires the driver's supervision. A camera in the cabin monitors the driver. Vohra credits that monitoring with detecting his loss of consciousness, and the system with slowing, putting on hazards and pulling onto the shoulder. Tesla has not said whether it designed the stop as a fallback for an unresponsive driver. The later drive to the emergency room used the system's ordinary driving from point to point.
record.system: Tesla Full Self-Driving (Supervised) with cabin driver monitoring, on a Tesla Cybertruck as described by the driver and Teslarati
record.model_version: Not reported; Vohra wrote only that Full Self-Driving was engaged, and Teslarati calls it FSD Supervised on a Cybertruck

ratings.reason: By Vohra's own post, the truck slowed and pulled onto the freeway shoulder while he was unconscious, with no crash. That is a serious harm averted in time. No vehicle data or official report confirms it.

data.retained_case_account: In an X post of 19 February 2026, Rishi Vohra wrote that he passed out while driving on 18 February. He was on a freeway in his Tesla Cybertruck, mid-call with his wife. He had passed out after a severe allergic reaction, following a 17-hour unintentional fast and medicine. Full Self-Driving (Supervised) was engaged, he wrote. Its driver monitoring system detected his loss of consciousness. The truck slowed, put on hazards and pulled onto the shoulder without a crash. His wife used Life360 to send emergency services, who reached him in five minutes. The car drove him to an emergency room, where he was stabilized overnight and discharged on 19 February. Musk replied “Glad you're ok!”. No vehicle data or official confirmation has been published.

fields.account: In an X post of 19 February 2026, Rishi Vohra wrote that he passed out while driving on 18 February. He was on a freeway in his Tesla Cybertruck, mid-call with his wife. He wrote that he had passed out after a severe allergic reaction. It followed a 17-hour unintentional fast. He had also taken medicine. He wrote that Full Self-Driving was engaged. He wrote that its driver monitoring system detected his loss of consciousness. By his account the truck slowed. It put on hazards. It pulled onto the shoulder without a crash. His wife used Life360 to send emergency services, who reached him in five minutes. He wrote that the car then drove him to an emergency room. He was stabilized there overnight. He was discharged on 19 February. Elon Musk replied “Glad you're ok!”. By 29 October 2026 no vehicle data had been published. No official confirmation had appeared. No account of the event had come from the police. None had come from a hospital. None had come from Tesla.

record.title: Staff resuscitate an 85-year-old in time on 14 January 2026 after the thynC monitoring system flags ventricular tachycardia at 192 beats per minute on a general ward of Gwangju Hanguk Hospital
record.summary: On 14 January 2026 the thynC monitoring system flagged ventricular tachycardia in an 85-year-old on a general ward in Gwangju. Staff resuscitated the patient.
record.account: On 9 January 2026 thynC began monitoring an 85-year-old patient on a general ward of Gwangju Hanguk Hospital (광주한국병원) in Gwangju, South Korea. The patient had cardiovascular risk factors at admission. On 14 January 2026 at about 3:10 p.m., the patient's heart rate climbed to 192 beats per minute. thynC's remote central monitor showed ventricular tachycardia, a precursor sign of cardiac arrest. It alarmed. Staff who ran to the room found seizure-like movements. They found reduced consciousness. They found no spontaneous breathing. They performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation. They gave artificial respiration. The heartbeat returned. Circulation returned. The patient was moved to intensive care. Daewoong Pharmaceutical, which supplies thynC, announced the rescue on 11 February 2026 with statements from the hospital's directors and nursing manager. The ThynC patch is made by Seers Technology of Seongnam. A study published in March 2024 by Seers staff and hospital cardiologists found that the patch matched conventional telemetry in 80 cardiology inpatients with less signal loss. Every article of 11 February 2026 on the Gwangju patient repeats the Daewoong announcement. No other account has appeared. On 19 June 2026 Asia Economy reported that Daewoong had completed thynC installations covering 558 beds at Chonnam National University Hospital and Hwasun Chonnam National University Hospital.
record.purpose: Seers Technology built thynC, which Daewoong Pharmaceutical supplies, to monitor patients on general wards as closely as in intensive care. Wearable devices measure the electrocardiogram, heart rate and respiratory rate, and the system sends an alarm to a central monitor when an abnormal sign appears. The head of Daewoong's hospital division says that thynC is built to detect changes in a patient's condition early and help medical staff respond quickly.

data.retained_case_account: On 14 January 2026 at about 3:10 p.m., an 85-year-old patient's heart rate climbed to 192 beats per minute. The patient was on a general ward of Gwangju Hanguk Hospital (광주한국병원) in Gwangju, South Korea. thynC had monitored the patient since 9 January because of cardiovascular risk factors at admission. thynC's remote central monitor flagged ventricular tachycardia, a precursor sign of cardiac arrest, and alarmed. Staff who ran to the room found seizure-like movements, reduced consciousness and no spontaneous breathing. They performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and artificial respiration. The heartbeat and circulation returned, and the patient was moved to intensive care. Daewoong Pharmaceutical, which supplies thynC, announced the case on 11 February 2026 with statements from the hospital's directors and nursing manager.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The system's contribution was detection and summons. The wearable ECG stream showed the heart rate climbing to 192 beats per minute. The remote central monitor identified ventricular tachycardia and raised an alarm. The attending director says that is how staff learned of it at once and reached the bedside to begin CPR within the golden time. The resuscitation itself was done by people. The counterfactual rests on the hospital's framing that general-ward patients are not under continuous observation and that deterioration can be noticed late. How long this patient would otherwise have gone unobserved is not recorded. No medical record or independent assessment has been published. The case reached the press through a Daewoong Pharmaceutical announcement of 11 February 2026.

fields.account: On 9 January 2026 thynC began monitoring an 85-year-old patient on a general ward of Gwangju Hanguk Hospital (광주한국병원) in Gwangju, South Korea. The patient had cardiovascular risk factors at admission. On 14 January 2026 at about 3:10 p.m., the patient's heart rate climbed to 192 beats per minute. thynC's remote central monitor showed ventricular tachycardia, a precursor sign of cardiac arrest. It alarmed. Staff who ran to the room found seizure-like movements. They found reduced consciousness. They found no spontaneous breathing. They performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation. They gave artificial respiration. The heartbeat returned. Circulation returned. The patient was moved to intensive care. Daewoong Pharmaceutical, which supplies thynC, announced the rescue on 11 February 2026 with statements from the hospital's directors and nursing manager. The ThynC patch is made by Seers Technology of Seongnam. A study published in March 2024 by Seers staff and hospital cardiologists found that the patch matched conventional telemetry in 80 cardiology inpatients with less signal loss. Every article of 11 February 2026 on the Gwangju patient repeats the Daewoong announcement. No other account has appeared. On 19 June 2026 Asia Economy reported that Daewoong had completed thynC installations covering 558 beds at Chonnam National University Hospital and Hwasun Chonnam National University Hospital.

ratings.reason: The hospital reports that the alarm brought staff to a patient in ventricular tachycardia who had stopped breathing. Resuscitation within the golden time restored heartbeat and circulation before the patient went to intensive care. That is a serious condition resolved in time. Survival to discharge and the neurological outcome are not reported, so the hospital's account does not show that a life was preserved.

fields.purpose: Seers Technology built thynC, which Daewoong Pharmaceutical supplies, to monitor patients on general wards as closely as in intensive care. Wearable devices measure the electrocardiogram, heart rate and respiratory rate, and the system sends an alarm to a central monitor when an abnormal sign appears. The head of Daewoong's hospital division says that thynC is built to detect changes in a patient's condition early and help medical staff respond quickly.

fields.summary: On 14 January 2026 the thynC monitoring system flagged ventricular tachycardia in an 85-year-old on a general ward in Gwangju. Staff resuscitated the patient.
fields.account: On 9 January 2026 thynC began monitoring an 85-year-old patient on a general ward of Gwangju Hanguk Hospital (광주한국병원) in Gwangju, South Korea. The patient had cardiovascular risk factors at admission. On 14 January 2026 at about 3:10 p.m., the patient's heart rate climbed to 192 beats per minute. thynC's remote central monitor showed ventricular tachycardia, a precursor sign of cardiac arrest. It alarmed. Staff who ran to the room found seizure-like movements. They found reduced consciousness. They found no spontaneous breathing. They performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation. They gave artificial respiration. The heartbeat returned. Circulation returned. The patient was moved to intensive care. Daewoong Pharmaceutical, which supplies thynC, announced the rescue on 11 February 2026 with statements from the hospital's directors and nursing manager. The ThynC patch is made by Seers Technology of Seongnam. A study published in March 2024 by Seers staff and hospital cardiologists found that the patch matched conventional telemetry in 80 cardiology inpatients with less signal loss. Every article of 11 February 2026 on the Gwangju patient repeats the Daewoong announcement. No other account has appeared. On 19 June 2026 Asia Economy reported that Daewoong had completed thynC installations covering 558 beds at Chonnam National University Hospital and Hwasun Chonnam National University Hospital.

record.title: Federal analysts detect anomalous Medicare billing. $4.41 billion in claims is held in escrow
record.summary: Justice Department analysts found anomalous Medicare billing through proactive data analytics. $4.41 billion was held in escrow. The software is unnamed. The department has not said that it used AI.
record.account: In June 2024 the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services called the 2023 billing volume for two types of intermittent urinary catheter codes significant. The agency called it a highly suspect anomaly. The American Hospital Association said that accountable care organizations had reported the suspect billing. On 18 June 2025 a federal indictment in the Eastern District of New York set out the alleged scheme. On 30 June 2025 the Department of Justice reported that its analysts had detected the anomalous billing in Operation Gold Rush. The Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services held $4.41 billion in escrow from about $4.45 billion scheduled for payment. Medicare paid about $41 million. Supplemental insurers paid about $900 million. The Department of Justice stated that the health agencies intended to seek the return of the escrow to the Medicare trust fund. In the same announcement the Department of Justice proposed an AI-enabled Data Fusion Center. The announcement does not establish that AI was used in the Gold Rush detection. On 3 February 2026 the Department of Justice announced that a Brooklyn banker had pleaded guilty to laundering proceeds of the Medicare fraud for the transnational criminal organization. It reported on 14 August 2026 that 35 people had been charged. It reported that 16 had been convicted, after a money-laundering guilty plea the previous day. These later announcements do not establish the final disposition of the $4.41 billion in escrow.

record.brief: The Department of Justice reported on 30 June 2025 that its analysts and their collaborators had detected anomalous Medicare billing in Operation Gold Rush. According to the department, health agencies stopped all but about $41 million of about $4.45 billion scheduled for payment. The agencies were the Office of Inspector General of the Department of Health and Human Services and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services. The $4.41 billion that was stopped went into escrow. The Justice Department said that the health agencies intended to seek its return to the Medicare trust fund. In its later announcements, the department does not say what finally became of that money.[1] Medicare supplemental insurers still paid about $900 million. The Justice Department credits the detection to proactive data analytics. In the same release, it announced plans for an AI-enabled Data Fusion Center. According to the American Hospital Association, accountable care organizations had also reported the suspect billing for intermittent urinary catheters. In June 2024 the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services called the 2023 volume of that billing highly suspect.[2] No source shows that AI flagged these claims. None says what share of the hold came from the analytics.[3]

Engaged by a double click of the stalk, it drove 13 miles to the VA emergency room without intervention and offered to park on arrival. record.title: Tesla Full Self-Driving v12 may have driven its owner 13 miles to a Veterans Affairs emergency room during an insulin-pump failure at 2 a.m. in North Carolina
record.summary: By his own uncorroborated account on X, Tesla Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v12 drove its owner 13 miles to a VA emergency room at 2 a.m. on 2 April 2024.
record.account: By his own account, a North Carolina television producer had severe dehydration at 2 a.m. on 2 April 2024. His blood glucose read 670 after his insulin pump malfunctioned. He says that he got into his Tesla Model Y and engaged a trial of Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v12, which had become available to him the day before. He says that it drove the 13 miles to the VA emergency room without intervention. He says that it offered to park. Il Fatto Quotidiano names the hospital as the Charles George VA Medical Center in Asheville. He reports a mild heart attack and discharge with no restrictions. He posted this account on X on 10 April 2024. Tesla and Elon Musk reposted it on 11 April 2024. No hospital or official source has confirmed it. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has an Office of Defects Investigation. That office raised the owner's post with Tesla at a meeting on 15 April 2024. It raised it again in an email of 14 May 2024. It wrote that Tesla's repost conflicted with Tesla's own message that drivers must keep control. NHTSA published the email in November 2024. It did not rule on whether the drive took place. Accounts by other owners of similar rescues, dated 15 November 2025 and 18 February 2026, appeared in 2026.
record.purpose: Tesla built Full Self-Driving (Supervised) to drive a Tesla to a chosen destination while an attentive driver supervises it. Tesla does not intend it for a driver impaired by a medical emergency. The Hindustan Times notes that the system depends on the driver stepping in when needed. A Tesla owner quoted by Tesla Oracle calls it a Level 2 system, which requires hands on the wheel and eyes on the road even when active.
record.system: Tesla Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v12 on a Tesla Model Y
record.model_version: FSD v12 (Supervised), unlocked on the car on 1 April 2024 per the owner and Tesla Oracle; the exact build is not stated (The Driven describes the then-current release as 12.3.3)

data.answer:
By his own X account, FSD v12 drove its owner 13 miles to a VA emergency room at 2 a.m. on 2 April 2024; uncorroborated.

The retained story rests on the driver's post and its republication. Vehicle logs, hospital confirmation, and a comparison with emergency transport are absent from the retained evidence. Reposts by Tesla or Musk add no independent verification.

The only description of what FSD did is the owner's. Engaged by a double click of the stalk, it drove 13 miles to the VA emergency room without intervention and offered to park on arrival. No Tesla vehicle data, dashcam footage, hospital record, emergency-service log or official statement has been found. No outlet reports having interviewed him or the hospital. Tesla's corporate account and Elon Musk reposted the story on 11 April 2024 but added no facts. The photos attached to the post are two hospital-bed selfies and a night shot of a Model Y in a wet car park. They show no route, timestamp or hospital name. Some syndicated coverage garbles the story (Sky TG24 places him in Virginia and describes low blood sugar). The counterfactual, calling emergency services, driving himself or not reaching care, is unexamined. Commenters cited by Il Fatto Quotidiano argued he should have called for help.

fields.account: By his own account, a North Carolina television producer had severe dehydration at 2 a.m. on 2 April 2024. His blood glucose read 670 after his insulin pump malfunctioned. He says that he got into his Tesla Model Y and engaged a trial of Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v12, which had become available to him the day before. He says that it drove the 13 miles to the VA emergency room without intervention. He says that it offered to park. Il Fatto Quotidiano names the hospital as the Charles George VA Medical Center in Asheville. He reports a mild heart attack and discharge with no restrictions. He posted this account on X on 10 April 2024. Tesla and Elon Musk reposted it on 11 April 2024. No hospital or official source has confirmed it. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has an Office of Defects Investigation. That office raised the owner's post with Tesla at a meeting on 15 April 2024. It raised it again in an email of 14 May 2024. It wrote that Tesla's repost conflicted with Tesla's own message that drivers must keep control. NHTSA published the email in November 2024. It did not rule on whether the drive took place. Accounts by other owners of similar rescues, dated 15 November 2025 and 18 February 2026, appeared in 2026.

He says that it drove the 13 miles to the VA emergency room without intervention. He says that it offered to park. Il Fatto Quotidiano names the hospital as the Charles George VA Medical Center in Asheville. He reports a mild heart attack and discharge with no restrictions. He posted this account on X on 10 April 2024. Tesla and Elon Musk reposted it on 11 April 2024. No hospital or official source has confirmed it. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has an Office of Defects Investigation. That office raised the owner's post with Tesla at a meeting on 15 April 2024. It raised it again in an email of 14 May 2024. It wrote that Tesla's repost conflicted with Tesla's own message that drivers must keep control. NHTSA published the email in November 2024. It did not rule on whether the drive took place. Accounts by other owners of similar rescues, dated 15 November 2025 and 18 February 2026, appeared in 2026.

record.title: An early resistance warning helped doctors change a woman’s antibiotic
record.summary: China Medical University Hospital’s Intelligent Anti-Microbial System flagged ceftazidime resistance in 1 hour. Doctors changed a 78-year-old woman’s antibiotic before she recovered.
record.account: A 78-year-old woman at China Medical University Hospital developed severe pneumonia during a prolonged admission. The hospital says that the pneumonia began at the end of May 2022. It says that she developed sepsis from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia on 2 June 2022. The hospital’s Intelligent Anti-Microbial System predicted within an hour that her Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolate resisted ceftazidime. It suggested levofloxacin. Hospital clinicians said that conventional susceptibility testing takes two to three days. The clinicians changed the antibiotic in June. The hospital reported that she recovered and went home in late July 2022, weeks after the switch. The account concerns one patient. The hospital's figure of more than 100,000 uses of the platform describes the wider service, not demonstrated recoveries. On 27 December 2022 the Ministry of Health and Welfare's Fengyuan Hospital signed a memorandum to adopt the platform. In a systematic review published on 30 September 2026, independent reviewers rated the hospital's own before-after study of the platform at serious risk of bias because it had no concurrent control group.

record.brief: A 78-year-old woman at China Medical University Hospital in Taichung developed severe pneumonia during a prolonged admission. Within an hour, the hospital's Intelligent Anti-Microbial System predicted from a bacterial mass spectrum that her Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolate resisted ceftazidime. It suggested levofloxacin. Po-Ren Hsueh, a vice-superintendent of the hospital, said that conventional susceptibility testing takes two to three days.[1] Clinicians changed the antibiotic in June 2022. The hospital reported that she recovered and went home in late July 2022.[2] The benefit rests on one patient. Every account of her comes from the hospital and its staff. Researchers with no tie to the hospital published a paper on 30 September 2026. They rated the hospital's own before-after study of the platform at serious risk of bias. They cited its lack of a concurrent control group.[3] The hospital counts more than 100,000 uses of the platform. That count covers the wider service and includes no number of recoveries.[4] The hospital's account supports an earlier change of antibiotic. None of the sources establishes that the prediction saved her life.

display.answer: Observed June 2022. The benefit is the switch of antibiotic after the platform flagged resistance. The hospital says that pneumonia set in at the end of May 2022, and a photo caption in the same release says that the patient developed sepsis from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia on 2 June 2022. produced_by: The hospital's own laboratory identifies isolates by MALDI-TOF, so a spectrum exists as soon as a culture grows

The platform returns the resistance prediction and a suggested alternative to the treating team within an hour
must_hold: The organism and antibiotic are ones the model was trained for

details.label: Contribution of the AI
details.value: The evidence is limited to the maker's account. On its page, Vyntra credits each block to its AI risk models detecting variables outside the customer's or bank's usual profile. Without a customer, bank, date or official record, Vyntra's page cannot show whether the models produced the outcome or whether staff or other controls did. The AI's contribution is not established.

record.title: Vyntra, formerly NetGuardians, says that its AI risk models blocked fraudulent payments at unnamed banks, including a USD 500,000 ATM scheme
record.summary: Vyntra credits its AI risk models with blocking payments of USD 7,500 to CHF 1,000,000. It credits them with stopping a USD 500,000 (KSh 58 million) ATM fraud that ended in arrests.
record.account: The metadata of Vyntra's “Fraud Cases” page dates it to 4 April 2022. The cases themselves are undated. On the page, Vyntra states that “Our solutions stop the fraud before the money leaves the bank”. It lists about two dozen short case studies at unnamed banks. In one, an account takeover after pharming was stopped before a CHF 19,990 payment. In another, an impersonation led a bank employee to validate a CHF 1,000,000 transaction, which was blocked because the beneficiary was unusual at bank level. Other cases involve voice phishing, fake technical support, impersonation of a chief executive, business email compromise, romance scams and redirected invoices. On the page, Vyntra says that payments of EUR 22,114, EUR 33,170, USD 7,500, GBP 21,000, EUR 125,000, EUR 170,000, USD 100,000, USD 170,000 and USD 850,000 were stopped in these cases. In each, variables of the e-banking payment (beneficiary, country, amount, currency, browser, screen resolution, language) did not match a usual profile. In some cases the profile was the customer's. In others it was the bank's. There are two internal-fraud cases. In one case “fraudsters were arrested while attempting to withdraw USD 500,000 (KSh 58 million) from the second bank's ATMs”. The models had flagged the unusual timing of withdrawals. They had flagged their unusual frequency. NetGuardians, a Swiss company, merged with Belgium's Intix to form Vyntra in June 2025 (FinTech Global, 19 June 2025). “NetGuardians solution” still appears in one entry on the page. On the current page, the CHF 19,990 example is placed in Switzerland. No customer on the page is identified. No bank on the page is identified. The page supplies no dated event, no finding by a regulator and no court record. The page is the vendor's own account. In a separate, undated case study, Vyntra names Sidian Bank in Nairobi as a client from April 2019. In it, Sidian's head of internal audit, Peter Karichu, says that the software flagged rapid ATM withdrawals one weekend in mid-December 2019. He says that the fraudsters were arrested at another bank. Vyntra gives no amount for that case. The Sidian case may or may not be the KSh 58 million case.
record.purpose: Vyntra built its risk models to score payments and e-banking sessions against customer and bank profiles in real time and block fraudulent transfers.

record.deployer: Unnamed client banks
record.location: Not stated; amounts are given in Swiss francs, euros, pounds, US dollars and Kenyan shillings

ratings.reason: The vendor describes customers whose transfers of EUR 125,000 and USD 170,000 to fraudsters were blocked, a serious loss averted in time for each, on the vendor's account alone.

data.retained_case_account: Vyntra's “Fraud Cases” page was published 4 April 2022 per its page metadata; the cases themselves are undated. It states that “Our solutions stop the fraud before the money leaves the bank” and lists about two dozen short case studies at unnamed banks. One is an account takeover after pharming stopped before a CHF 19,990 payment. Another is an impersonation that led a bank employee to validate a CHF 1,000,000 transaction, blocked because the beneficiary was unusual at bank level. There are vishing, tech-support, CEO-fraud, business-email-compromise, romance and invoice-redirection cases. Their payments of EUR 22,114, EUR 33,170, USD 7,500, GBP 21,000, EUR 125,000, EUR 170,000, USD 100,000, USD 170,000 and USD 850,000 were stopped. Transaction or e-banking session variables (beneficiary, country, amount, currency, browser, screen resolution, language) did not match the customer's or bank's usual profile. There are two internal-fraud cases. In one case “fraudsters were arrested while attempting to withdraw USD 500,000 (KSh 58 million) from the second bank's ATMs”. The models had flagged unusual timing and frequency of withdrawals. One entry still names “NetGuardians solution”, the Swiss company that merged with Belgium's Intix to form Vyntra in June 2025 (FinTech Global, 19 June 2025). No customer or bank is identified, and no dated event, regulator finding or court record is supplied. The current page labels the CHF 19,990 example as Switzerland. The page is the vendor's own account.

fields.summary: Vyntra credits its AI risk models with blocking payments of USD 7,500 to CHF 1,000,000. It credits them with stopping a USD 500,000 (KSh 58 million) ATM fraud that ended in arrests.
fields.account: The metadata of Vyntra's “Fraud Cases” page dates it to 4 April 2022. The cases themselves are undated. On the page, Vyntra states that “Our solutions stop the fraud before the money leaves the bank”. It lists about two dozen short case studies at unnamed banks. In one, an account takeover after pharming was stopped before a CHF 19,990 payment. In another, an impersonation led a bank employee to validate a CHF 1,000,000 transaction, which was blocked because the beneficiary was unusual at bank level. Other cases involve voice phishing, fake technical support, impersonation of a chief executive, business email compromise, romance scams and redirected invoices. On the page, Vyntra says that payments of EUR 22,114, EUR 33,170, USD 7,500, GBP 21,000, EUR 125,000, EUR 170,000, USD 100,000, USD 170,000 and USD 850,000 were stopped in these cases. In each, variables of the e-banking payment (beneficiary, country, amount, currency, browser, screen resolution, language) did not match a usual profile. In some cases the profile was the customer's. In others it was the bank's. There are two internal-fraud cases. In one case “fraudsters were arrested while attempting to withdraw USD 500,000 (KSh 58 million) from the second bank's ATMs”. The models had flagged the unusual timing of withdrawals. They had flagged their unusual frequency. NetGuardians, a Swiss company, merged with Belgium's Intix to form Vyntra in June 2025 (FinTech Global, 19 June 2025). “NetGuardians solution” still appears in one entry on the page. On the current page, the CHF 19,990 example is placed in Switzerland. No customer on the page is identified. No bank on the page is identified. The page supplies no dated event, no finding by a regulator and no court record. The page is the vendor's own account. In a separate, undated case study, Vyntra names Sidian Bank in Nairobi as a client from April 2019. In it, Sidian's head of internal audit, Peter Karichu, says that the software flagged rapid ATM withdrawals one weekend in mid-December 2019. He says that the fraudsters were arrested at another bank. Vyntra gives no amount for that case. The Sidian case may or may not be the KSh 58 million case.

record.title: A Yunnan man cancels a transfer of 190,000 yuan to a suspected romance scammer after WeChat Pay's “anti-fraud customer service reminder” interrupts it (reported 14 December 2021)
record.summary: WeChat says that its WeChat Pay anti-fraud reminder put a Yunnan man in touch with customer service. An agent advised him to cancel a 190,000 yuan transfer to a woman whom he had met online.
record.account: On 14 December 2021 WeChat announced that WeChat Pay had launched an “anti-fraud customer service reminder” (IT之家 and ChinaZ, 14 December 2021). ZOL reported it on 16 December 2021. When a payment is flagged as a risky transaction, the screen shows an “answer the reminder” button. The system connects automatically. Tencent Cloud Zhifu then provides online customer service to help judge the risk. The Yunnan story is WeChat's own example in that announcement. ChinaZ reports that a man in Yunnan had met a woman on a video platform. Within a week she asked to borrow 190,000 yuan for medical treatment. As he initiated the transfer, a WeChat Pay voice reminder appeared. In the announcement relayed by IT之家, WeChat says that the man received a call from WeChat Pay customer service while making the transfer. Customer service judged from experience that this looked like a dating scam. It explained the pattern to him. It advised him to cancel. He avoided a loss of 190,000 yuan. In September 2022 Xinhua reported that the reminder was still part of WeChat Pay's risk warnings.
record.purpose: Tencent built the reminder to warn WeChat Pay users during risky transactions and to connect them to online customer service that helps them judge the risk.

record.brief: On 14 December 2021 WeChat announced an “anti-fraud customer service reminder” for WeChat Pay. WeChat's example was a man in Yunnan, identified only by his surname.[1] ChinaZ reported that the man had met a woman on a video platform. Within a week she asked to borrow 190,000 yuan for medical treatment. As he began the transfer, a voice reminder from WeChat Pay appeared. He then received a call from its customer service. The agent on the call judged from experience that this looked like a dating scam and advised him to cancel.[2] He canceled the payment. The automated step in these accounts is the flagging of a risky transaction. Neither WeChat nor ChinaZ says how this transfer was flagged or whether any model was involved. WeChat and ChinaZ credit the agent's advice with his decision to cancel. No confirmation from the police or a bank is reported. No date is given for the transfer. In September 2022 Xinhua listed the reminder among WeChat Pay's risk warnings. It gave no figures on the reminder's effect.[3]

data.retained_case_account: According to WeChat (ChinaZ, 14 December 2021; ZOL, 16 December 2021), WeChat Pay launched an “anti-fraud customer service reminder”. When a payment is flagged as a risky transaction, the screen shows an “answer the reminder” button and the system connects automatically. Tencent Cloud Zhifu then provides online customer service to help judge the risk. ChinaZ reports that a man in Yunnan had met a woman on a video platform. Within a week she asked to borrow 190,000 yuan for medical treatment. As he initiated the transfer, a WeChat Pay voice reminder appeared. The customer service, judging from experience that this looked like a dating scam, explained the pattern and advised him to cancel. He avoided a loss of 190,000 yuan. The Monitor bundles this with Shanghai police figures for 2021 (115,000 scam calls blocked daily; 510 million yuan directly recovered). Xinmin attributes those to police, the communications administration and carriers without naming AI.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The automated part the sources describe is the flagging of a risky transaction. ChinaZ says the WeChat Pay customer service judged “from experience” that this was a dating scam, which reads as a human agent. Neither report says how the transaction was flagged or whether any model was involved. The advice, not the flag alone, led the man to cancel.

record.summary: Yeongdeungpo-gu says that its AI search system tracked a missing dementia patient across CCTV footage. It says that a patrol car found the patient about two hours after the report.
record.account: The Herald Business reported on 15 July 2026 on the Yeongdeungpo-gu district's account of how its Integrated Control Center found a missing dementia patient. The district said that a report arrived at about 3:57 p.m. on a Friday. It said that the police emergency dispatch center asked the control center to trace the patient. Operators entered the patient's description into the AI-based high-speed search system, which identified the patient near Yeongdeungpo Park. Officers arrived after the patient had moved on. The center kept tracking with the AI system. It spotted the patient again at about 5:50 p.m. A patrol car arrived three minutes after the center passed on the location. The patient was reunited with family about two hours after the report. The district built the system with a 200 million won grant from the Seoul Metropolitan Government. It has run the system since December 2025. The article rests on the district's announcement. It contains no reporting of its own. The article gives no baseline for a search without the system.

fields.account: The Herald Business reported on 15 July 2026 on the Yeongdeungpo-gu district's account of how its Integrated Control Center found a missing dementia patient. The district said that a report arrived at about 3:57 p.m. on a Friday. It said that the police emergency dispatch center asked the control center to trace the patient. Operators entered the patient's description into the AI-based high-speed search system, which identified the patient near Yeongdeungpo Park. Officers arrived after the patient had moved on. The center kept tracking with the AI system. It spotted the patient again at about 5:50 p.m. A patrol car arrived three minutes after the center passed on the location. The patient was reunited with family about two hours after the report. The district built the system with a 200 million won grant from the Seoul Metropolitan Government. It has run the system since December 2025. The article rests on the district's announcement. It contains no reporting of its own. The article gives no baseline for a search without the system.

record.title: As a NIO owner sleeps at 110 km/h on a rainy highway, his car's emergency pull-over function stops it while an SOS call wakes him
record.summary: The NIO World Model, NIO's assisted-driving software, pulled over a car whose driver fell asleep at 110 km/h on 1 June 2025. An SOS call woke him.
record.account: On 30 May 2025 NIO began pushing the first release of its NIO World Model to more than 400,000 Banyan-platform cars. NIO added an emergency autonomous pull-over function in that release. CnEVPost reports that before this release NIO cars could only slow in their own lane when a driver stopped responding. They could stop there. Around midnight on 1 June 2025, a NIO owner fell asleep driving at 110 km/h on a highway in rain in China. NIO's assisted driving was engaged. The emergency autonomous pull-over function triggered. An SOS call woke him. He posted a video on social media on 2 June. NIO founder William Li reposted it. He described the function. The car decelerated gradually. It changed to the rightmost emergency lane. It put on hazard lights. It made an SOS intervention. He stressed that assisted driving is not autonomous driving. No crash or injury was reported. The vehicle model has not been named. The highway has not been identified. On 28 January 2026 NIO rolled out a major update of the software to more than 460,000 Banyan-system vehicles. In October 2026 Kuai Keji relayed another NIO owner's account. She said that she was taken ill on an elevated road with her daughter. She said that assisted driving and the NOMI assistant got the car to the roadside. She said that they called for help.
record.purpose: NIO built an “emergency autonomous pull-over” into the first release of its NWM, which it pushed to cars on the Banyan platform from 30 May 2025. It works on a highway or urban expressway when the assisted-driving system detects an unresponsive driver. The car slows gradually, moves to the rightmost emergency lane, turns on its hazard lights and triggers an SOS call. CnEVPost notes that NIO cars previously could only slow down and stop within the current lane.

data.retained_case_account: Around midnight on 1 June 2025, a NIO owner fell asleep driving at 110 km/h on a highway in rain in China. NIO's assisted driving was engaged. The NIO World Model (NWM) emergency autonomous pull-over function triggered, and an SOS call woke him. NIO had begun pushing it to more than 400,000 Banyan-platform cars on 30 May 2025. He posted a video on social media on 2 June. NIO founder William Li reposted it, describing the function (gradual deceleration, a lane change to the rightmost emergency lane, hazard lights, SOS intervention). He stressed that assisted driving is not autonomous driving. No crash or injury was reported. The vehicle model and highway are not named.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The NWM-based assisted-driving system judged the driver unresponsive, ran the emergency pull-over and placed the SOS call that woke him. The car was already under assisted driving. Its specific contribution was therefore taking the car out of the live lane and rousing the driver rather than keeping it in lane. The sequence is known only from the owner's video as relayed by independent outlets. NIO's founder confirmed the function's design. No telemetry, police report or third-party verification was published.

fields.account: On 30 May 2025 NIO began pushing the first release of its NIO World Model to more than 400,000 Banyan-platform cars. NIO added an emergency autonomous pull-over function in that release. CnEVPost reports that before this release NIO cars could only slow in their own lane when a driver stopped responding. They could stop there. Around midnight on 1 June 2025, a NIO owner fell asleep driving at 110 km/h on a highway in rain in China. NIO's assisted driving was engaged. The emergency autonomous pull-over function triggered. An SOS call woke him. He posted a video on social media on 2 June. NIO founder William Li reposted it. He described the function. The car decelerated gradually. It changed to the rightmost emergency lane. It put on hazard lights. It made an SOS intervention. He stressed that assisted driving is not autonomous driving. No crash or injury was reported. The vehicle model has not been named. The highway has not been identified. On 28 January 2026 NIO rolled out a major update of the software to more than 460,000 Banyan-system vehicles. In October 2026 Kuai Keji relayed another NIO owner's account. She said that she was taken ill on an elevated road with her daughter. She said that assisted driving and the NOMI assistant got the car to the roadside. She said that they called for help.

They could stop there. Around midnight on 1 June 2025, a NIO owner fell asleep driving at 110 km/h on a highway in rain in China. NIO's assisted driving was engaged. The emergency autonomous pull-over function triggered. An SOS call woke him. He posted a video on social media on 2 June. NIO founder William Li reposted it. He described the function. The car decelerated gradually. It changed to the rightmost emergency lane. It put on hazard lights. It made an SOS intervention. He stressed that assisted driving is not autonomous driving. No crash or injury was reported. The vehicle model has not been named. The highway has not been identified. On 28 January 2026 NIO rolled out a major update of the software to more than 460,000 Banyan-system vehicles. In October 2026 Kuai Keji relayed another NIO owner's account. She said that she was taken ill on an elevated road with her daughter. She said that assisted driving and the NOMI assistant got the car to the roadside. She said that they called for help.

produced_by: The car was running the first NIO World Model (NWM) release with the “emergency autonomous pull-over” function, pushed to Banyan-platform cars from 30 May 2025.
Assisted driving was engaged on a highway, the function's stated operating domain (highways and urban expressways).
The assisted-driving system judged the driver unresponsive. He did not respond to the escalating alarms NIO describes. The pull-over and the SOS call therefore ran to completion.
must_hold: Driver monitoring must detect an unresponsive driver. The road must offer a rightmost emergency lane to stop in.
The SOS call needs working connectivity and a NIO emergency-response channel to reach the driver or a responder.
NIO and its founder present the function as a safety net within assisted driving, not autonomous driving. The driver remains responsible for staying awake.

echoes.setting: A NIO owner driving with her six-year-old daughter on an elevated road, probably in Hangzhou, fell ill and could not move. She wrote on social media that she switched on assisted driving and asked the NOMI assistant to call for help. She wrote that the car pulled over after a tunnel to wait for an ambulance. Kuai Keji reported her post on 15 October 2026 and did not give the day of the event.

record.title: ALERTCalifornia's AI cameras may have helped crews hold Kern County's Trotter Fire to 52 acres through rapid detection (August 2023)
record.summary: Microsoft, which funds ALERTCalifornia, says that the network's AI cameras helped crews hold Kern County's Trotter Fire to 52 acres in August 2023 by early detection. The software has not been named.
record.account: On 14 August 2023 KBAK (Bakersfield) reported a mandatory evacuation for Skyline Drive between Saddleback Drive and Cumberland Road in Bear Valley Springs. It gave an estimated 40 acres, forward progress stopped by 2:17 p.m. and the evacuation lifted by 3:12 p.m. The Kern County Fire Department said that the fire “was started by an electrical strike”. KBAK illustrated its report with photos credited to ALERTCalifornia. In the text, KBAK does not say how the fire was first reported. KGET blamed lightning in a headline the same day. In the same headline, KGET said that no homes were damaged. Cal Fire's archived incident record lists the Trotter Fire at Trotter Drive and Skyline Drive, west of Tehachapi, Kern County. It lists the Kern County Fire Department as the agency in charge. The fire was therefore not a Cal Fire incident. The record gives the start as 11:10 a.m. on 14 August 2023, which is 18:10 in Coordinated Universal Time. The fire burned 52 acres. In universal time the record dates its 100% containment to 17 August 2023. It gives the same date for its extinguishment. In local time it gives containment as 5:00 p.m. on 16 August 2023. The record lists the cause as under investigation. It holds nothing on how the fire was detected. It does not show how the fire was reported. Microsoft made a $5 million contribution to ALERTCalifornia that included a $3 million Azure grant, which ALERTCalifornia announced on 3 February 2026. Since February 2026 Microsoft has worked with ALERTCalifornia's research team through the Microsoft AI for Good Lab. In Microsoft's “Unlocked” feature “The first five minutes” (27 August 2026), Bruna Mori writes that in 2023 ALERTCalifornia's cameras with AI helped crews rapidly detect the fire. She writes that they then helped the crews contain the Trotter Fire at 52 acres. ALERTCalifornia founder Neal Driscoll estimates that without AI-powered imaging the fire may have spread to nearly 4,000 acres. Mori quotes Zachary Wells, deputy chief of the Kern County Fire Department. He holds a second post as deputy director of operations at ALERTCalifornia. The claim of AI detection is found only in Microsoft and ALERTCalifornia material. Fire agencies, regulators and independent news outlets have not mentioned AI detection in their accounts of the fire. None of them has said which agency received the alert. None has said when the alert came relative to 911 calls.

fields.account: On 14 August 2023 KBAK (Bakersfield) reported a mandatory evacuation for Skyline Drive between Saddleback Drive and Cumberland Road in Bear Valley Springs. record.title: Software at China Medical University Hospital in Taichung flags a severe blockage of a heart artery that a manual reading rated moderate
record.summary: China Medical University Hospital’s Exercise ECG AI-Assisted Interpretation System gave a man a 72 percent chance of severe narrowing. Angiography found a 99 percent stenosis.
record.account: A 75-year-old man with controlled hypertension woke one day with chest tightness. He had palpitations. Both symptoms were first taken for reflux. Liberty Times puts the onset in 2021. At China Medical University Hospital in Taichung, his exercise electrocardiogram was read manually. It was scored with the Duke Treadmill Score. That reading put him at moderate risk with about 50 percent narrowing. It called for follow-up only. The hospital's own Exercise ECG AI-Assisted Interpretation System, in use since May 2022, put the probability of severe narrowing (over 70 percent) at 72 percent. Cardiologist 吳宏彬 then ordered angiography. It found a 99 percent stenosis of the left anterior descending artery, which he stented at once. He said that the manual reading would have led to drug treatment. He said that it would have led to follow-up only. He put the man's chance of an acute infarction at 8 in 10. The man went home. His chest tightness improved markedly. The hospital presented the case on 28 December 2022. The date of the test is not reported. No date is given for the procedure. In three news reports of 28 December 2022, reporters carry the account of the hospital's doctors and quote no one outside the hospital.
record.purpose: The hospital's AI Center built the system to estimate from an exercise electrocardiogram whether a patient's coronary arteries are severely narrowed (over 70%). The hospital says that manual reading of a dozen tracings is slow and only 40–50% accurate.
record.system: 運動心電圖AI輔助判讀系統 (Exercise ECG AI-Assisted Interpretation System), China Medical University Hospital
record.model_version: Not reported. The hospital describes a deep-learning model that takes exercise-ECG signals at three time points plus 10 measured and 2 derived features (such as history and maximum workload), trained on nearly 1,000 exercise ECGs matched to catheterization data, accuracy about 80%, sensitivity 88%, in clinical use since May 2022; the authors' 2025 paper describes a convolutional recurrent network with three ECG slices and 12 features, AUC 0.83, sensitivity 0.89, specificity 0.60.
record.developer: China Medical University Hospital (中國醫藥大學附設醫院人工智慧中心), director 許凱程
record.deployer: China Medical University Hospital, Division of Cardiology (心臟血管系), Taichung

ratings.reason: A man with a 99 percent stenosis of the left anterior descending artery had it stented after the software flagged a 72 percent probability of severe narrowing. The manual reading of his exercise electrocardiogram had rated his risk moderate and would have left him to drug treatment and follow-up. The cardiologist put his chance of an acute infarction at 8 in 10. He said that the stent removed the risk of sudden death. The man left hospital, and his symptoms improved markedly. The hospital calls the case life-saving in its headlines. But the harm lay in the future, and the only account comes from the hospital that built the model, so no source shows that a life was saved.

The published model has a specificity of 0.60, so such flags are often false positives.

data.retained_case_account: A 75-year-old man with controlled hypertension woke one day with chest tightness and palpitations first taken for reflux. Liberty Times puts the onset in 2021. At China Medical University Hospital (CMUH), Taichung, his exercise electrocardiogram (ECG) was read manually with a risk score. That gave about 50% blockage, moderate risk, follow-up only. The hospital's own Exercise ECG AI-Assisted Interpretation System, in use since May 2022, put the probability of severe (over 70%) narrowing at 72%. So cardiologist 吳宏彬 ordered angiography, found a 99% stenosis of the left anterior descending artery and stented it at once. He went home, chest tightness resolved. The hospital presented it on 28 December 2022. Test and procedure dates are not reported.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The model read the exercise-ECG signals and report features. It returned a 72% probability of severe coronary narrowing, above the moderate-risk verdict of the manual reading and risk score. On that basis the cardiologist ordered angiography, which showed the 99% stenosis, and he stented it. The counterfactual rests on the treating cardiologist's statement, carried by three outlets and the hospital's release. He said the manual reading would have led to drug treatment and follow-up only. The hospital that says so also built the model. The dates of the reading and procedure are not reported. The published model's specificity of 0.60 means such flags are often false positives.

He said that the manual reading would have led to drug treatment. He said that it would have led to follow-up only. He put the man's chance of an acute infarction at 8 in 10. The man went home. fields.summary: China Medical University Hospital’s Exercise ECG AI-Assisted Interpretation System gave a man a 72 percent chance of severe narrowing. Angiography found a 99 percent stenosis.
fields.account: A 75-year-old man with controlled hypertension woke one day with chest tightness. He had palpitations. Both symptoms were first taken for reflux. Liberty Times puts the onset in 2021. At China Medical University Hospital in Taichung, his exercise electrocardiogram was read manually. It was scored with the Duke Treadmill Score. That reading put him at moderate risk with about 50 percent narrowing. It called for follow-up only. The hospital's own Exercise ECG AI-Assisted Interpretation System, in use since May 2022, put the probability of severe narrowing (over 70 percent) at 72 percent. Cardiologist 吳宏彬 then ordered angiography. It found a 99 percent stenosis of the left anterior descending artery, which he stented at once. He said that the manual reading would have led to drug treatment. He said that it would have led to follow-up only. He put the man's chance of an acute infarction at 8 in 10. The man went home. His chest tightness improved markedly. The hospital presented the case on 28 December 2022. The date of the test is not reported. No date is given for the procedure. In three news reports of 28 December 2022, reporters carry the account of the hospital's doctors and quote no one outside the hospital.

record.account: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber on 5 November 2026. It is a model trained to find security flaws, build working exploits and propose patches. OpenAI says that its researchers used the model in a targeted campaign against Firefox. The model found 81 previously unknown severe flaws, although earlier AI models had already tested the browser. OpenAI also says that the model showed 30 known issues to be more severe than first thought. The Decoder and TNW report that Mozilla accepted the reports and has shipped fixes. The Decoder links the claim to Mozilla's advisory for Firefox 159, announced on 27 October 2026. The advisory lists 167 fixed flaws. It credits OpenAI Codex Security with 34 of them, all rated high, and an OpenAI researcher with 7 more. The figure of 81 is OpenAI's own. The Decoder notes that no independent testing of the model has been published.

record.title: West Yorkshire Police's first deployment of live facial recognition in Huddersfield leads to three arrests over three days, including a domestic stalking suspect. It also leads to six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks
record.summary: West Yorkshire Police reported three arrests and six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks after NEC NeoFace live facial recognition issued nine alerts in Huddersfield on 12 to 14 August 2026.
record.account: The National Physical Laboratory tested NEC NeoFace V4 for the Metropolitan Police and South Wales Police in 2022. It reported in March 2023. It found that at a face-match threshold of 0.64 the system produced no false positives, with a true recognition rate of 79 percent. West Yorkshire Police records the same threshold of 0.64 for its deployments. The force identifies NEC NeoFace as the matching system. It states that trained officers review alerts before intervention. West Yorkshire Police used live facial recognition in Huddersfield from 12 to 14 August 2026. The force reported the arrests of three people: a domestic stalking suspect, a person wanted on a warrant and a shoplifting suspect. It reported six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks. Its deployment register records five alerts on 12 August. It records two on each following day. All nine were recorded as confirmed true alerts. The estimated numbers of faces seen were 5,824, 2,951 and 4,100, which total 12,875. These figures come from the force's own operational records. No independent study of these deployments has been found. The absence of recorded false alerts does not establish that the system missed no matches. The reported results do not establish a conviction. They do not establish a specific harm that was prevented. The force's register shows that the vans returned to Huddersfield town center on 8, 9 and 10 September 2026, with 16 alerts, all confirmed true. On a further return on 10 October 2026 they recorded no alerts.
record.purpose: West Yorkshire Police deploys the vans to match passersby against a watchlist of wanted people and suspects, so that officers can arrest or check them. The Examiner adds that the cameras also serve to find missing people, witnesses and victims.

data.retained_case_account: West Yorkshire Police used live facial recognition in Huddersfield on August 12–14, 2026. The force reported three arrests, involving a domestic stalking suspect, a person wanted on a warrant, and a shoplifting suspect, along with six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks. Its deployment register records five alerts on August 12 and two on each subsequent day. All nine were recorded as confirmed true alerts. The estimated numbers of faces seen were 5,824, 2,951, and 4,100, totaling 12,875. These are the force’s operational records, not an independent accuracy study. Zero recorded false alerts does not establish that there were no missed matches. The force identifies NEC NeoFace as the matching system and states that trained officers review alerts before intervention. The reported arrests and checks do not establish a conviction or a specific harm that was prevented.

fields.account: The National Physical Laboratory tested NEC NeoFace V4 for the Metropolitan Police and South Wales Police in 2022. It reported in March 2023. It found that at a face-match threshold of 0.64 the system produced no false positives, with a true recognition rate of 79 percent. West Yorkshire Police records the same threshold of 0.64 for its deployments. The force identifies NEC NeoFace as the matching system. It states that trained officers review alerts before intervention. West Yorkshire Police used live facial recognition in Huddersfield from 12 to 14 August 2026. The force reported the arrests of three people: a domestic stalking suspect, a person wanted on a warrant and a shoplifting suspect. It reported six Sexual Harm Prevention Order checks. Its deployment register records five alerts on 12 August. It records two on each following day. All nine were recorded as confirmed true alerts. The estimated numbers of faces seen were 5,824, 2,951 and 4,100, which total 12,875. These figures come from the force's own operational records. No independent study of these deployments has been found. The absence of recorded false alerts does not establish that the system missed no matches. The reported results do not establish a conviction. They do not establish a specific harm that was prevented. The force's register shows that the vans returned to Huddersfield town center on 8, 9 and 10 September 2026, with 16 alerts, all confirmed true. On a further return on 10 October 2026 they recorded no alerts.

record.title: Mozilla fixes 271 vulnerabilities in Firefox 150 that an early version of Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview identified in an initial evaluation, after a scan with Claude Opus 4.6 had led to 22 fixes in Firefox 148
record.summary: Mozilla says that Firefox 150 fixes 271 vulnerabilities that an early version of Claude Mythos Preview identified in an initial evaluation: 180 rated high, 80 moderate and 11 low.
record.account: Mozilla began working with Anthropic in February 2026. A scan of Firefox with Claude Opus 4.6 led to fixes for 22 security-sensitive bugs in Firefox 148. Mozilla then applied an early version of Claude Mythos Preview to Firefox. Firefox 150, released on 21 April 2026, fixes 271 vulnerabilities identified during that initial evaluation. In May, Mozilla's engineers wrote that 180 of the 271 were rated high, 80 moderate and 11 low, and that the model's reports produced few false positives. The same post says that Mozilla fixed 423 security bugs in its April releases in all, since its security team also hunts for bugs by fuzzing, by manual inspection and with other models, and that further fixes from the evaluation shipped in 149.0.2, 150.0.1 and 150.0.2. Anthropic cites the result in its Project Glasswing update. Privacy Guides reported the announcement on 22 April 2026. The count of 271 is Mozilla's own, and Mozilla has not described most of the individual bugs.

fields.account: Mozilla began working with Anthropic in February 2026. A scan of Firefox with Claude Opus 4.6 led to fixes for 22 security-sensitive bugs in Firefox 148. Mozilla then applied an early version of Claude Mythos Preview to Firefox. Firefox 150, released on 21 April 2026, fixes 271 vulnerabilities identified during that initial evaluation. In May, Mozilla's engineers wrote that 180 of the 271 were rated high, 80 moderate and 11 low, and that the model's reports produced few false positives. The same post says that Mozilla fixed 423 security bugs in its April releases in all, since its security team also hunts for bugs by fuzzing, by manual inspection and with other models, and that further fixes from the evaluation shipped in 149.0.2, 150.0.1 and 150.0.2. Anthropic cites the result in its Project Glasswing update. Privacy Guides reported the announcement on 22 April 2026. The count of 271 is Mozilla's own, and Mozilla has not described most of the individual bugs.

record.title: Argentina's fisheries secretariat says that it collected a fine for the Bao Feng without a capture after analysis with Skylight validated the detection
record.summary: Argentina collected a fine of 1,260 million pesos for illegal fishing by a foreign vessel that it never captured. Its fisheries secretariat says that analysis with Skylight validated the detection.
record.account: On 10 January 2026 the Prefectura Naval Argentina, the coast guard, detected the Vanuatu-flagged fishing vessel Bao Feng with its Sistema Guardacostas. The coast guard's own staff built that system. It placed the vessel in Argentina's exclusive economic zone for about an hour and a half at under 4 knots, a sign of fishing. Analysis on the Skylight platform of the Allen Institute for AI validated these data. On 26 March 2026 the Secretaría de Agricultura, Ganadería y Pesca reported that a fine of "$1.260 millones" (1,260 million pesos) had been collected with operating costs. The coast guard and the Subsecretaría de Recursos Acuáticos y Pesca worked on the case together. The secretariat calls it a historic precedent, a fine made effective without the physical capture of the vessel. Both agencies belong to the government that used the platform, so the release is the deployer's own account. It does not give the result of the Skylight analysis. The release does not show whether Skylight's machine-learning models took part. Diario Panorama reported the detection on 13 January 2026 without naming Skylight. It reported a fine.
record.purpose: The Allen Institute for AI built Skylight to detect suspicious vessel behavior and fishing at sea for agencies that enforce maritime law.

fields.account: On 10 January 2026 the Prefectura Naval Argentina, the coast guard, detected the Vanuatu-flagged fishing vessel Bao Feng with its Sistema Guardacostas. The coast guard's own staff built that system. It placed the vessel in Argentina's exclusive economic zone for about an hour and a half at under 4 knots, a sign of fishing. Analysis on the Skylight platform of the Allen Institute for AI validated these data. On 26 March 2026 the Secretaría de Agricultura, Ganadería y Pesca reported that a fine of "$1.260 millones" (1,260 million pesos) had been collected with operating costs. The coast guard and the Subsecretaría de Recursos Acuáticos y Pesca worked on the case together. The secretariat calls it a historic precedent, a fine made effective without the physical capture of the vessel. Both agencies belong to the government that used the platform, so the release is the deployer's own account. It does not give the result of the Skylight analysis. The release does not show whether Skylight's machine-learning models took part. Diario Panorama reported the detection on 13 January 2026 without naming Skylight. It reported a fine.

record.title: South Wales Police's Operator Initiated Facial Recognition app identifies a 38-year-old in Cardiff wanted on a 2012 European arrest warrant from Poland, who is remanded to Westminster magistrates
record.summary: South Wales Police's Operator Initiated Facial Recognition phone app matched a man in Cardiff to a European arrest warrant issued in Poland in 2012. He was remanded in custody (July 2025).
record.account: South Wales Police and Gwent Police are the first UK forces with the Operator Initiated Facial Recognition (OIFR) app. It lets an officer photograph a person on a police phone. The officer can then compare the image with a reference database. It is for when a person will not give true details. In 2022 the National Physical Laboratory tested the NEC NeoFace V4 algorithm that the app uses, under contract to the Metropolitan Police and South Wales Police. The app launched in December 2024. In one use, an officer in Cardiff identified a 38-year-old man wanted on a European arrest warrant since 2012. The warrant was for drug dealing in Poland. It covered an armed assault there on a police officer. He was remanded in custody to Westminster magistrates' court (Wales Online, 14 July 2025). The arrest date is not given. The forces report 50 searches in South Wales, which produced 10 arrests. They report six uses in Gwent, with three matches. One arrest followed. They cite the National Physical Laboratory testing, in which the correct match came top for people in the database (Wales Online). The accuracy claim rests on those 2022 tests. More than 500 officers had been trained by July 2025 (Emergency Services Times, 15 July 2025). In an audit report of August 2025, the Information Commissioner's Office said that it had observed the app at the two forces. It called the app a pilot in its infancy. In August 2026 the Information Commissioner's Office still described the app as a pilot in a limited number of forces. The extradition proceedings have no reported outcome.
record.purpose: South Wales Police and Gwent Police brought in the app for people who cannot or will not give their details. It confirms the identity of a person whom an officer suspects to be missing, at risk or wanted.
