In this report, the ICO establishes the pilot status and says nothing about arrests.
evidence.title: South Wales Police and Gwent Police: Data protection audit report, executive summary
evidence.quote: During the audit, the SWGP pilot scheme of Operator Initiated Facial Recognition Technology (OIFR) was also observed. Given the pilot is in its infancy, rather than make formal recommendations for SWGP to accept or reject upon the conclusion of this audit, the ICO has provided feedback based on what was observed for SWGP to incorporate into their learnings as the pilot scheme progresses.

evidence.citation: Information Commissioner's Office, Findings from ICO consensual audits on the use of facial recognition technology by police forces in England and Wales (audit outcomes report), August 2026. The ICO audited five forces, including South Wales and Gwent, between June 2025 and March 2026. It observed OIFR at one force and made no formal recommendations on it because the app was still a pilot.
evidence.title: Facial recognition technology in police forces: audit outcomes report
evidence.quote: OIFR is currently a pilot scheme taking in a limited number of police forces in England and Wales.

evidence.citation: Mansfield T, Facial Recognition Technology in Law Enforcement Equitability Study, Final Report, NPL Report MS 43, National Physical Laboratory, March 2023. NPL tested the system under a contract for the Metropolitan Police and South Wales Police, so it is a commissioned evaluator. It ran the OIFR tests offline on volunteer photographs, without officers in the loop.
evidence.title: Facial Recognition Technology in Law Enforcement Equitability Study, Final Report
evidence.quote: For every probe image submitted for OIFR in the evaluation, the correct reference identifier was returned at Rank 1 (i.e., as the top match).

data.retained_case_account: South Wales Police and Gwent Police are the first UK forces with the Operator Initiated Facial Recognition (OIFR) app. It lets an officer photograph a person on a police phone and compare the image with a reference database. It is for when the person refuses or gives false details. It launched in December 2024. More than 500 officers had been trained by July 2025 (Emergency Services Times, 15 July 2025). In one use, an officer in Cardiff identified a 38-year-old man wanted on a European arrest warrant since 2012. The warrant was for drug dealing and assaulting a police officer with a weapon in Poland. He was remanded in custody to Westminster magistrates' court (Wales Online, 14 July 2025). The forces report 50 South Wales searches producing 10 arrests, and six Gwent uses with three matches and one arrest. They cite National Physical Laboratory testing in which the correct match came top for people in the database (Wales Online). The arrest date is not given.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The app compared a photograph taken on a police phone to the reference database and returned the match that identified the man. Officers then confirmed the warrant and detained him. The force says National Physical Laboratory testing found the correct match returned as the top result for persons in the database. It says the app returns nothing for people not in it. Neither report names the vendor, the algorithm or a match score. Both rest on the force's figures.

record.title: The 1st Military Police Battalion arrests a woman wanted for drug trafficking after Vigia Mais MT facial recognition identifies her in downtown Cuiabá
record.summary: Mato Grosso's security secretariat reports that Vigia Mais MT facial recognition matched a woman wanted for drug trafficking in central Cuiabá on 12 July 2025. Police arrested her.
record.account: On 19 June 2024 the 9th Criminal Court Specialized in Drug Offenses issued a warrant for a woman for drug trafficking. On Saturday 12 July 2025 the video-monitoring system of Mato Grosso's State Secretariat of Public Security (Sesp) helped arrest her in downtown Cuiabá. It acted through the Vigia Mais MT program. Cameras in the city center identified her by facial recognition. After the system confirmed her identity, the monitoring center of the Integrated Public Security Operations Center (Ciosp) tracked her movements in real time. The center passed them to a team of the 1st Military Police Battalion, which made the approach. She was taken to a Civil Judicial Police unit. On 14 July 2025 Maria Klara Duque wrote a release about the arrest for the secretariat. Diário de Cuiabá and O Documento carried the text of that release on 14 July. CliqueF5 carried it on 15 July 2025. Diário de Cuiabá and CliqueF5 credit it to the secretariat. The secretariat adds that from April to July 2025 about 60 fugitives were located by state security forces. They were then arrested. By its account, the Vigia Mais MT program then covered 128 municipalities.
record.purpose: Mato Grosso's security secretariat runs Vigia Mais MT, its video-monitoring program. Its facial recognition compares faces seen on public cameras with wanted persons, so that Ciosp can direct patrols to them.

data.retained_case_account: On Saturday 12 July 2025 the video-monitoring system of Mato Grosso's State Secretariat of Public Security (Sesp) helped arrest a woman in downtown Cuiabá. It acted through the Vigia Mais MT program. She had an open warrant for drug trafficking. That is per the same text carried by Diário de Cuiabá and O Documento on 14 July and CliqueF5 on 15 July 2025. Cameras in the city center identified her by facial recognition. After the system confirmed her identity, the monitoring center of the Integrated Public Security Operations Center (Ciosp) tracked her movements in real time. It passed them to a team of the 1st Military Police Battalion, which made the approach. Her warrant had been issued on 19 June 2024 by the 9th Criminal Court Specialized in Drug Offenses. She was taken to a Civil Judicial Police unit. The reports add that from April to July 2025 about 60 fugitives were located and arrested by state security forces.

fields.account: On 19 June 2024 the 9th Criminal Court Specialized in Drug Offenses issued a warrant for a woman for drug trafficking. On Saturday 12 July 2025 the video-monitoring system of Mato Grosso's State Secretariat of Public Security (Sesp) helped arrest her in downtown Cuiabá. It acted through the Vigia Mais MT program. Cameras in the city center identified her by facial recognition. After the system confirmed her identity, the monitoring center of the Integrated Public Security Operations Center (Ciosp) tracked her movements in real time. The center passed them to a team of the 1st Military Police Battalion, which made the approach. She was taken to a Civil Judicial Police unit. On 14 July 2025 Maria Klara Duque wrote a release about the arrest for the secretariat. Diário de Cuiabá and O Documento carried the text of that release on 14 July. CliqueF5 carried it on 15 July 2025. Diário de Cuiabá and CliqueF5 credit it to the secretariat. The secretariat adds that from April to July 2025 about 60 fugitives were located by state security forces. They were then arrested. By its account, the Vigia Mais MT program then covered 128 municipalities.

fields.title: The 1st Military Police Battalion arrests a woman wanted for drug trafficking after Vigia Mais MT facial recognition identifies her in downtown Cuiabá
fields.headline: Police arrest a wanted woman in Cuiabá after face recognition flags her

fields.account: On 19 June 2024 the 9th Criminal Court Specialized in Drug Offenses issued a warrant for a woman for drug trafficking. On Saturday 12 July 2025 the video-monitoring system of Mato Grosso's State Secretariat of Public Security (Sesp) helped arrest her in downtown Cuiabá. It acted through the Vigia Mais MT program. Cameras in the city center identified her by facial recognition. After the system confirmed her identity, the monitoring center of the Integrated Public Security Operations Center (Ciosp) tracked her movements in real time. The center passed them to a team of the 1st Military Police Battalion, which made the approach. She was taken to a Civil Judicial Police unit. On 14 July 2025 Maria Klara Duque wrote a release about the arrest for the secretariat. Diário de Cuiabá and O Documento carried the text of that release on 14 July. CliqueF5 carried it on 15 July 2025. Diário de Cuiabá and CliqueF5 credit it to the secretariat. The secretariat adds that from April to July 2025 about 60 fugitives were located by state security forces. They were then arrested. By its account, the Vigia Mais MT program then covered 128 municipalities.

record.title: From clues in threat intelligence, Google's Big Sleep may have isolated the SQLite flaw CVE-2025-6965, which SQLite fixed in version 3.50.2 before any reported exploitation
record.summary: Google says that its Big Sleep agent isolated SQLite flaw CVE-2025-6965 from signs that attackers were preparing to exploit an unknown flaw. SQLite fixed it in version 3.50.2 on 28 June 2025.
record.account: The SQLite developers state that the flaw was fixed on 27 June 2025. They state that it needs an attacker who can inject arbitrary SQL into an application. The SQLite 3.50.2 release carrying the fix is dated 28 June 2025. SQLite's release log lists the corresponding fix. The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures record for the flaw, CVE-2025-6965, was published on 15 July 2025. In the CVE record, which it assigned, Google credits Vlad Stolyarov of Google's Threat Analysis Group with assistance from Google Big Sleep. In a post of the same day, Google says that, based on intelligence from Google Threat Intelligence, the Big Sleep agent discovered an SQLite vulnerability known only to threat actors. Google says that it was at risk of being exploited. A Google spokesperson told The Record that its threat intelligence group found artifacts indicating that a zero-day was being staged but could not identify the vulnerability. The spokesperson said that Big Sleep was used to isolate it. Google declined to name the actors. It declined to describe the indicators. The sources hold no independent confirmation that exploitation was imminent. The claim rests on Google. On 11 August 2025 the Big Sleep team reported a curl vulnerability, later published as CVE-2025-9086, which curl's maintainer confirmed. As of 28 October 2026 the CVE is not in the catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities kept by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.

fields.summary: Google says that its Big Sleep agent isolated SQLite flaw CVE-2025-6965 from signs that attackers were preparing to exploit an unknown flaw. SQLite fixed it in version 3.50.2 on 28 June 2025.
fields.account: The SQLite developers state that the flaw was fixed on 27 June 2025. They state that it needs an attacker who can inject arbitrary SQL into an application. The SQLite 3.50.2 release carrying the fix is dated 28 June 2025. SQLite's release log lists the corresponding fix. The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures record for the flaw, CVE-2025-6965, was published on 15 July 2025. In the CVE record, which it assigned, Google credits Vlad Stolyarov of Google's Threat Analysis Group with assistance from Google Big Sleep. In a post of the same day, Google says that, based on intelligence from Google Threat Intelligence, the Big Sleep agent discovered an SQLite vulnerability known only to threat actors. Google says that it was at risk of being exploited. A Google spokesperson told The Record that its threat intelligence group found artifacts indicating that a zero-day was being staged but could not identify the vulnerability. The spokesperson said that Big Sleep was used to isolate it. Google declined to name the actors. It declined to describe the indicators. The sources hold no independent confirmation that exploitation was imminent. The claim rests on Google. On 11 August 2025 the Big Sleep team reported a curl vulnerability, later published as CVE-2025-9086, which curl's maintainer confirmed. As of 28 October 2026 the CVE is not in the catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities kept by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.

record.title: By Skylight's account, its alerts led Argentina's Prefectura Naval to stop the Vanuatu-flagged XINRUN 579 on 5 January 2025, and the vessel paid a fine
record.summary: Skylight says that its speed alert led Argentina's coast guard to intercept a trawler on 5 January 2025. Its machine-learning fishing alert did too. Skylight also says that the vessel paid a fine.
record.account: On Sunday 5 January 2025 the Prefectura Naval Argentina (PNA), Argentina's coast guard, detected the Vanuatu-flagged trawler XinRun 579. It was in Argentina's exclusive economic zone off Caleta Olivia, Santa Cruz, sailing at under 6 knots. Under local rules, that speed is a sign of trawling. The coast guard vessel GC-25 Azopardo intercepted it. The captain was formally notified of an infraction under Law 24.922, which opened administrative proceedings (Agenda Malvinas, 8 January 2025, citing official information). Agenda Malvinas credits the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas. It does not mention Skylight. AI does not appear in its account. On 3 March 2025 NVIDIA wrote in a Developer blog post that the coast guard interdicted the vessel after Skylight alerted it. NVIDIA wrote that the coast guard later fined the vessel. Skylight, the free AI maritime-monitoring platform of the Allen Institute for AI, published its own account on 31 March 2025. A rule-based Speed Range Event first alerted the authorities. A Fishing Event alert from its machine-learning model came 40 minutes later. PNA analysts redirected a nearby coast guard vessel. Skylight says that the interception led to Argentina's first international electronic fine using AI-powered evidence. It says that the vessel paid the fine along with the operational costs. Skylight quotes a retired PNA captain who coordinates EICEMAR, an interdisciplinary team for the control of maritime spaces and their resources. It quotes the lead of the PNA's geographic information systems division. Both credit Skylight. The PNA release that Skylight links to cannot be found online. No archived copy has been found.

fields.account: On Sunday 5 January 2025 the Prefectura Naval Argentina (PNA), Argentina's coast guard, detected the Vanuatu-flagged trawler XinRun 579. It was in Argentina's exclusive economic zone off Caleta Olivia, Santa Cruz, sailing at under 6 knots. Under local rules, that speed is a sign of trawling. The coast guard vessel GC-25 Azopardo intercepted it. The captain was formally notified of an infraction under Law 24.922, which opened administrative proceedings (Agenda Malvinas, 8 January 2025, citing official information). Agenda Malvinas credits the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas. It does not mention Skylight. AI does not appear in its account. On 3 March 2025 NVIDIA wrote in a Developer blog post that the coast guard interdicted the vessel after Skylight alerted it. NVIDIA wrote that the coast guard later fined the vessel. Skylight, the free AI maritime-monitoring platform of the Allen Institute for AI, published its own account on 31 March 2025. A rule-based Speed Range Event first alerted the authorities. A Fishing Event alert from its machine-learning model came 40 minutes later. PNA analysts redirected a nearby coast guard vessel. Skylight says that the interception led to Argentina's first international electronic fine using AI-powered evidence. It says that the vessel paid the fine along with the operational costs. Skylight quotes a retired PNA captain who coordinates EICEMAR, an interdisciplinary team for the control of maritime spaces and their resources. It quotes the lead of the PNA's geographic information systems division. Both credit Skylight. The PNA release that Skylight links to cannot be found online. No archived copy has been found.

record.title: Kunshan police “AI police” models flag a mobile gambling ring at Zhouzhuang, where over 20 suspects are arrested on 10 September 2024, and trace a telecom fraud's card transfers to freeze 500,000 yuan within 10 minutes
record.summary: Kunshan police say that their “AI police” models found a mobile gambling ring that police broke up on 10 September 2024. The models traced a telecom fraud. 500,000 yuan was frozen within 10 minutes.
record.account: The “Kunpeng Squad”, 35 officers assembled in May 2024, built the “AI police” models for the Kunshan Public Security Bureau in Jiangsu. On 10 September 2024, the bureau broke up a gang running a mobile open-air casino in Zhouzhuang town. It arrested over 20 suspects. Modern Express reported that the “AI police” had found the ring (NetEase reprint, 6 October 2024). These are models that detect outdoor gambling from behavioral patterns in bulk data. In a telecom fraud handled by the Lujia police station, a victim lost 980,000 yuan. Suzhou Daily reports that the fraud case came earlier in 2024. The models traced three tiers of card transfers and froze 500,000 yuan within 10 minutes. They identified 87 suspect accounts within 8 hours. Nine suspects were arrested on the third day with 200,000 yuan recovered (Suzhou Daily via suzhou.gov.cn, 7 October 2024). The police say that the same work would once have taken five or six officers two weeks before the first arrests. The squad reports over 220 models. It reports 609 fraud cases solved over six months. It reports 32.47 million yuan recovered in the same period (both sources). All figures are the police's own.
record.purpose: The Kunshan police built the models to detect crime patterns and to trace funds for investigators. The bust and the freeze were that purpose.

data.retained_case_account: On 10 September 2024, the Kunshan Public Security Bureau in Jiangsu broke up a gang running a mobile open-air casino in Zhouzhuang town. It arrested over 20 suspects. Modern Express reported that the “AI police” had found the ring (NetEase reprint, 6 October 2024). These are models that detect outdoor gambling from behavioral patterns in bulk data. In a telecom fraud handled by the Lujia police station, a victim lost 980,000 yuan. The models traced three tiers of card transfers and froze 500,000 yuan within 10 minutes. They identified 87 suspect accounts within 8 hours. Nine suspects were arrested on the third day with 200,000 yuan recovered (Suzhou Daily via suzhou.gov.cn, 7 October 2024). The models were built by the “Kunpeng Squad”, 35 officers assembled in May 2024. They report over 220 models and, over six months, 609 fraud cases solved and 32.47 million yuan recovered (both sources). All figures are the police's own.

fields.headline: Police models in Kunshan flag a gambling ring

fields.account: The “Kunpeng Squad”, 35 officers assembled in May 2024, built the “AI police” models for the Kunshan Public Security Bureau in Jiangsu. On 10 September 2024, the bureau broke up a gang running a mobile open-air casino in Zhouzhuang town. It arrested over 20 suspects. Modern Express reported that the “AI police” had found the ring (NetEase reprint, 6 October 2024). These are models that detect outdoor gambling from behavioral patterns in bulk data. In a telecom fraud handled by the Lujia police station, a victim lost 980,000 yuan. Suzhou Daily reports that the fraud case came earlier in 2024. The models traced three tiers of card transfers and froze 500,000 yuan within 10 minutes. They identified 87 suspect accounts within 8 hours. Nine suspects were arrested on the third day with 200,000 yuan recovered (Suzhou Daily via suzhou.gov.cn, 7 October 2024). The police say that the same work would once have taken five or six officers two weeks before the first arrests. The squad reports over 220 models. It reports 609 fraud cases solved over six months. It reports 32.47 million yuan recovered in the same period (both sources). All figures are the police's own.

record.title: In response to a federal audit prompted by an ALICE alert, Brazil's highway department cuts almost R$100 million from a tender in Pará
record.summary: ALICE, the federal comptroller's AI alert tool, flagged a highway tender in Pará, Brazil. The auditors' findings led the contracting agency to cut almost R$100 million from the tender's budget.
record.account: Brazil's federal comptroller, the Controladoria-Geral da União, runs ALICE. The robot reads planning documents on Compras.gov.br with artificial-intelligence techniques. It reads the notices on the same site. It issues alerts about risk that auditors confirm. In May 2024 the Departamento Nacional de Infraestrutura de Transportes published Concorrência 154/2024, a federal tender for engineering works on roads. It covered the restoration of the BR-158 highway in Pará between kilometer 699 and kilometer 889.58. An ALICE alert led the comptroller's auditors to examine the budget. They questioned the price of the asphalt binder, the costs of the site, the costs of mobilization, the sizes of the trucks and other items. The department suspended the tender on 19 June 2024. It then corrected some findings. It justified the others. The final budget of 19 August 2024 cut the reference value from R$549.66 million to R$436.47 million. In audit report 1632530, published on 17 December 2024, the comptroller attributes almost R$100 million of the cut to its auditors' findings. In its statement of 30 December 2024 on the year's results, the comptroller reported that federal managers had adjusted the budget after the alert, reducing the reference value by about R$100 million. The comptroller named neither the contracting agency nor the date in that statement. In the same statement, it gives aggregates for 2024. It analyzed 118,069 procurement processes. It opened 206 preventive audits on purchases worth R$25.57 billion. It reports R$257.25 million saved in concluded audits. On 14 January 2025 the comptroller reported that ALICE alerts had led to audits of three federal hospital tenders in Rio de Janeiro. One was suspended. One was revoked. One was re-estimated.
record.purpose: The Controladoria-Geral da União built ALICE to screen federal procurement continuously and flag budget and pricing risks before contracting.

data.retained_case_account: In its 30 December 2024 statement on the year's results, the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU) reported on an alert from its ALICE robot. The alert led CGU auditors to examine the budget of a federal road-works engineering tender. Federal managers then adjusted it, reducing the reference value by about R$100 million (CGU audit report 1632530). The statement names neither the contracting agency nor the date of the case. Its “this year” wording applies only to a separate water-bottle example. The same release gives 2024 aggregates: 118,069 procurement processes analyzed and 206 preventive audits opened on purchases worth R$25.57 billion. It reports R$257.25 million saved in concluded audits. ALICE reads planning documents and notices on Compras.gov.br with artificial-intelligence techniques and issues risk alerts that auditors confirm.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The CGU states the chain explicitly: “A partir do alerta do ALICE, auditores da CGU examinaram a adequação de um orçamento de uma obra rodoviária, o que gerou ajustes efetuados pelos gestores federais.” The adjustment was made by managers after a human audit. ALICE's role was the initial alert. Developer and deployer are the same public body. The page is on record as an archived copy, because the live page was restricted during Brazil's 2026 electoral period.

fields.account: Brazil's federal comptroller, the Controladoria-Geral da União, runs ALICE. The robot reads planning documents on Compras.gov.br with artificial-intelligence techniques. It reads the notices on the same site. It issues alerts about risk that auditors confirm. In May 2024 the Departamento Nacional de Infraestrutura de Transportes published Concorrência 154/2024, a federal tender for engineering works on roads. It covered the restoration of the BR-158 highway in Pará between kilometer 699 and kilometer 889.58. An ALICE alert led the comptroller's auditors to examine the budget. They questioned the price of the asphalt binder, the costs of the site, the costs of mobilization, the sizes of the trucks and other items. The department suspended the tender on 19 June 2024. It then corrected some findings. It justified the others. The final budget of 19 August 2024 cut the reference value from R$549.66 million to R$436.47 million. In audit report 1632530, published on 17 December 2024, the comptroller attributes almost R$100 million of the cut to its auditors' findings. In its statement of 30 December 2024 on the year's results, the comptroller reported that federal managers had adjusted the budget after the alert, reducing the reference value by about R$100 million. The comptroller named neither the contracting agency nor the date in that statement. In the same statement, it gives aggregates for 2024. It analyzed 118,069 procurement processes. It opened 206 preventive audits on purchases worth R$25.57 billion. It reports R$257.25 million saved in concluded audits. On 14 January 2025 the comptroller reported that ALICE alerts had led to audits of three federal hospital tenders in Rio de Janeiro. One was suspended. One was revoked. One was re-estimated.

record.title: Minas Gerais court of accounts (TCE-MG) screens 2,297 tenders from August 2022 with Alice, whose alerts on 60 irregularities worth R$113.7 million receive 53 answers that lead to corrected notices worth R$91.7 million
record.summary: The Minas Gerais court of accounts screened 2,297 tenders from August 2022 with Alice, a system that analyzes tender notices. It obtained corrections of notices worth R$91,723,011.31.
record.account: The Tribunal de Contas do Estado de Minas Gerais (TCE-MG), the state court of accounts, is one of more than ten Brazilian courts of accounts that adopted Alice. Alice (Análise de Licitações e Editais) was created by the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU) and the Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU). In December 2022 the court published an audit of 2,297 tenders held in a single month, August 2022. Some were municipal tenders. Others were state tenders. The exact day is not given. The court gives the results in its own news item of 27 June 2023, which Atricon reproduced on 28 June 2023. The auditors detected 60 irregularities involving R$113,713,128.26. Of the 60 alerts sent to the audited bodies, 53 received answers that allowed control verification. Some irregularities were fixed in republished notices. Others were fixed through measures adopted for future tenders. As a result, the audit achieved corrections of notices worth R$91,723,011.31. The figures are aggregates presented by analysts Maria Aparecida Aiko Ikemura and Leonardo Alves Mateus to about 60 people from courts of accounts across Brazil. No individual tender is named. On 17 January 2024 Atricon reported that TCE-MG presented Alice and Solaris to the Espírito Santo court of accounts (TCE-ES). No adoption is reported. On 23 July 2025, O Fator reported that TCE-MG had built two tools of its own on the basis of Alice. Solaris screens purchase notices. Apolo screens engineering budgets. The court says that the two tools analyzed notices worth more than R$8.1 billion in 2025. It says that they helped correct these notices. One alert led the court to suspend a tender in Montezuma for R$4.3 million of alcoholic drinks. All of these figures come from the court.

data.retained_case_account: The Tribunal de Contas do Estado de Minas Gerais (TCE-MG) is one of more than ten Brazilian courts of accounts that adopted Alice. Alice is the Análise de Licitações e Editais system created by the CGU and the TCU. In December 2022 it published an audit of 2,297 municipal and state tenders held in a single month, August 2022. The exact day is not given. The court's own news item of 27 June 2023, reproduced by Atricon on 28 June 2023, gives the results. The work detected 60 irregularities involving R$113,713,128.26. 53 of the 60 alerts sent to the audited bodies received answers that allowed control verification. Irregularities were fixed in republished notices or measures adopted for future tenders. The audit achieved corrected notices worth R$91,723,011.31. The figures are aggregates presented by analysts Maria Aparecida Aiko Ikemura and Leonardo Alves Mateus to about 60 people from courts of accounts across Brazil. No individual tender is named.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: Alice produced the alerts on the 2,297 tenders. TCE-MG analysts forwarded 60 alerts and the audited bodies made the corrections. The AI role was detection and triage. The only sources are the deployer's own news item (TCE-MG, 27 June 2023) and Atricon's reproduction of it the next day. No audit report, tender or court decision is among the sources. TCE-MG did not build the tool (CGU/TCU did), so the statement is not vendor-authored. It is the user describing its own results.

fields.account: The Tribunal de Contas do Estado de Minas Gerais (TCE-MG), the state court of accounts, is one of more than ten Brazilian courts of accounts that adopted Alice. Alice (Análise de Licitações e Editais) was created by the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU) and the Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU). In December 2022 the court published an audit of 2,297 tenders held in a single month, August 2022. Some were municipal tenders. Others were state tenders. The exact day is not given. The court gives the results in its own news item of 27 June 2023, which Atricon reproduced on 28 June 2023. The auditors detected 60 irregularities involving R$113,713,128.26. Of the 60 alerts sent to the audited bodies, 53 received answers that allowed control verification. Some irregularities were fixed in republished notices. Others were fixed through measures adopted for future tenders. As a result, the audit achieved corrections of notices worth R$91,723,011.31. The figures are aggregates presented by analysts Maria Aparecida Aiko Ikemura and Leonardo Alves Mateus to about 60 people from courts of accounts across Brazil. No individual tender is named. On 17 January 2024 Atricon reported that TCE-MG presented Alice and Solaris to the Espírito Santo court of accounts (TCE-ES). No adoption is reported. On 23 July 2025, O Fator reported that TCE-MG had built two tools of its own on the basis of Alice. Solaris screens purchase notices. Apolo screens engineering budgets. The court says that the two tools analyzed notices worth more than R$8.1 billion in 2025. It says that they helped correct these notices. One alert led the court to suspend a tender in Montezuma for R$4.3 million of alcoholic drinks. All of these figures come from the court.

fields.summary: The Minas Gerais court of accounts screened 2,297 tenders from August 2022 with Alice, a system that analyzes tender notices. It obtained corrections of notices worth R$91,723,011.31.
fields.account: The Tribunal de Contas do Estado de Minas Gerais (TCE-MG), the state court of accounts, is one of more than ten Brazilian courts of accounts that adopted Alice. Alice (Análise de Licitações e Editais) was created by the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU) and the Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU). In December 2022 the court published an audit of 2,297 tenders held in a single month, August 2022. Some were municipal tenders. Others were state tenders. The exact day is not given. The court gives the results in its own news item of 27 June 2023, which Atricon reproduced on 28 June 2023. The auditors detected 60 irregularities involving R$113,713,128.26. Of the 60 alerts sent to the audited bodies, 53 received answers that allowed control verification. Some irregularities were fixed in republished notices. Others were fixed through measures adopted for future tenders. As a result, the audit achieved corrections of notices worth R$91,723,011.31. The figures are aggregates presented by analysts Maria Aparecida Aiko Ikemura and Leonardo Alves Mateus to about 60 people from courts of accounts across Brazil. No individual tender is named. On 17 January 2024 Atricon reported that TCE-MG presented Alice and Solaris to the Espírito Santo court of accounts (TCE-ES). No adoption is reported. On 23 July 2025, O Fator reported that TCE-MG had built two tools of its own on the basis of Alice. Solaris screens purchase notices. Apolo screens engineering budgets. The court says that the two tools analyzed notices worth more than R$8.1 billion in 2025. It says that they helped correct these notices. One alert led the court to suspend a tender in Montezuma for R$4.3 million of alcoholic drinks. All of these figures come from the court.

record.title: Philippine Red Cross activated its typhoon Early Action Protocol on a machine-learning forecast of impact from 510 before Storm Nalgae (October 2022)
record.summary: A machine-learning damage forecast from 510 met the early-action trigger on 27 October 2022. The Philippine Red Cross installed shelter kits for 78 Aurora households before Storm Nalgae.
record.account: The Philippine Red Cross approved its Early Action Protocol for typhoons in December 2019. Its model forecasts by impact. The Philippine Red Cross developed it with 510, an initiative of the Netherlands Red Cross. It applies machine learning to predict damage to housing in each municipality from typhoon forecasts. In 2021 the 510 model became the trigger model for the anticipatory action pilot of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) in the Philippines. The Central Emergency Response Fund funded the OCHA pilot with $7.5 million for the 2023 typhoon season. Under the protocol, early actions start when the forecast shows at least 10 percent of houses totally damaged in more than three municipalities 72 hours before landfall. As Tropical Storm Paeng (Nalgae) approached on 27 October 2022, the 510 forecast projected up to 10 percent shelter damage in priority municipalities. That met the trigger at 56 hours' lead time. According to the final report, the 56-hour lead time was granted as an exception. With anticipatory funds from the Disaster Response Emergency Fund of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, the Philippine Red Cross activated the protocol in Aurora Province. From 27 to 29 October, 40 workers distributed kits for strengthening shelters to 78 of 100 planned households in Dipaculao before landfall. They installed them. According to the same report, strong winds limited the distribution to 78 households. The onset of rain limited it. In its survey after the storm, the Philippine Red Cross reports that all 78 kits were installed. It reports that 390 people were reached. The operation spent CHF 7,002 of its CHF 117,555 budget. The final report of 30 June 2023 records a workshop on lessons learned. Its participants judged the trigger high. They recommended a review of the protocol.

data.retained_case_account: The Philippine Red Cross (PRC) approved its Early Action Protocol (EAP) for typhoons in December 2019. Its impact-based forecasting (IBF) model, developed with 510 (Netherlands Red Cross), applies machine learning (ML) to predict housing damage per municipality from typhoon forecasts. As Tropical Storm Paeng (Nalgae) approached on 27 October 2022, the 510/IBF forecast projected up to 10 percent shelter damage in priority municipalities. That hit the trigger at 56 hours' lead time. fields.account: The Philippine Red Cross approved its Early Action Protocol for typhoons in December 2019. Its model forecasts by impact. The Philippine Red Cross developed it with 510, an initiative of the Netherlands Red Cross. It applies machine learning to predict damage to housing in each municipality from typhoon forecasts. In 2021 the 510 model became the trigger model for the anticipatory action pilot of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) in the Philippines. The Central Emergency Response Fund funded the OCHA pilot with $7.5 million for the 2023 typhoon season. Under the protocol, early actions start when the forecast shows at least 10 percent of houses totally damaged in more than three municipalities 72 hours before landfall. As Tropical Storm Paeng (Nalgae) approached on 27 October 2022, the 510 forecast projected up to 10 percent shelter damage in priority municipalities. That met the trigger at 56 hours' lead time. According to the final report, the 56-hour lead time was granted as an exception. With anticipatory funds from the Disaster Response Emergency Fund of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, the Philippine Red Cross activated the protocol in Aurora Province. From 27 to 29 October, 40 workers distributed kits for strengthening shelters to 78 of 100 planned households in Dipaculao before landfall. They installed them. According to the same report, strong winds limited the distribution to 78 households. The onset of rain limited it. In its survey after the storm, the Philippine Red Cross reports that all 78 kits were installed. It reports that 390 people were reached. The operation spent CHF 7,002 of its CHF 117,555 budget. The final report of 30 June 2023 records a workshop on lessons learned. Its participants judged the trigger high. They recommended a review of the protocol.

record.title: With ALICE, the CGU cuts R$2.38 million from a glove tender of Hospital Federal de Ipanema in 2021. It cuts R$5.95 million from an undated glove tender of INCA
record.summary: With its ALICE tool, the CGU cut R$2.38m from a glove tender of the Ipanema hospital in 2021. It cut R$5.95m from one at Brazil's National Cancer Institute. It reports that it avoided R$8.33m.
record.account: Pregão 15/2021 of the Hospital Federal de Ipanema, a glove tender estimated at R$34 million, reused the price survey of Pregão 05/2021. On the recommendation of the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU), it was suspended. It was then re-estimated, which cut R$2,381,663.00. The auction held on 21 July 2021 bought every item at or below the new estimates, for a total of R$14,315,793.42. In March 2023 Fernanda Odilla of the University of Bologna reported in an independent study that Alice has helped auditors stop irregular tenders across Brazil. Its accuracy fell from 88.27% in testing to 73.91% in later auditing. She did not examine these tenders. In a statement of 4 October 2023, the CGU describes five preventive audits of tenders by federal hospitals and institutes in Rio de Janeiro, among them the Ipanema tender. The automated tool ALICE supported them. The CGU says that this prevented at least R$8.33 million of overpriced purchases. At the Instituto Nacional de Câncer (INCA), a glove auction estimated at R$11 million was re-estimated at R$5.1 million after ALICE indicated prices above market. That avoided about R$5.95 million. The CGU gives no date for the INCA auction. It gives no tender number.

data.retained_case_account: A CGU statement of 4 October 2023 describes five preventive audits of tenders by federal hospitals and institutes in Rio de Janeiro. The automated tool ALICE supported them. The CGU says this prevented at least R$8.33 million of overpriced purchases. At the Instituto Nacional de Câncer (INCA), a glove auction estimated at R$11 million was re-estimated at R$5.1 million after ALICE indicated prices above market. That avoided about R$5.95 million. At the Hospital Federal de Ipanema, Pregão 15/2021 for gloves (estimated R$34 million) had reused the price survey of Pregão 05/2021. On CGU's recommendation it was suspended and re-estimated, cutting R$2,381,663.00. The auction held on 21 July 2021 bought every item at or below the new estimates, totaling R$14,315,793.42.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The CGU states the audits were done “com apoio da ferramenta automatizada ALICE”. At INCA, it says, the overpricing risk was identified “com a ajuda do ALICE”. For the Ipanema tender, suspension followed a CGU recommendation after analysis of the price survey. ALICE's documented role is alerting and supporting the audit; auditors and managers decided. Developer and deployer are the same public body. The CGU page is on record as an archived copy, because the live page was restricted during Brazil's 2026 electoral period.

fields.summary: With its ALICE tool, the CGU cut R$2.38m from a glove tender of the Ipanema hospital in 2021. It cut R$5.95m from one at Brazil's National Cancer Institute. It reports that it avoided R$8.33m.
fields.account: Pregão 15/2021 of the Hospital Federal de Ipanema, a glove tender estimated at R$34 million, reused the price survey of Pregão 05/2021. On the recommendation of the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU), it was suspended. It was then re-estimated, which cut R$2,381,663.00. The auction held on 21 July 2021 bought every item at or below the new estimates, for a total of R$14,315,793.42. In March 2023 Fernanda Odilla of the University of Bologna reported in an independent study that Alice has helped auditors stop irregular tenders across Brazil. Its accuracy fell from 88.27% in testing to 73.91% in later auditing. She did not examine these tenders. In a statement of 4 October 2023, the CGU describes five preventive audits of tenders by federal hospitals and institutes in Rio de Janeiro, among them the Ipanema tender. The automated tool ALICE supported them. The CGU says that this prevented at least R$8.33 million of overpriced purchases. At the Instituto Nacional de Câncer (INCA), a glove auction estimated at R$11 million was re-estimated at R$5.1 million after ALICE indicated prices above market. That avoided about R$5.95 million. The CGU gives no date for the INCA auction. It gives no tender number.

record.title: Warning signs triggered by AI software that detects wildlife in thermal camera feeds slow drivers by an average of 3 mph on an elk corridor near Grundy, Virginia
record.summary: In a Virginia pilot, Crosstek software detected wildlife in thermal camera feeds with 97 percent accuracy. Drivers slowed by an average of 3 mph at the warning signs that it activated.
record.account: In September 2023 the Virginia Transportation Research Council reported on wildlife crossings for Corridor Q. It estimated the societal cost of an elk crash, including monetized pain and suffering, at $80,771.49 in 2020 dollars. The Virginia Department of Transportation (VDOT) later sponsored a one-year pilot by the Virginia Tech Transportation Institute (VTTI). It ran on Route 460 near Grundy in Southwest Virginia, as part of the Corridor Q expansion. VDOT names the pilot the Animal Detection and Driver Warning System. On its project page, it identifies VTTI as the research partner. VDOT gave the study an estimated start of February 2025, with completion estimated for September 2026. Eight portable solar-powered trailers with thermal cameras were installed on a 750-meter section of a 14-mile corridor that is home to about 100 elk. AI software from Crosstek analyzed the camera feeds. When the software detected wildlife, dynamic message signs showed motorists a warning that wildlife had been detected ahead, with an instruction to slow down. T-Mobile provided 5G links along with satellite links. WCYB reported the test on 19 November 2025. In its separate interview, Michelle Earl of VDOT described how animals are detected. She described how the system communicates with the message boards. The pilot ended in September 2026. Gwen Sheldon reported the results for Virginia Tech on 20 October 2026. The system identified wildlife of at least medium size with 97 percent accuracy across all detections. In the initial analysis the researchers found an average speed reduction of 3 mph as vehicles approached activated signs. Virginia Tech reports that the team collected data on more than 10,000 passing vehicles. It reports that data analysis was continuing after the pilot ended. Virginia Tech reports no result on collisions prevented. It reports no result on fatalities prevented. According to Virginia Tech, Crosstek supplied the cameras with their AI software. The measured results come from Virginia Tech's own report. WCYB covered only the deployment in its earlier interview.
record.purpose: Virginia's transportation department and Virginia Tech built the system to detect large wildlife near the road and warn approaching drivers in real time. The aim is fewer collisions between vehicles and wildlife.

fields.account: In September 2023 the Virginia Transportation Research Council reported on wildlife crossings for Corridor Q. It estimated the societal cost of an elk crash, including monetized pain and suffering, at $80,771.49 in 2020 dollars. The Virginia Department of Transportation (VDOT) later sponsored a one-year pilot by the Virginia Tech Transportation Institute (VTTI). It ran on Route 460 near Grundy in Southwest Virginia, as part of the Corridor Q expansion. VDOT names the pilot the Animal Detection and Driver Warning System. On its project page, it identifies VTTI as the research partner. VDOT gave the study an estimated start of February 2025, with completion estimated for September 2026. Eight portable solar-powered trailers with thermal cameras were installed on a 750-meter section of a 14-mile corridor that is home to about 100 elk. AI software from Crosstek analyzed the camera feeds. When the software detected wildlife, dynamic message signs showed motorists a warning that wildlife had been detected ahead, with an instruction to slow down. T-Mobile provided 5G links along with satellite links. WCYB reported the test on 19 November 2025. In its separate interview, Michelle Earl of VDOT described how animals are detected. She described how the system communicates with the message boards. The pilot ended in September 2026. Gwen Sheldon reported the results for Virginia Tech on 20 October 2026. The system identified wildlife of at least medium size with 97 percent accuracy across all detections. In the initial analysis the researchers found an average speed reduction of 3 mph as vehicles approached activated signs. record.account: Southern Water runs around 34,000 sewer level monitors with machine learning. Its proactive operations control manager Daniel McElhinney says that the system learns the normal behavior of sewers. He says that it can tell a forming blockage from daily rushes. He says that it can tell one from rain. Shortly before 22 April 2026 the sensors detected an abnormal flow in Rowner, Gosport. They alerted the control room. A crew cleared the sewer with a jet. They found a fatberg of wet wipes and other unflushable items. The company said that, left unchecked, the sewer could have overflowed from a manhole into a surface water drain leading to the River Alver. The blockage was reported on 22 April 2026. A second blockage that the sensors found, at Warlands Lane, Shalfleet, Isle of Wight, was reported on 23 April. BBC Future reported on 12 May 2026 that the sensors use radar to measure sewer levels. It reported that a model compares them with rainfall and weather data. The BBC reported that Southern Water had cleared 700 blockages with AI so far that year. It noted that the company still had more than 15,500 sewage spills in 2025, a drop of 47 percent from 2024. The BBC did not mention the blockage at Rowner. In October 2026 the same sensor network flagged a blockage of wet wipes before it overflowed into the Lymington River in the New Forest, by the company's account.

fields.summary: Southern Water's machine-learning sewer monitors flagged a forming fatberg in Rowner, Gosport. A crew cleared it before any overflow into the River Alver.
fields.account: Southern Water runs around 34,000 sewer level monitors with machine learning. Its proactive operations control manager Daniel McElhinney says that the system learns the normal behavior of sewers. He says that it can tell a forming blockage from daily rushes. He says that it can tell one from rain. Shortly before 22 April 2026 the sensors detected an abnormal flow in Rowner, Gosport. They alerted the control room. A crew cleared the sewer with a jet. They found a fatberg of wet wipes and other unflushable items. The company said that, left unchecked, the sewer could have overflowed from a manhole into a surface water drain leading to the River Alver. The blockage was reported on 22 April 2026. A second blockage that the sensors found, at Warlands Lane, Shalfleet, Isle of Wight, was reported on 23 April. BBC Future reported on 12 May 2026 that the sensors use radar to measure sewer levels. It reported that a model compares them with rainfall and weather data. The BBC reported that Southern Water had cleared 700 blockages with AI so far that year. It noted that the company still had more than 15,500 sewage spills in 2025, a drop of 47 percent from 2024. The BBC did not mention the blockage at Rowner. In October 2026 the same sensor network flagged a blockage of wet wipes before it overflowed into the Lymington River in the New Forest, by the company's account.

record.title: Taoyuan's AI sound cameras locate a white BMW that had been roaring down Jieshou Road at night, within a day of residents' complaint
record.summary: Mobile AI sound cameras of Taoyuan's environmental department located a loud white BMW within a day of a complaint from residents. Officers stopped it on 23 April 2025.
record.account: Residents of Bade District, Taoyuan, complained in the Facebook group 記憶八德. A white BMW with a loud exhaust kept roaring down Jieshou Road late at night. The Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection received the complaint on the night of 22 April 2025. Its Quiet Taoyuan (靜桃) task force immediately set up sound cameras that use AI at the relevant spots. By analyzing the noise data against the complaints, it worked out where the car appeared. It worked out when. On 23 April environmental and police officers stopped it near Daxing Road. The car was referred to the motor vehicle office for a modification review. The bureau said that a fine of up to NT$3,600 under the Noise Control Act would follow. It said that an order to fix the car would follow. All five cited reports reproduce statements from the Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection. None adds reporting of its own. In January 2026 the bureau said that noise complaints had fallen 38 percent since the Quiet Taoyuan project began. The bureau reported that 50 sets of sound cameras were installed across the city.
record.purpose: The Taoyuan environmental bureau places mobile AI sound cameras on main roads and residential streets to collect data on noise. Its staff combine the data with complaints to find when and where illegally modified, noisy vehicles appear.

fields.account: Residents of Bade District, Taoyuan, complained in the Facebook group 記憶八德. A white BMW with a loud exhaust kept roaring down Jieshou Road late at night. The Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection received the complaint on the night of 22 April 2025. Its Quiet Taoyuan (靜桃) task force immediately set up sound cameras that use AI at the relevant spots. By analyzing the noise data against the complaints, it worked out where the car appeared. It worked out when. On 23 April environmental and police officers stopped it near Daxing Road. The car was referred to the motor vehicle office for a modification review. The bureau said that a fine of up to NT$3,600 under the Noise Control Act would follow. It said that an order to fix the car would follow. All five cited reports reproduce statements from the Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection. None adds reporting of its own. In January 2026 the bureau said that noise complaints had fallen 38 percent since the Quiet Taoyuan project began. The bureau reported that 50 sets of sound cameras were installed across the city.

value.text: The car was located and stopped within 24 hours of the complaint, and the sources leave open whether its noise stopped afterward. In January 2026 the bureau reported 50 sound-camera sets installed citywide and noise complaints down 38 percent since the Quiet Taoyuan project began.

record.title: WINGS says, quoting the mayor, that wi.breathe cameras alert authorities to a Troizina wildfire
record.summary: WINGS says that the AI fire detector on its wi.breathe cameras alerted authorities to a wildfire at Troizina on 28 August 2025. The municipality did not mention them in its statement that day.
record.account: ERT, Greece's public broadcaster, reported on 28 August 2025 that 45 firefighters, 13 vehicles, two planes and four helicopters had been sent to the fire at Diavologefyro near Troizina. It reported that footage showed the fire close to houses. Saronic Magazine quoted the municipality, which said that the fire was put out quickly, before it grew out of control. In its statement that evening, the municipality credits a coordinated response. More than 80 firefighters took part, with six aircraft. The municipality thanks the fire service, the police and volunteers. It credits cooperation among agencies. It does not mention the cameras. Reporters and the municipality set out how large the fire was. They give the scale of the response. None of them verifies the AI's contribution. WINGS reported on 2 September 2025 that its wi.breathe cameras in Methana had detected the wildfire in Troizina on 28 August. It reported that the cameras had alerted authorities. The company quoted Mayor Tasos Ath. Mougios crediting the system with preventing a larger disaster. The mayor's credit to wi.breathe appears only in this WINGS release. That account comes with no alert log, no detection time, no chronology of the response and no estimate of avoided damage. WINGS later announced completion of the wider camera installation on 12 May 2026. Detection within one minute is claimed in publicity for the completed installation. That figure concerns the system's capability. WINGS gives no measurement of it for the August fire.
record.purpose: Its Athens developer built wi.breathe to detect wildfire smoke and fire on monitoring cameras and alert civil-protection authorities, so that they can respond earlier.
record.system: wi.breathe Operational Intelligence Platform (WINGS ICT Solutions): hybrid optical-thermal cameras, a WINGS-trained AI smoke and fire detection model, cloud infrastructure and 5G/4G links with dashboard, email and SMS alerts
record.deployer: Municipality of Troizinia-Methana (cameras at Vigla on Poros, Tsepeleni Aderon and Agios Georgios Methanon)
record.segment: Camera-based AI smoke and fire detection

ratings.reason: The developer and the mayor credit the system with an early warning and with keeping the fire from growing. No alert log, causal comparison or estimate of avoided damage has been published.

fields.account: ERT, Greece's public broadcaster, reported on 28 August 2025 that 45 firefighters, 13 vehicles, two planes and four helicopters had been sent to the fire at Diavologefyro near Troizina. It reported that footage showed the fire close to houses. Saronic Magazine quoted the municipality, which said that the fire was put out quickly, before it grew out of control. In its statement that evening, the municipality credits a coordinated response. More than 80 firefighters took part, with six aircraft. The municipality thanks the fire service, the police and volunteers. It credits cooperation among agencies. It does not mention the cameras. Reporters and the municipality set out how large the fire was. They give the scale of the response. None of them verifies the AI's contribution. WINGS reported on 2 September 2025 that its wi.breathe cameras in Methana had detected the wildfire in Troizina on 28 August. It reported that the cameras had alerted authorities. The company quoted Mayor Tasos Ath. Mougios crediting the system with preventing a larger disaster. The mayor's credit to wi.breathe appears only in this WINGS release. That account comes with no alert log, no detection time, no chronology of the response and no estimate of avoided damage. WINGS later announced completion of the wider camera installation on 12 May 2026. Detection within one minute is claimed in publicity for the completed installation. That figure concerns the system's capability. WINGS gives no measurement of it for the August fire.

fields.summary: WINGS says that the AI fire detector on its wi.breathe cameras alerted authorities to a wildfire at Troizina on 28 August 2025. The municipality did not mention them in its statement that day.
fields.account: ERT, Greece's public broadcaster, reported on 28 August 2025 that 45 firefighters, 13 vehicles, two planes and four helicopters had been sent to the fire at Diavologefyro near Troizina. It reported that footage showed the fire close to houses. Saronic Magazine quoted the municipality, which said that the fire was put out quickly, before it grew out of control. In its statement that evening, the municipality credits a coordinated response. More than 80 firefighters took part, with six aircraft. The municipality thanks the fire service, the police and volunteers. It credits cooperation among agencies. It does not mention the cameras. Reporters and the municipality set out how large the fire was. They give the scale of the response. None of them verifies the AI's contribution. WINGS reported on 2 September 2025 that its wi.breathe cameras in Methana had detected the wildfire in Troizina on 28 August. It reported that the cameras had alerted authorities. The company quoted Mayor Tasos Ath. Mougios crediting the system with preventing a larger disaster. The mayor's credit to wi.breathe appears only in this WINGS release. That account comes with no alert log, no detection time, no chronology of the response and no estimate of avoided damage. WINGS later announced completion of the wider camera installation on 12 May 2026. Detection within one minute is claimed in publicity for the completed installation. That figure concerns the system's capability. WINGS gives no measurement of it for the August fire.

record.title: An automated classifier on a glider detects right whale calls, which prompt a voluntary NOAA Slow Zone east of Portland, Maine
record.summary: The Low-Frequency Detection and Classification System on a glider detected right whales east of Portland, Maine, on 27 December 2023. NOAA declared a voluntary Slow Zone.
record.account: On 19 October 2023 Oceana, a group that campaigns for the ocean, reported an analysis of data on the movements of vessels from November 2020 to July 2022. In it, 82% of boats ignored the voluntary 10-knot limit in Slow Zones. On 27 December 2023 the Gulf of Maine Winter Slocum glider acoustically detected North Atlantic right whales east of Portland, Maine. Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution and NOAA's Northeast Fisheries Science Center operate the glider. Such gliders carry a DMON instrument running the Low-Frequency Detection and Classification System (LFDCS). The system compares the pitch of calls with a library of calls, using quadratic discriminant function analysis. Shore-based analysts validate detections. On 29 December 2023 NOAA Fisheries announced a voluntary Right Whale Slow Zone. Its bounds were 43°49'N, 43°09'N, 67°02'W and 68°57'W. It ran from 27 December 2023 through 11 January 2024. NOAA asked mariners to route around the area or transit at 10 knots or less. NOAA Fisheries has not reported how vessels behaved inside this Slow Zone. On 20 January 2024 a glider made the first definite glider-based acoustic detection in southeast United States waters. In 2025 Indeck and colleagues, among them the system's developer, reported on the program's first four years. In that time, acoustic detections led to 154 Slow Zones. Some zones were new. Others were extensions. Gliders accounted for 51 of them.
record.purpose: Mark Baumgartner built the Low-Frequency Detection and Classification System to detect and classify the calls of baleen whales almost in real time, for use by managers. Triggering a Slow Zone is the use that it was built for.

Oceana is an advocacy group for the oceans with no role in the glider or the Slow Zone program. Its analysis of tracking data for boats of 65 feet or more shows that most did not slow down in voluntary Slow Zones from November 2020 to July 2022. This result limits any protective effect of the zone in this benefit.

comparator.quote: Gliders triggered more slowdowns than aerial surveillance by a factor of two to five during fall and summer but were less effective during spring, as whales migrating into the GoSL tend to call at lower rates and occur at lower densities than during other behavioral states (Parks et al., 2011; Matthews and Parks, 2021).

later.quote: In the four years since its inception, 154 Slow Zones have been triggered or extended by acoustic detections of NARWs, and 51 (33%) of those Slow Zones were triggered or extended by gliders operated by the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Rutgers University, Stony Brook University, and The University of Maine during 57 separate glider missions.

learns_from_data.note: LFDCS classifies calls with quadratic discriminant analysis fitted to libraries of labeled example calls, a statistical classifier rather than deep learning.
learns_from_data.quote: Attributes of the pitch track (e.g., start frequency, end frequency, duration, slope of frequency variation) are extracted and compared to the attributes of known call types using quadratic discriminant function analysis.

In it, 82% of boats ignored the voluntary 10-knot limit in Slow Zones. On 27 December 2023 the Gulf of Maine Winter Slocum glider acoustically detected North Atlantic right whales east of Portland, Maine. Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution and NOAA's Northeast Fisheries Science Center operate the glider. Such gliders carry a DMON instrument running the Low-Frequency Detection and Classification System (LFDCS). The system compares the pitch of calls with a library of calls, using quadratic discriminant function analysis. Shore-based analysts validate detections. On 29 December 2023 NOAA Fisheries announced a voluntary Right Whale Slow Zone. Its bounds were 43°49'N, 43°09'N, 67°02'W and 68°57'W. It ran from 27 December 2023 through 11 January 2024. NOAA asked mariners to route around the area or transit at 10 knots or less. NOAA Fisheries has not reported how vessels behaved inside this Slow Zone. On 20 January 2024 a glider made the first definite glider-based acoustic detection in southeast United States waters. In 2025 Indeck and colleagues, among them the system's developer, reported on the program's first four years. In that time, acoustic detections led to 154 Slow Zones. Some zones were new. Others were extensions. Gliders accounted for 51 of them.

record.title: Xuanwu Hospital implants Epilcure, a responsive neurostimulator, in a man with drug-resistant bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy on 9 March 2022, in a trial whose team later reports fewer seizures in the cohort
record.summary: Xuanwu Hospital implanted the Epilcure responsive neurostimulator in a man with epilepsy in March 2022. Its trial team reports a 61.1% mean seizure reduction in seven patients, with no result for him.
record.account: On 9 March 2022 a team at Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, implanted the Epilcure closed-loop responsive neurostimulation system. Hospital president Zhao Guoguang and neurosurgeon Shan Yongzhi led it. The patient, a man with drug-resistant bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy, was the first enrollee in a hospital-led registration clinical trial for China's National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). cnBeta and Kuai Keji reported the operation on 12 March 2022. Both cited the neurosurgery department's WeChat account. Both outlets describe an AI chip implanted in the skull, with intracranial electrodes monitoring electroencephalography (EEG) rhythms around the clock. They say that the device predicts an imminent seizure. They say that it then delivers an interfering rhythm to block seizure formation at the focus. They call bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy a relative contraindication for open surgery. The operation went smoothly. The stimulator's indicators worked normally during surgery. Post-operative reconstruction showed precise electrode placement. It showed clear EEG signals (cnBeta). The outlets gave no seizure outcome for this patient. They did not give his age. They reported no follow-up. In 2023 the Xuanwu Hospital team reported with two partner centers that 10 patients were enrolled in the first-in-human trial between March and November 2022. They reported that seven patients followed over three months had a mean seizure reduction of 61.1%, with no serious adverse events. The same group later reported on 19 patients at eight centers through June 2023. They found a median reduction of 58% at month 12. Four patients had seizure-free periods. In that paper, the authors identify the maker as Hangzhou Genlight MedTech. They describe five detection algorithms, configured by clinicians, that trigger stimulation when signal measures cross set thresholds. Nothing in it shows that a learned model predicted seizures. The authors give no outcome for the first patient in either paper. The 2022 news reports come from the hospital's WeChat post.

fields.account: On 9 March 2022 a team at Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, implanted the Epilcure closed-loop responsive neurostimulation system. Hospital president Zhao Guoguang and neurosurgeon Shan Yongzhi led it. The patient, a man with drug-resistant bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy, was the first enrollee in a hospital-led registration clinical trial for China's National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). cnBeta and Kuai Keji reported the operation on 12 March 2022. Both cited the neurosurgery department's WeChat account. Both outlets describe an AI chip implanted in the skull, with intracranial electrodes monitoring electroencephalography (EEG) rhythms around the clock. They say that the device predicts an imminent seizure. They say that it then delivers an interfering rhythm to block seizure formation at the focus. They call bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy a relative contraindication for open surgery. The operation went smoothly. The stimulator's indicators worked normally during surgery. Post-operative reconstruction showed precise electrode placement. It showed clear EEG signals (cnBeta). The outlets gave no seizure outcome for this patient. They did not give his age. They reported no follow-up. In 2023 the Xuanwu Hospital team reported with two partner centers that 10 patients were enrolled in the first-in-human trial between March and November 2022. They reported that seven patients followed over three months had a mean seizure reduction of 61.1%, with no serious adverse events. The same group later reported on 19 patients at eight centers through June 2023. They found a median reduction of 58% at month 12. Four patients had seizure-free periods. In that paper, the authors identify the maker as Hangzhou Genlight MedTech. They describe five detection algorithms, configured by clinicians, that trigger stimulation when signal measures cross set thresholds. Nothing in it shows that a learned model predicted seizures. The authors give no outcome for the first patient in either paper. The 2022 news reports come from the hospital's WeChat post.

fields.summary: Xuanwu Hospital implanted the Epilcure responsive neurostimulator in a man with epilepsy in March 2022. Its trial team reports a 61.1% mean seizure reduction in seven patients, with no result for him.
fields.account: On 9 March 2022 a team at Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, implanted the Epilcure closed-loop responsive neurostimulation system. Hospital president Zhao Guoguang and neurosurgeon Shan Yongzhi led it. The patient, a man with drug-resistant bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy, was the first enrollee in a hospital-led registration clinical trial for China's National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). cnBeta and Kuai Keji reported the operation on 12 March 2022. Both cited the neurosurgery department's WeChat account. Both outlets describe an AI chip implanted in the skull, with intracranial electrodes monitoring electroencephalography (EEG) rhythms around the clock. They say that the device predicts an imminent seizure. They say that it then delivers an interfering rhythm to block seizure formation at the focus. They call bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy a relative contraindication for open surgery. The operation went smoothly. The stimulator's indicators worked normally during surgery. Post-operative reconstruction showed precise electrode placement. It showed clear EEG signals (cnBeta). The outlets gave no seizure outcome for this patient. They did not give his age. They reported no follow-up. In 2023 the Xuanwu Hospital team reported with two partner centers that 10 patients were enrolled in the first-in-human trial between March and November 2022. They reported that seven patients followed over three months had a mean seizure reduction of 61.1%, with no serious adverse events. The same group later reported on 19 patients at eight centers through June 2023. They found a median reduction of 58% at month 12. Four patients had seizure-free periods. In that paper, the authors identify the maker as Hangzhou Genlight MedTech. They describe five detection algorithms, configured by clinicians, that trigger stimulation when signal measures cross set thresholds. Nothing in it shows that a learned model predicted seizures. The authors give no outcome for the first patient in either paper. The 2022 news reports come from the hospital's WeChat post.

value.text: The implant was intended to monitor intracranial EEG continuously and trigger stimulation automatically when configured detectors recognized abnormal activity. The later clinical protocol sets out signal thresholds. It shows no learned model for predicting seizures.

produced_by: Intracranial electrodes at the epileptic focus feeding continuous EEG to a chip implanted in the skull
Clinician-configured EEG detection algorithms that trigger stimulation when signal measures cross set thresholds, as described in the later clinical paper
Enrollment in the hospital-led NMPA registration trial for patients whose epilepsy is drug-resistant and unsuited to open surgery
must_hold: Electrode placement is precise and signals are clear, as the post-operative reconstruction reported here
